readings.vyakhya_en: Number lives on the verb too. नरौ are two, so the verb takes the द्विवचन ending: of the प्रथम triad तिप्-तस्-झि (1.4.101/102), the middle one तस् gives गच्छतः. Side by side: गच्छति (one goes), गच्छतः (two go) — same root, tense, person; only वचन shifts.

readings.sentence: यदि सः अगमिष्यत् तर्हि सुखम् अलप्स्यत।
readings.translation: Had he gone, he would have obtained happiness.
readings.teaches: लृङ् — the conditional, for an act that never came about (क्रियातिपत्ति)

notes.role: लिङ्निमित्ते लृङ् क्रियातिपत्तौ — when the act fails to happen, लृङ् → अगमिष्यत्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → सुखम्
लिङ्निमित्ते लृङ् क्रियातिपत्तौ → अलप्स्यत

readings.vyakhya: क्रियायाः अनिष्पत्तौ लृङ्। यदि अगमिष्यत् — न तु अगच्छत्। फलमपि न लब्धम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The लृङ् conditional is for what would-have-been but was NOT — क्रियातिपत्ति, the act's non-occurrence (3.3.139). It looks like the future-stem (गमिष्य-, लप्स्य-) with the augment अ and the लङ् imperfect endings: अगमिष्यत्, अलप्स्यत. यदि सः अगमिष्यत् "had he gone" — implying he did not. This completes the ten लकारs: present, three pasts, two futures, three moods, and now the conditional.

readings.translation: The village is gone-to by Rāma. (Rāma goes to the village.)
readings.teaches: कर्मणि प्रयोग — the passive: the object becomes the nominative subject; agent → instrumental; यक् + आत्मनेपद

notes.en: the agent, now in the instrumental (not nominative)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → कर्तृ in the passive → रामेण

words.gloss: the village — now the grammatical subject

notes.en: the logical object, raised to nominative subject in the passive

notes.role: प्रातिपदिकार्थ…प्रथमा → the कर्म, when verb-denoted, takes प्रथमा → ग्रामः

quiz.q: Which form is ग्राम · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the passive विकरण — root + य, with आत्मनेपद endings

notes.role: सार्वधातुके यक् — the passive विकरण यक् (य) → गम्यते
लः कर्मणि च — the ल-affix denotes the कर्म (passive) → ātmanepada ending
भावकर्मणोः — passive/impersonal take आत्मनेपद → गम्यते

readings.vyakhya: कर्मणि यक्, आत्मनेपदं च। रामः गच्छति → रामेण ग्रामः गम्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en: The passive (कर्मणि प्रयोग) re-stages the same act: the OBJECT becomes the nominative subject (ग्रामः), the AGENT drops to the instrumental (रामेण), and the verb takes the passive marker यक् (य, 3.1.67) with ātmanepada endings (1.3.13) — गम्यते "is gone-to." Active रामः ग्रामं गच्छति = passive रामेण ग्रामः गम्यते. The ल-affix now points to the कर्म, not the कर्तृ (3.4.69).

readings.translation: It is slept by Devadatta. (Devadatta sleeps.)
readings.teaches: भावे प्रयोग — the impersonal passive of an intransitive verb: no subject, agent in the instrumental

notes.en: the agent, in the instrumental (no nominative exists)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → कर्तृ in भाव/passive → देवदत्तेन

notes.en: the passive विकरण — root + य, with आत्मनेपद endings

notes.role: …भावे चाकर्मकेभ्यः — for intransitive roots the ल-affix denotes भाव (the bare act)
भावकर्मणोः → आत्मनेपद → सुप्यते (3sg, no agreement with any noun)

readings.vyakhya: अकर्मकात् भावे प्रयोगः। कर्तृ तृतीयायाम्, क्रिया एव प्रधाना। देवदत्तेन सुप्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en: An intransitive verb has no object to promote, so its passive is IMPERSONAL — भावे प्रयोग, "the bare act" (3.4.69 …भावे चाकर्मकेभ्यः). There is no subject at all: the verb stands in a fixed 3rd-singular (सुप्यते), and the agent is instrumental (देवदत्तेन). Literally "it-is-slept by Devadatta" = "Devadatta sleeps." Sanskrit's way of foregrounding the action over the doer.

readings.translation: He did (it). / He made (it).
readings.teaches: लुङ् — the aorist, the simple/unmarked past (no restriction to a time-frame)

notes.role: लुङ् — past action without a time restriction → the aorist → अकार्षीत्

readings.vyakhya: सामान्ये भूते लुङ्। अकार्षीत् — न अद्यतनानद्यतनविशेषः। कृ-धातोः सिजन्तम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The लुङ् aorist is the UNMARKED past: plain "did," with none of the today/before-today restrictions that लङ् (अकरोत्, imperfect) and लिट् (चकार, perfect) carry — 3.2.110 simply says लुङ् for past action. √कृ → अकार्षीत् "he did," with the augment अ and the सिच् marker. So √कृ now spans all four pasts-and-presents: करोति · अकरोत् · चकार · अकार्षीत्, plus the future करिष्यति. The full time-axis of one root.

readings.translation: The boy cooks; the rice is cooked.
readings.teaches: कर्तरि शप् vs कर्मणि यक् — the विकरण (stem-marker) shows the voice: active शप् (अ) vs passive यक् (य)

quiz.q: Which form is बाल · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.role: कर्तरि शप् — in the active, the विकरण शप् (अ) → पच् + अ + ति → पचति

words.gloss: the rice — subject of the passive clause

notes.en: the object, raised to nominative in the passive

notes.role: सार्वधातुके यक् — in the passive, the विकरण यक् (य) → पच् + य + ते → पच्यते

readings.vyakhya: कर्तरि शप्, कर्मणि यक्। पच् + अ → पचति; पच् + य → पच्यते। विकरणः प्रयोगं सूचयति।
readings.vyakhya_en: What tells active from passive is the विकरण — the little stem-marker between root and ending. Active uses शप्, अ (3.1.68 कर्तरि शप्): पच् + अ + ति → पचति "cooks." Passive uses यक्, य (3.1.67 सार्वधातुके यक्): पच् + य + ते → पच्यते "is cooked." Same root पच्, same tense; the विकरण अ vs य, and the ending परस्मै- vs आत्मनेपद, carry the whole voice contrast.

readings.sentence: भवामि भवावः भवामः। भवसि भवथः भवथ। भवति भवतः भवन्ति।
readings.translation: Present tense of भू "be", all nine cells: I/we-two/we am/are; you/you-two/you-all are; he/those-two/they are.
readings.teaches: the whole present-tense paradigm — three पुरुष across three वचन

notes.role: तिप्तस्झि… — the ending series; 1sg मिप् → भवामि
तिप्तस्झि… → 3sg तिप् → भवति
बहुषु बहुवचनम् → plural → भवन्ति

readings.vyakhya: लटि परस्मैपदस्य नव तिङः — त्रयः पुरुषाः त्रीणि वचनानि च। भू + शप् + तिङ् = भवति इत्यादि।
readings.vyakhya_en: You met the तिङ् frame one cell at a time (ex014–016, ex092). Here is the WHOLE present-tense paradigm of भू "be" in one place — the verbal counterpart to the देव declension table (ex094). Read across each row for a person (उत्तम / मध्यम / प्रथम), down each column for a number (sg · dual · pl). The nine endings come from one master sūtra, तिप्तस्झि… (3.4.78); the stem is भू + शप् (अ) → भव-. Learn these nine and every parasmaipada present (गच्छति, पठति, वदति) falls into place.

chapters.title: सन्धि — the sound-changes at word and morpheme joins

readings.translation: "curds, Indra" → दधीन्द्रः (curds-Indra)
readings.teaches: सवर्णदीर्घ — two like (सवर्ण) vowels merge into one long vowel

notes.text: दधि + इन्द्रः: इ meets इ

notes.en: homogeneous — vowels of the same place of articulation

notes.role: अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः — a simple vowel before a like vowel; the two become one long vowel

notes.text: → ई → दधीन्द्रः

readings.vyakhya: समाने सवर्णे अकः दीर्घ एकादेशः। इ + इ = ई।
readings.vyakhya_en: When a simple vowel (अक्) meets a homogeneous vowel — इ with इ, उ with उ, अ with अ — the pair fuses into the single long vowel of that class. दधि + इन्द्रः gives दधीन्द्रः: two इ become one ई.

readings.translation: "not here" → नेह
readings.teaches: गुण — अ/आ before इ/उ/ऋ yields the गुण vowel (ए, ओ, अर्)

notes.text: न + इह: अ meets इ

notes.role: आद्गुणः — when अ/आ is followed by another vowel, the two become the single गुण vowel

notes.text: अ + इ → ए → नेह

readings.vyakhya: अवर्णात् अचि गुण एकादेशः। अ + इ = ए।
readings.vyakhya_en: An अ or आ followed by इ, उ, or ऋ does not merge to a long vowel but shifts to the गुण grade: अ + इ → ए, अ + उ → ओ, अ + ऋ → अर्. So न + इह → नेह. The same अ behaves differently depending on the vowel it meets.

readings.translation: "yours indeed" → तवैव
readings.teaches: वृद्धि — अ/आ before ए/ऐ/ओ/औ yields the वृद्धि vowel (ऐ, औ)

notes.text: तव + एव: अ meets ए

notes.role: वृद्धिरेचि — when अ/आ is followed by एच् (ए ऐ ओ औ), the two become the वृद्धि vowel

notes.text: अ + ए → ऐ → तवैव

readings.vyakhya: अवर्णात् एचि वृद्धिः एकादेशः। अ + ए = ऐ।
readings.vyakhya_en: When अ or आ meets one of the diphthong-grade vowels (ए, ऐ, ओ, औ), the result climbs to the वृद्धि grade: अ + ए → ऐ, अ + ओ → औ. So तव + एव → तवैव. गुण and वृद्धि are the two upward grades of इ and उ.

readings.translation: "the wise one is to be served" → सुध्युपास्यः
readings.teaches: यण् — इ/उ/ऋ before an unlike vowel become the glide य्/व्/र्

notes.text: सुधी + उपास्यः: ई meets उ (unlike)

notes.en: the glides य् व् र् ल्

notes.role: इको यणचि — an इक् vowel (इ उ ऋ ऌ) before any vowel becomes its corresponding यण् glide

notes.text: ई → य् → सुध्युपास्यः

readings.vyakhya: इकः अचि यण् आदेशः। ई + उ → य् + उ = यु।
readings.vyakhya_en: When इ, उ, or ऋ meets an unlike vowel, it does not merge but turns into its glide — य्, व्, र् — and the following vowel stands: सुधी + उपास्यः → सुध्युपास्यः. (Like meeting like gave the long vowel of ex023; unlike gives the glide here.)

readings.translation: Hari dwells among the sages.
readings.teaches: one sentence, both sibilant outcomes — हरिः takes visarga, ऋषिषु takes ष्

notes.en: nominative — the ending स् stands at a pause before a vowel

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — the स् of the ending → visarga → हरिः
आदेशप्रत्ययोः — the स् of सु → ष् after the इ → ऋषिषु

readings.vyakhya: एकस्मिन् वाक्ये द्वौ सकारौ द्वयोः गत्योः — हरिः इति विसर्जनीयः, ऋषिषु इति षत्वम्। उभयत्र इकारः पूर्वः, फलम् तु भिन्नम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Both words end their stem in इ and both have an ending in स्, and the two स् go different ways: हरिः becomes visarga, ऋषिषु becomes ष्. What separates them is where the स् stands — at the end of the word in हरिः, with nothing after it to give it a place, and inside the word in ऋषिषु, with a उ following. The इ before it is the same in both.

readings.translation: "again and again" — पुनर् at the pause shows as पुनः
readings.teaches: रु → visarga before a hard consonant and at the pause (खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः)

notes.text: the word ends in र्; before a vowel or soft sound it stays पुनर् — पुनर् अपि

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — र् → visarga before a खर् consonant and at the pause

notes.text: the second one stands at the pause, and takes the visarga for that reason alone

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — अवसान, the pause, is the other trigger

readings.vyakhya: खरि अवसाने च रोः विसर्जनीयः। पुनर् → पुनः। स्वरे तु पुनर् अपि इति तिष्ठति।
readings.vyakhya_en: One rule, two triggers. The र् of पुनर् becomes visarga both before a hard consonant (पुनः कः) and at a pause, where nothing follows at all — पुनः पुनः shows the second case twice over. Before a vowel the र् survives: पुनर् अपि. So the visarga is not part of the word; it is what the word's final र् turns into when the surroundings give it nothing voiced to lean on.

readings.translation: "in the fires" → अग्निषु
readings.teaches: षत्व — the ending's स् becomes ष् after an इ (आदेशप्रत्ययोः)

notes.text: the ending is सु; its स् meets the इ of अग्नि

notes.role: आदेशप्रत्ययोः — a प्रत्यय's स् goes ष् after an इण् vowel → अग्निषु

quiz.q: Which form is अग्नि · सप्तमी · बहुवचन?

readings.vyakhya: प्रत्ययस्य सकारः इण्कुभ्याम् उत्तरः षकारः। अग्नि + सु = अग्निषु। न तु सर्वः सकारः — प्रत्ययस्य एव।
readings.vyakhya_en: The locative plural ending सु carries a स्, and after the इ of अग्नि that स् retroflexes to ष् — अग्निषु. The rule is narrow in a way worth noticing: it applies to the स् of an ending, not to every स् in the language. A स् that belongs to the stem itself is untouched by it, which is why the same इ does nothing to the स् of a following separate word.

readings.translation: "speech here" → वाग् अत्र
readings.teaches: जश्त्व — a word-final hard stop softens to its voiced counterpart

notes.en: the soft (voiced) stops ग् ज् ड् द् ब्

notes.role: झलां जशोऽन्ते — a stop at word's end becomes its जश् (voiced) counterpart; क् → ग्

notes.text: वाक् → वाग्

readings.vyakhya: पदान्ते झलां जश्। क् → ग्, यथा वाक् → वाग्।
readings.vyakhya_en: A hard stop standing at the end of a word softens to its voiced partner: क्→ग्, त्→द्, प्→ब्. So वाक् "speech" appears as वाग् before अत्र. The word's lemma is वाक्; its sentence-form follows the join.

readings.translation: "and that" → तच्च
readings.teaches: श्चुत्व — a dental meeting a palatal becomes palatal

notes.text: तत् + च: dental त् meets palatal च

notes.en: the palatal series श् च् छ् ज् झ् ञ्

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — a dental (त-class/स) next to a palatal (च-class/श) turns palatal; त् → च्

notes.text: त् → च् → तच्च

readings.vyakhya: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुत्वम्। त् + च → च् + च = च्च।
readings.vyakhya_en: A dental sound touching a palatal is pulled into the palatal series: तत् + च → तच्च. The त् becomes च् to match the following च. Assimilation — the first sound takes on the place of the second.

readings.translation: "the forest laughs" → वनं हसति
readings.teaches: a word-final म् becomes anusvāra (ं) before a consonant

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — a word-final म् before a consonant becomes anusvāra; म् → ं

notes.text: वनम् → वनं (before हसति)

readings.vyakhya: पदान्ते मकारस्य हलि अनुस्वारः। वनम् → वनं हसति।
readings.vyakhya_en: A म् at the end of a word, when a consonant follows, contracts to the anusvāra ं: वनम् हसति → वनं हसति. (Before a vowel, or at a true pause, the म् stays — so it is the following consonant that triggers the change.)

readings.translation: "by Rāma": रामेन → रामेण (न becomes ण after र)
readings.teaches: णत्व — न् becomes ण् after र्/ष् in the same word

notes.text: राम + इन (instr.sg ending ट्→इन): the न् stands after the र् of राम

notes.role: अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि — णत्व applies across the intervening vowel → ण्
अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि → the change still applies across an intervening vowel/guttural/labial (here the ए) → रामेण

readings.vyakhya: रेफात् परः नकारः णकारः समानपदे, अट्-व्यवधानेऽपि। रामेन → रामेण।
readings.vyakhya_en: Within one word, a न् turns cerebral (ण्) when an र् or ष् precedes it (8.4.1) — even when a vowel, guttural, or labial stands between them (8.4.2). So राम + the instrumental -इन gives रामेण, not *रामेन*: the र् of राम reaches across the ए to retroflex the न्. This णत्व is why we say रामायण, ब्राह्मणः, नारायण.

readings.translation: "Rāma the sixth" → रामष्षष्ठः (स/त-series cerebralised by ष)
readings.teaches: ष्टुत्व — स् and the dentals turn cerebral (ष्/ट-series) next to ष् or a cerebral

notes.text: रामस् + षष्ठः: a dental स् meets the cerebral ष्

notes.en: cerebralisation — स्/तवर्ग → ष्/टवर्ग in contact with ष् or a cerebral

notes.role: ष्टुना ष्टुः → स् and the dentals next to ष्/टवर्ग become ष्/टवर्ग → रामष्षष्ठः

readings.vyakhya: षकारटवर्गसन्निधौ सकारतवर्गयोः ष्टुत्वम्। रामस् षष्ठः → रामष्षष्ठः।
readings.vyakhya_en: Mirror of श्चुत्व (which palatalised before श्/च-series): ष्टुत्व *cerebralises*. A dental स् or त-series sound, meeting a cerebral ष् or ट-series sound, itself becomes cerebral (8.4.41). रामस् + षष्ठः → रामष्षष्ठः; तत् + टीका → तट्टीका. The articulation simply assimilates to its neighbour's place — the same logic as जश्त्व and श्चुत्व, one row over.

readings.sentence: सम् कृतम् → संस्कृतम् (सङ्… → the nasal homorganic).
readings.translation: "well-made" सम्+कृत → the nasal matches the following stop
readings.teaches: अनुस्वार → परसवर्ण — anusvāra becomes the nasal of the following class

notes.text: सम् + कृत: final म् → anusvāra (8.3.23), then the anusvāra may take the class-nasal

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः → word-final म् before a consonant → anusvāra (संकृत)

notes.en: the nasal homogeneous with the following sound

notes.role: अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः → the anusvāra becomes the class-nasal of the following यय् consonant

readings.vyakhya: मकारः अनुस्वारः, सः ययि परसवर्णः। सम् + कृत → संकृत → सङ्… परसवर्णेन।
readings.vyakhya_en: A final म् before a consonant first becomes anusvāra (8.3.23, the rule that gave वनं); then that anusvāra may take the *homorganic* nasal — the nasal belonging to the following sound's class (8.4.58). सम् + कृतम् → संस्कृतम्; सम् + गतः → सङ्गतः (the guttural ङ् before ग). The nasal quietly tunes itself to whatever stop follows.

readings.translation: "homage to thee": the विसर्ग returns to स् before त
readings.teaches: विसर्ग → स् — a visarga becomes स् before a hard dental (खर्)

notes.text: नमः + ते: the visarga of नमः meets the त् of ते

notes.role: विसर्जनीयस्य सः → a visarga → स् before a खर् consonant → नमस्ते

notes.text: नमस् here is a गति/preverb-like form; 8.3.40 also fixes its स् → नमस्ते, नमस्कारः

readings.vyakhya: विसर्गस्य सकारः खरि। नमः + ते → नमस्ते। पुनः सकारः प्रत्येति।
readings.vyakhya_en: The visarga is not the end of the story — before a hard consonant (खर्) it can revert to स् (8.3.34): नमः + ते → नमस्ते, नमः + कारः → नमस्कारः. The final स् of नरः became visarga before pause (8.2.66 → 8.3.15); here the reverse environment pulls the visarga back to स्. Sandhi is contextual all the way down: the same sound shows different faces by what stands next.

readings.translation: He too goes.
readings.teaches: visarga → ओ before a voiced sound (अतो रोः → उ, then गुण ओ); the अवग्रह (ऽ) marks the elided अ

notes.text: विग्रह: सः + अपि; the अः before a voiced sound → ओ, and अ of अपि elides (ऽ)

notes.role: अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते — अः (from रु) becomes उ before a voiced sound → स उ
आद्गुणः — अ + उ → गुण ओ → सो; the following अ drops (पूर्वरूप), marked ऽ

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

readings.vyakhya: अतो रोः उत्वम्, ततः गुणः। सः + अपि = सोऽपि। लोपे अवग्रहः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The commonest visarga outcome: सः before a voiced sound. The अः (a visarga from रु, 8.2.66) becomes उ (6.1.113), then अ + उ fuse by गुण to ओ (6.1.87) → सो; the following short अ then drops, written with the अवग्रह ऽ. सः + अपि → सोऽपि "he too." This is why सः appears as सो only before voiced sounds — before a vowel other than अ, or a consonant, it shifts differently.

readings.translation: Salutation to you.
readings.teaches: visarga → स् before a त्-class stop (विसर्जनीयस्य सः)

notes.text: विग्रह: नमः + ते; the visarge before त् becomes स् (its homorganic sibilant)

notes.role: विसर्जनीयस्य सः — visarga → स् before a sibilant/dental-स् context → नमस्

readings.vyakhya: विसर्जनीयस्य सकारः सवर्णे। नमः + ते = नमस्ते।
readings.vyakhya_en: Before a dental, the visarga assimilates to स् (8.3.34, विसर्जनीयस्य सः). नमः + ते → नमस्ते "salutations to you" — the visarga of नमः becomes स् before the त् of ते. The same gives दुस्तर (दुः + तर), निस्तेज (निः + तेज): visarga takes the sibilant of the place that follows.

readings.translation: He covers over.
readings.teaches: छ-doubling (तुक्) — a short vowel before छ inserts त् → च्छ (छे च)

notes.text: विग्रह: आ + छादयति; before छ a त् (तुक्) is inserted → च्छ

notes.role: छे च — a short vowel (here the आ-preverb context) before छ takes the augment तुक् (त्) → च्छ

readings.vyakhya: छकारे परे तुक् (त्); त् + छ = च्छ। आ + छादयति = आच्छादयति।
readings.vyakhya_en: छ never stands alone after a vowel: छे च (6.1.73) inserts the augment तुक् (त्), and त् + छ surfaces as च्छ. आ + छादयति → आच्छादयति "covers over." The same doubling gives तच्छ्रुत्वा (तत् + छ्रुत्वा... via श्), शिवच्छाया (शिव + छाया "Śiva's shade"): a vowel + छ always becomes -च्छ-.

readings.translation: For this (is so).
readings.teaches: before ह, a stop voices and doubles it — here त् + ह gives द्ध

notes.text: विग्रह: एतत् + हि; final त् → द् (जश्त्व) before voiced ह, and ह → ध (झयो हः)

notes.role: झलां जशोऽन्ते — final त् voices to द् before a voiced sound
झयो होऽन्यतरस्याम् — ह after a झय् stop optionally becomes its voiced aspirate → ध

notes.en: "for, indeed" (the ह that triggers the change)

readings.vyakhya: अन्त्यस्य जश्त्वम् (त्→द्), झयः परस्य हस्य घोषवदादेशः (ह→ध)। एतत् + हि = एतद्धि।
readings.vyakhya_en: Two changes meet at त् + ह. First जश्त्व: the final त् voices to द् before the voiced ह (8.2.39). Then the ह, now after a voiced stop, optionally becomes that stop's voiced aspirate — झयो होऽन्यतरस्याम् (8.4.62) — so ह → ध and the cluster surfaces as द्ध: एतत् + हि → एतद्धि. The same gives तद्धित (तत् + हित), वाग्घरि (वाक् + हरि): a stop + ह coalesces into a doubled voiced aspirate.

readings.translation: He delights again.
readings.teaches: visarga → र् before a voiced sound — the other outcome, beside सोऽपि

notes.text: पुनः ends in रु; before a voiced sound the visarga surfaces as र् (not ओ)

notes.role: ससजुषो रुः — word-final स् → रु; its visarga becomes र् before a voiced sound
अतो रोः — applies to अ-final रु (सः→सो); पुनर् keeps र् because its base is पुनर्, not अतः

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

readings.vyakhya: रेफान्तस्य रुत्वम् घोषे। पुनः + रमते = पुनर् रमते। (अतो भिन्नत्वात् न ओत्वम्।)
readings.vyakhya_en: Not every visarga becomes ओ. Words whose underlying final is -र् (पुनर्, अन्तर्, प्रातर्) show र् before a voiced sound, NOT the अ + उ → ओ fusion of ex155. पुनः + रमते → पुनर् रमते "delights again." Contrast सोऽपि (सः, base स-अः → सो) with पुनर् (base पुनर्): the visarga's outcome depends on what stands under it — an अ that fuses to ओ, or an र् that simply reappears.

readings.sentence: रामः च लक्ष्मणः च → रामश्च लक्ष्मणश्च।
readings.translation: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.
readings.teaches: visarga → श् before a च्-class stop (श्चुत्व applied to the visarga-sibilant)

notes.text: विग्रह: रामः + च; visarga → स् (8.3.34), then स् → श् before च् (श्चुत्व)

notes.role: विसर्जनीयस्य सः — visarga → स् before the following stop
स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — स्/त् before a च्-class sound become श्/च् → रामश्च

notes.text: same change: लक्ष्मणः + च → लक्ष्मणश्च

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः → श् before च

readings.vyakhya: विसर्जनीयस्य सः, ततः श्चुत्वम्। रामः + च = रामश्च। द्वयोः योगे चकारः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The visarga before a च-class stop ends up as श्. First it becomes स् (8.3.34); then स् before च् is cerebralised — really palatalised — to श् by स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40). रामः च → रामश्च, लक्ष्मणः च → लक्ष्मणश्च, the standard "X and Y" linkage. The visarga's three sibilant outcomes — स् (before त्, ex156), श् (before च्, here), ष् (before ट्) — all follow the place of the stop that comes next.

chapters.title: समास — compounds: two words joined into one

readings.translation: the king's man (विग्रह: राज्ञः पुरुषः)
readings.teaches: तत्पुरुष — the second member is primary, and the first qualifies it

notes.text: विग्रह: राज्ञः पुरुषः — "the man of the king"

notes.role: प्राक् कडारात् समासः — from here the combinations are named समास

notes.en: determinative — the second member is the head

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — a compound whose second member carries the main sense is तत्पुरुष

readings.vyakhya: उत्तरपदार्थप्रधानः तत्पुरुषः। राजपुरुषः — पुरुषः प्रधानम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: In a तत्पुरुष the second member is the head and the first qualifies it: राजपुरुषः is a kind of पुरुष (man) — the king's. Resolve it (विग्रह) as राज्ञः पुरुषः, "the man of the king." The compound is whatever its last member is.

readings.translation: Rāma-and-Kṛṣṇa (विग्रह: रामः च कृष्णः च)
readings.teaches: द्वन्द्व — members are coordinate ("and"); none subordinate

notes.text: विग्रह: रामः च कृष्णः च

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः — words standing in the sense of "च" (and) form a द्वन्द्व

notes.en: dual — two people, so the compound is dual

readings.vyakhya: उभयपदार्थप्रधानः द्वन्द्वः। रामः च कृष्णः च = रामकृष्णौ।
readings.vyakhya_en: A द्वन्द्व joins members that would each stand with "and" — none is subordinate, both are heads: रामः च कृष्णः च collapses to रामकृष्णौ, "Rāma and Kṛṣṇa." Two people, so the compound itself is dual.

readings.translation: the yellow-clothed one [Viṣṇu] (विग्रह: पीतम् अम्बरम् यस्य सः)
readings.teaches: बहुव्रीहि — neither member is the head; the compound points outside itself

words.gloss: the one whose garment is yellow

notes.text: विग्रह: पीतम् अम्बरम् यस्य सः

notes.en: possessive / exocentric — denotes someone characterised by the members

notes.role: शेषो बहुव्रीहिः — the remaining kind of compound is बहुव्रीहि
अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — several words denoting ANOTHER thing (the possessor) form a बहुव्रीहि

readings.vyakhya: अन्यपदार्थप्रधानः बहुव्रीहिः। पीतम् अम्बरम् यस्य — सः विष्णुः।
readings.vyakhya_en: A बहुव्रीहि names neither member: पीताम्बरः is not "yellow" and not "garment" but the one who has a yellow garment — Viṣṇu. The sense lies OUTSIDE the compound (अन्यपदार्थ). Resolve with यस्य: "he whose (यस्य) garment is yellow."

readings.translation: near Kṛṣṇa (विग्रह: कृष्णस्य समीपम्)
readings.teaches: अव्ययीभाव — the first member, an indeclinable, is primary, and the whole behaves as one

notes.text: विग्रह: कृष्णस्य समीपम् — उप = "near"

notes.en: adverbial — the compound behaves as an indeclinable

notes.role: अव्ययीभावः — a compound headed by an indeclinable (here उप) is अव्ययीभाव

readings.vyakhya: पूर्वपदार्थप्रधानः अव्ययीभावः। उप कृष्णस्य समीपम् — सर्वम् अव्ययम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: In an अव्ययीभाव the first member — an indeclinable like उप ("near") — is primary, and the whole compound becomes an indeclinable itself: उपकृष्णम्, "near Kṛṣṇa," fixed in form. Four types, four answers to one question: which member carries the sense?

readings.translation: a great man (विग्रह: महान् पुरुषः)
readings.teaches: कर्मधारय — a तत्पुरुष whose members share one case (adjective + noun)

notes.text: विग्रह: महान् पुरुषः — "a man who is great"

notes.en: a तत्पुरुष of adjective + noun, both in the same case

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः समानाधिकरणः कर्मधारयः — a तत्पुरुष whose members are co-referential (same case) is कर्मधारय
विशेषणं विशेष्येण — a qualifier (महत्) combines with the qualified (पुरुष)

readings.vyakhya: समानाधिकरणः तत्पुरुषः कर्मधारयः। महान् च असौ पुरुषः च।
readings.vyakhya_en: A कर्मधारय is a तत्पुरुष where the two members refer to the SAME thing — adjective and noun, both nominative: महान् पुरुषः → महापुरुषः, "great man." Unlike राजपुरुषः (the king's man — two different things, genitive relation), here महत् simply describes पुरुष. (महत् → महा in the compound.)

readings.translation: the three worlds (विग्रह: त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः)
readings.teaches: द्विगु — a numeral-first तत्पुरुष, denoting an aggregate

notes.text: विग्रह: त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः — "the aggregate of three worlds"

notes.en: a numeral-first compound, naming a counted aggregate

notes.role: संख्यापूर्वो द्विगुः — a तत्पुरुष with a number (त्रि) as its first member is द्विगु

readings.vyakhya: संख्यापूर्वः तत्पुरुषः द्विगुः। त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः त्रिलोकी।
readings.vyakhya_en: A द्विगु is a तत्पुरुष whose first member is a numeral: त्रि (three) + लोक (world) → त्रिलोकी, "the three worlds" taken as one set. It names a counted aggregate — द्वि-गु itself means "worth two cows." Same तत्पुरुष frame (second member heads), special first member: a number.

readings.translation: The boy gone-to-Kṛṣṇa (who has taken refuge with Kṛṣṇa).
readings.teaches: द्वितीया-तत्पुरुष — the विग्रह uses the accusative (कृष्णं श्रितः); named by that case

words.gloss: gone to / having resorted to Kṛṣṇa

notes.text: विग्रह: कृष्णं श्रितः — "resorted-to Kṛष्ण"; the first member is logically accusative

notes.role: द्वितीया श्रितातीतपतित… — a 2nd-case word compounds with श्रित etc. → द्वितीया-तत्पुरुष

quiz.q: Which form is बाल · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

readings.vyakhya: द्वितीयान्तं श्रितादिभिः समस्यते। कृष्णं श्रितः = कृष्णश्रितः।
readings.vyakhya_en: तत्पुरुष compounds are NAMED by the case the analysis (विग्रह) would use. Here the विग्रह is कृष्णं श्रितः — "resorted-to Kṛṣṇa," with कृष्ण in the द्वितीया (accusative) — so the compound is a द्वितीया-तत्पुरुष (2.1.24). The later member श्रित heads it, as in every तत्पुरुष; only the internal case-relation differs. This is the template: each case gives a named sub-type.

readings.translation: Bring the wood for the sacrificial post.
readings.teaches: चतुर्थी-तत्पुरुष — the विग्रह uses a dative of purpose: यूपाय दारु, "wood for a post"

notes.text: विग्रह: यूपाय दारु — "wood for-a-post"; first member is logically dative (purpose)

notes.role: चतुर्थी तदर्थार्थ… — a 4th-case (purpose) word compounds → चतुर्थी-तत्पुरुष

notes.en: object of आनय (accusative neuter, unchanged in form)

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → आनय

readings.vyakhya: चतुर्थ्यन्तं तदर्थेन समस्यते। यूपाय दारु = यूपदारु।
readings.vyakhya_en: The dative-of-purpose तत्पुरुष: यूपाय दारु, "wood FOR a sacrificial post," compounds to यूपदारु (2.1.36). The विग्रह's चतुर्थी (purpose, "for") names it. Compare कृष्णश्रितः (द्वितीया, ex143): same heads-later frame, the internal case is what the name records.

readings.translation: The king's man comes.
readings.teaches: षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष — the commonest तत्पुरुष; the विग्रह uses the genitive (राज्ञः पुरुषः)

notes.text: विग्रह: राज्ञः पुरुषः — "the king's man"; first member is logically genitive

notes.role: षष्ठी → a 6th-case word compounds with what it relates to → षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

readings.vyakhya: षष्ठ्यन्तं सुबन्तेन समस्यते। राज्ञः पुरुषः = राजपुरुषः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष is the workhorse compound: राज्ञः पुरुषः "the king's man" → राजपुरुषः (2.2.8). Whenever the relation between two nouns is the plain "of / 's" (the genitive, षष्ठी शेषे), it can compound this way — देवदत्तस्य गृहम् → देवदत्तगृहम्, and so on. It is the तत्पुरुष you meet most.

readings.translation: A man skilled at dice.
readings.teaches: सप्तमी-तत्पुरुष — the विग्रह uses the locative (अक्षेषु शौण्डः, "expert AT dice")

notes.text: विग्रह: अक्षेषु शौण्डः — "expert at dice"; first member is logically locative

notes.role: सप्तमी शौण्डैः — a 7th-case word compounds with शौण्ड etc. → सप्तमी-तत्पुरुष

quiz.q: Which form is नर · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

readings.vyakhya: सप्तम्यन्तं शौण्डादिभिः समस्यते। अक्षेषु शौण्डः = अक्षशौण्डः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The locative तत्पुरुष: अक्षेषु शौण्डः, "expert AT dice," → अक्षशौण्डः (2.1.40). The विग्रह's सप्तमी (the locus of the skill) names it. With ex143–146 you now have the four case-तत्पुरुषes — द्वितीया, चतुर्थी, षष्ठी, सप्तमी — each the same heads-later compound, distinguished only by which case the analysis restores.

readings.translation: This one is a non-brahmin.
readings.teaches: नञ्-तत्पुरुष — negation by नञ् (न → अ before a consonant); "non-X"

notes.text: विग्रह: न ब्राह्मणः — "not a brahmin"; नञ् (न) prefixes, surfacing as अ before a consonant

notes.role: नञ् → the negative नञ् compounds with the following word → नञ्-तत्पुरुष

readings.vyakhya: नञः समासे न-कारस्य अ-आदेशः (हलि)। न ब्राह्मणः = अब्राह्मणः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The नञ्-तत्पुरुष negates: न ब्राह्मणः "not a brahmin" → अब्राह्मणः (2.2.6). The particle नञ् surfaces as अ- before a consonant (and as अन्- before a vowel — अनश्वः "non-horse"). This is the productive "non-/un-/a-" prefix of Sanskrit: अधर्मः, अहिंसा, असत्य — every one a नञ्-तत्पुरुष.

readings.translation: The eminent teacher instructs.
readings.teaches: प्रादि-तत्पुरुष — a preverb/particle (here प्र "forth, eminent") compounds as the first member

notes.text: विग्रह: प्रगतः आचार्यः — "a foremost teacher"; प्र (preverb) is the first member

notes.role: कुगतिप्रादयः → कु, गति-words, and the प्र-class particles compound (तत्पुरुष)

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

readings.vyakhya: प्रादयः सुबन्तेन समस्यन्ते (कुगतिप्रादयः)। प्रगतः आचार्यः = प्राचार्यः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The प्रादि-तत्पुरुष lets a preverb or particle head a compound: प्र "forth, eminent" + आचार्य → प्राचार्यः, "a foremost teacher" (2.2.18, कुगतिप्रादयः — कु "bad," the गति preverbs, and the प्र-series). The same rule gives अतिराजः "surpassing a king," कुपुरुषः "a wretched man." It rounds out the तत्पुरुष: not only case-relations but particles can occupy the first slot.

readings.sentence: तत्र एकः अब्रवीत् — देव, व्याकरणम् एव द्वादश वर्षाणि अध्येतव्यम्। ततः धर्मशास्त्राणि अर्थशास्त्राणि च। एवं व्यतीते काले बुद्धिः प्रबुध्यते इति।
readings.translation: One of them said — "Your Majesty, grammar alone must be studied for twelve years. After that, the treatises on dharma and on statecraft. When time has passed in this way, the intellect awakens."
readings.teaches:
the ministers' counsel. व्यतीते काले is a locative absolute — "when the
time had passed", with no "when" in the Sanskrit.

vocative — the ordinary way to address a king

notes.en: what is to be studied — the gerundive's object stands in the nominative
accusative — a numeral agreeing with वर्षाणि
duration — how long the studying lasts, not what it acts on
accusative plural, the case of extent in time

notes.en: gerundive — obligation, standing as the whole predicate

notes.role: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः — तव्य forms the gerundive → अध्येतव्यम्

notes.en: neuter nominative plural — the same compound shape on a second stem

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → एवं

notes.en: past participle in the locative — half of the सति सप्तमी
the locative absolute — "when time had passed in this way"
प्र + बुध् in the middle — it wakes of itself

readings.vyakhya: व्यतीते काले — सति सप्तमी। द्वादश वर्षाणि — कालद्वितीया।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Two constructions here do work that English gives to conjunctions.
व्यतीते काले is a noun and a participle both in the locative, and together
they mean "when the time had passed" — no "when" anywhere in the Sanskrit.
Once recognised, it is everywhere in classical prose.

And द्वादश वर्षाणि is accusative, though nothing is being acted on. The
accusative also marks extent — how long, how far — so "for twelve years"
takes the same case as an object would.

source.curated: Viṣṇuśarman's undertaking, lightly abridged; the words are the text's own

readings.sentence: अथ विष्णुशर्मा नाम ब्राह्मणः अवदत् — देव, एतान् राजपुत्रान् षण्मासाभ्यन्तरे नीतिशास्त्रज्ञान् करिष्यामि। यदि न करोमि तदा देवः मम नाम त्यजतु।
readings.translation: Then a brahmin named Viṣṇuśarman said — "Your Majesty, within six months I will make these princes knowers of the science of policy. If I do not, then let Your Majesty discard my name."
readings.teaches:
the promise the Pañcatantra hangs on. नीतिशास्त्रज्ञान् is the second
accusative of "make X into Y"; त्यजतु stakes an oath.

notes.en: nominative — an अन्-stem, so the न् drops in the bare form

notes.en: षट् मासाः — a numeral compound, then "within" compounded onto it
locative — the span inside which the thing happens

words.gloss: knowers of the science of policy

notes.en: नीतिशास्त्रं जानन्ति इति — the object sits inside the compound with ज्ञ
the SECOND accusative — "make them INTO knowers"

notes.role: लृट् शेषे च — लृट् for the future → करिष्यामि

notes.en: present — कृ is तनादि, taking उ rather than शप्
agent — the king referred to in the third person, as courtesy requires

quiz.q: Which form is देव · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: object of त्यजतु — a different नाम from the indeclinable above
imperative, third person — a formal undertaking, not a command

notes.role: लोट् च — the imperative → त्यजतु

readings.vyakhya: नाम इति द्विः — अव्ययं नाम, नाम्नः नाम च। संदर्भः भेदं दर्शयति।
readings.vyakhya_en:
नाम appears twice and is not the same word. विष्णुशर्मा नाम ब्राह्मणः is
the indeclinable, "by name"; मम नाम त्यजतु is the noun नामन् in the
accusative, the thing to be discarded. Nothing but position and sense
separates them.

And note त्यजतु. A third-person imperative aimed at the king is not an
order — it is how a formal oath is staked: let my name be thrown away if I
fail. The grammar is imperative; the force is a wager.

readings.sentence: अस्ति दाक्षिणात्ये जनपदे महिलारोप्यं नाम नगरम्। तत्र अमरशक्तिर् नाम राजा बभूव। तस्य त्रयः पुत्राः परमदुर्मेधसः आसन्। ततः राजा मन्त्रिणः आहूय उवाच — किम् अत्र कर्तव्यम् इति।
readings.translation: There is, in a southern country, a city named Mahilāropya. There ruled a king named Amaraśakti. He had three sons, exceedingly dull-witted. Then the king, having summoned his ministers, said — "What is to be done here?"
readings.teaches:
the Pañcatantra frame, in the same अस्ति … नाम नगरम् formula. Closes on
किम् अत्र कर्तव्यम् — a whole question with no verb in it.

notes.en: the same opening formula as the Hitopadeśa passage
"belonging to the south" — from दक्षिण with vṛddhi

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → महिलारोप्यं

notes.en: अमरशक्तिः + नाम — the visarga becomes र् before a voiced sound
nominative — the न् of राजन् drops in the bare form

notes.role: नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य — the final न् of the stem drops → राजा

quiz.q: Which form is राजन् · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the perfect — reduplicated भू → बभूव, beside आसन् below

notes.role: परोक्षे लिट् — the perfect for what lies outside the speaker's sight → बभूव

notes.en: genitive — Sanskrit says "of him were three sons" for "he had"
परम + दुर्मेधस् — "extremely of-bad-intellect", one word in Sanskrit
past plural — the imperfect beside the perfect बभूव above
the gerund with a preverb — आ + ह्वे, the summoning before the speaking

notes.role: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले — the earlier of two acts by one agent → आहूय

notes.en: the perfect — a third narrative past in four sentences
neuter nominative — the subject of the gerundive
the gerundive — obligation, and it needs no verb to predicate it

notes.role: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः — तव्य forms the gerundive → कर्तव्यम्

readings.vyakhya: अस्ति नाम नगरम् — कथामुखस्य रूढा रीतिः। हितोपदेशे अपि सैव।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The same three words open this as opened the Hitopadeśa passage: अस्ति,
then a place, then नाम and the name. It is a formula, and recognising it
is worth more than parsing it — a classical story announces itself this way
and the reader can stop working until the कथा actually starts.

किम् अत्र कर्तव्यम् has no verb in it. कर्तव्यम् is a gerundive, "to-be-done",
and that is the whole predicate: what, here, is to-be-done. Sanskrit builds
a complete question out of a participle and two indeclinables.

readings.sentence: अस्ति भागीरथीतीरे पाटलिपुत्रनामधेयं नगरम्। तत्र सर्वस्वामिगुणोपेतः सुदर्शनो नाम नरपतिः आसीत्। सः भूपतिः एकदा केनचित् पठ्यमानं श्लोकद्वयं शुश्राव।
readings.translation: There is, on the bank of the Bhāgīrathī, a city named Pāṭaliputra. There lived a king called Sudarśana, endowed with every quality of a sovereign. One day that lord of the earth heard two verses being recited by someone.
readings.teaches:
the Hitopadeśa frame opens. Three long compounds — भागीरथीतीरे,
पाटलिपुत्रनामधेयं, सर्वस्वामिगुणोपेतः — of the kind classical prose runs on.

notes.en: present — the storyteller's opening, "there is / there was"

words.gloss: on the bank of the Bhāgīrathī

notes.en: भागीरथ्याः तीरे — "the bank OF the Gaṅgā", compounded

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → पाटलिपुत्रनामधेयं

notes.en: "having Pāṭaliputra as its name" — the compound describes the city, not itself
neuter nominative — what अस्ति asserts the existence of

notes.role: अतोऽम् — the neuter अ-stem takes अम् in प्रथमा and द्वितीया → नगरम्

words.gloss: endowed with every quality of a sovereign

notes.en: सर्वस्वामिगुणैः उपेतः — a four-member compound, resolved from the end backwards
उपेत is a past participle — "come near to, endowed with"
सुदर्शनः + नाम — the visarga becomes ओ before a voiced sound
past of अस् — the frame shifts from अस्ति to आसीत्
भुवः पतिः — a second compound for the same man, as classical prose prefers
the agent of the passive participle — who was doing the reciting
instrumental, with the indefinite particle चित्
the present participle of the PASSIVE — पठ् + य + मान
the passive विकरण — what is recited, not who recites

मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → श्लोकद्वयं

notes.en: द्वौ श्लोकौ — a numeral compound, taken as a single neuter aggregate
the perfect — reduplicated श्रु → शुश्राव, the narrative past of a told tale

notes.role: परोक्षे लिट् — the perfect for a past outside the speaker's sight → शुश्राव

readings.vyakhya: कथामुखम् — अस्ति इति आरम्भः। समासबहुला गद्यरीतिः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Up to here the attested readings have been single-line maxims. This is
narrative, and it moves differently: three of its nouns are compounds
several members deep — भागीरथीतीरे, सर्वस्वामिगुणोपेतः, पाटलिपुत्रनामधेयं —
and unpacking them is most of the work of reading classical prose.

Take सर्वस्वामिगुणोपेतः from the back: उपेत, "endowed with"; endowed with
गुण, qualities; whose qualities — those of a सर्वस्वामिन्, an absolute
lord. English needs a clause where Sanskrit uses one word.

readings.sentence: अनेकसंशयोच्छेदि परोक्षार्थस्य दर्शकम्। सर्वस्य लोचनं शास्त्रं यस्य नास्त्य् अन्ध एव सः॥
readings.translation: Destroying many doubts, revealing what lies beyond sight — learning is the eye of everyone; he who has it not is blind indeed.
readings.teaches:
the verse the king overhears. परोक्षार्थस्य दर्शकम् — an agent-noun takes
the षष्ठी where the sense is transitive.

notes.en: अनेकान् संशयान् उच्छिनत्ति इति — the object stands inside the compound
genitive governed by दर्शकम् — an agent-noun takes the षष्ठी, not the द्वितीया

notes.role: कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति — before a कृत् form, the object stands in the षष्ठी → परोक्षार्थस्य

मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → शास्त्रं

genitive of possession — "of whom there is not"
न + अस्ति — the vowels merge, and the ि becomes य् before the next vowel

notes.role: इको यणचि — इ before a vowel becomes य् → नास्त्य् अन्धः

readings.vyakhya: शास्त्रं लोचनम्। यस्य तत् नास्ति सः अन्धः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The verse says learning is an eye, and then does not soften it: whoever
lacks it is blind — अन्ध एव सः, with एव refusing the metaphor any room.

परोक्षार्थस्य दर्शकम् is worth slowing on. दर्शक is "one who shows", and
what it shows stands in the genitive rather than the accusative. That is
regular before a कृत् form and catches most readers the first time: the
sense is transitive, the case is not.

readings.translation: Knowledge gives humility.
readings.teaches: a line of Hitopadeśa, read whole — an आ-stem feminine agent, a कर्मन् in the द्वितीया, a present verb

notes.text: an आ-stem feminine (formed with टाप्)

notes.role: अजाद्यतष्टाप् — feminines like विद्या take टाप् (the आ-ending); विद्या stands in प्रथमा
वर्तमाने लट् → present tense
कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → विनय is the कर्मन्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → विनयम्

readings.vyakhya: विद्या कर्त्री, विनयः कर्म, ददाति क्रिया — सर्वं पूर्वोक्तम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Your first real sentence, from the Hitopadeśa — and you can already read it. विद्या (knowledge) is the कर्तृ in प्रथमा; विनयम् (humility) is the कर्मन् in द्वितीया; ददाति (gives) is a present-tense verb. Every piece is grammar you have met on toy sentences; here it stands in real Sanskrit, unchanged.

readings.translation: From humility one attains worthiness.

notes.en: source — that from which one proceeds

notes.role: ध्रुवमपायेऽपादानम् — the starting point (humility, whence worthiness comes) is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी → विनयात् (→ विनयाद् before the voiced य, by जश्त्व)

notes.role: कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → पात्रता is the कर्मन्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → पात्रताम्

readings.vyakhya: विनयात् इति अपादानम्, पात्रताम् इति कर्म। एकस्माद् गुणाद् अन्यः फलति।
readings.vyakhya_en: The verse continues: from humility (विनयाद्, अपादान/पञ्चमी) one attains worthiness (पात्रताम्, कर्मन्/द्वितीया). Note विनयात् → विनयाद् — the final त् softens to द् before the voiced य (जश्त्व, the consonant-sandhi you met). Real text, real sandhi, all grammar you hold. The chain so far: knowledge → humility → worthiness.

source.curated: third quarter; taken whole

readings.translation: From worthiness one obtains wealth.
readings.teaches: third link of the same chain — the अपादान→कर्मन् pattern is now a rhythm

notes.role: ध्रुवमपायेऽपादानम् — the source (worthiness) is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी → पात्रत्वात् (→ पात्रत्वाद् before the voiced ध, जश्त्व)
कर्मणि द्वितीया → धनम्

readings.vyakhya: पात्रत्वाद् इति अपादानम्, धनम् इति कर्म — स एव विधिः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The same shape a third time: from worthiness (पात्रत्वाद्, पञ्चमी) one obtains wealth (धनम्, द्वितीया). Once you see the अपादान→कर्मन् rhythm — "from X, attain Y" — the verse reads itself. पात्रत्वात् → पात्रत्वाद् again by जश्त्व before ध.

source.curated: fourth quarter, completing the verse; taken whole

readings.translation: From wealth, righteousness; from that, happiness.
readings.teaches: the closing link, with the repeated verb left unspoken — आप्नोति is understood

notes.role: अपादाने पञ्चमी → धनात् (→ धनाद् before voiced ध, जश्त्व)

quiz.q: Which form is धन · पञ्चमी · एकवचन?

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → धर्मं

notes.text: धर्मम् → धर्मं (final म् → anusvāra before त, the sandhi you met)

notes.en: indeclinable adverb (= "from that", standing for तस्मात्)

readings.vyakhya: धनाद् धर्मः, धर्मात् सुखम् — क्रिया अनुवर्तते। विद्यायाः सुखपर्यन्तः क्रमः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The verse closes: from wealth, righteousness (धर्मं); from that (ततः), happiness (सुखम्). The verb आप्नोति is not repeated — it is understood, carried over (अनुवृत्ति) from the previous line, exactly as a sūtra carries words forward. You have now read a whole verse: विद्या → विनय → पात्रत्व → धन → धर्म → सुख, knowledge leading step by step to happiness.

source.curated: second hemistich only; the first (śatruṇā na hi sandadhyāt…, optative) omitted as harder

readings.sentence: सुतप्तम् अपि पानीयं शमयत्य् एव पावकम्।
readings.translation: Even well-heated water puts out fire.
readings.teaches: the first line of Pañcatantra — a complete maxim, with the particle अपि

notes.role: अतोऽम् — the neuter अ-stem takes अम् in प्रथमा and द्वितीया → सुतप्तम्

notes.en: adjective qualifying पानीयम् (agrees with it — neuter, प्रथमा)

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → पानीय (water) is the agent
अतोऽम् — neuter a-stem प्रथमा → पानीयम् (→ पानीयं, anusvāra before श)
वर्तमाने लट् → present
कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → पावक (fire) is the कर्मन्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → पावकम्

readings.vyakhya: पानीयं कर्तृ, पावकम् कर्म, शमयति क्रिया। अपि-शब्देन विरोधः सूच्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en: A complete Pañcatantra maxim, and it parses cleanly: पानीयं (water, कर्तृ/प्रथमा) शमयति (extinguishes) पावकम् (fire, कर्मन्/द्वितीया). The particle अपि ("even") + सुतप्तम् ("well-heated") carry the twist — even water that has itself been heated still quells fire. Real text, real rhetoric, grammar you hold.

source.curated: first hemistich only; second (dhanur vaṃśa-viśuddho…) omitted

readings.sentence: यस्य कस्य प्रसूतोऽपि गुणवान् पूज्यते नरः।
readings.translation: A virtuous man, though born of whomever, is honored.
readings.teaches: a genitive relative यस्य कस्य, and a passive verb पूज्यते

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि — यद् is a सर्वनाम (pronoun)
षष्ठी शेषे — the relational genitive → यस्य

notes.text: यस्य कस्य together = "of no matter whom"

notes.en: agent (a past participle agreeing with नरः)

notes.text: प्रसूतः → प्रसूतो before अपि (visarga sandhi)

notes.en: the passive विकरण — root + य, with आत्मनेपद endings

notes.text: passive (कर्मणि प्रयोग) — "is honored", as भुज्यन्ते earlier

notes.en: agent (here the grammatical subject of the passive)

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → नर

quiz.q: Which form is नर · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

readings.vyakhya: यस्य कस्य प्रसूतः अपि — सम्बन्धः अनिश्चितः; गुणवान् नरः पूज्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en: The genitive pair यस्य कस्य ("of whomsoever") waives the question of birth; अपि ("even/though") concedes it; and the verse turns on पूज्यते — "is honored," a passive, the same कर्मणि form you met in नरैः फलानि भुज्यन्ते. The sense: a man of merit (गुणवान्) is honored whatever his lineage. A relative clause and a passive, working together in real Sanskrit.

readings.sentence: न अग्निस् तृप्यति काष्ठानां न अपगानां महोदधिः।
readings.translation: Fire is not sated with logs, nor the great ocean with rivers.
readings.teaches: a genitive plural for what one is sated with, and the कर्मधारय compound महा + उदधि

notes.text: the इ-stem अग्नि you declined (अग्निः); न+अग्निः → नाग्निः

quiz.q: Which form is अग्नि · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
genitive — the thing one is sated OF

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे — the relational genitive; "sated of logs" takes षष्ठी

notes.en: compound — महा (great) + उदधि (ocean), adjective+noun same case

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः समानाधिकरणः कर्मधारयः — महा+उदधि is a कर्मधारय (महा+उदधि → महोदधि by सन्धि)

readings.vyakhya: अग्निः काष्ठानां न तृप्यति, महोदधिः अपगानां न — षष्ठी तृप्तेः विषये।
readings.vyakhya_en: Two parallel clauses: fire (अग्निः) is not sated of logs (काष्ठानां, genitive plural), the great ocean (महोदधिः, a कर्मधारय compound = महा "great" + उदधि "ocean") not of rivers. The genitive marks what one is sated *of*; the verb तृप्यति is shared across both halves. You now meet your own grammar — इ-stem, षष्ठी, कर्मधारय — in a real Pañcatantra verse.

readings.sentence: अ॒ग्निमी॑ळे पु॒रोहि॑तं य॒ज्ञस्य॑ दे॒वमृ॒त्विजं॑। होता॑रं रत्न॒धात॑मं॥
readings.translation: I praise Agni, the chosen priest, god, minister of the sacrifice, the invoker, lavisher of treasure.
readings.teaches: the accent marks appear for the first time — ॒ anudātta and ॑ for the udātta context. The grammar is already familiar: accusatives in apposition, a present verb

notes.en: "accent — the marks ॒ (anudātta, low) and ॑ (udātta/svarita); the underline on अ॒ is anudātta"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → अग्निम् (the इ-stem अग्नि you declined, here accusative)
तङानावात्मनेपदम् — ईळे is आत्मनेपद (the middle voice you met in पचते)

words.gloss: the one placed in front — the chosen priest

notes.text: padapāṭha shows the compound split: पुरः-हित (saṃhitā पुरोहितम्)

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → यज्ञस्य

quiz.q: Which form is देव · द्वितीया · एकवचन?

words.gloss: the sacrificing priest, minister of the rite
the invoker (the priest who calls the gods)

notes.en: an ऋ-stem (होतृ, like कर्तृ) in the accusative → होतारम्

notes.text: padapāṭha split रत्न-धातम (saṃhitā रत्नधातमम्)

readings.vyakhya: सर्वाणि कर्माणि अग्निविशेषणानि — द्वितीयायाम्। स्वराः उपरि अधश्च चिह्निताः।
readings.vyakhya_en: Your first Vedic verse, and the grammar is already yours: ईळे "I praise" governs a string of accusatives all in apposition to अग्निम् — पुरोहितम्, देवम्, ऋत्विजम्, होतारम्, रत्नधातमम् — "I praise Agni: priest, god, minister, invoker, treasure-giver." The ONE new thing is accent: the underline ॒ marks anudātta (low pitch), the stroke ॑ marks the raised/svarita pitch. Each word's accent is shown in its padapāṭha (isolated) form — पुरोहितं appears word-alone as पुरः-हितम्. Read it aloud with the pitches: this is how the Veda is chanted.

readings.sentence: अ॒ग्निः पूर्वे॑भि॒र्ऋषि॑भि॒रीड्यो॒ नूत॑नैरु॒त। स दे॒वाँ एह व॑क्षति॥
readings.translation: Agni, worthy to be praised by ancient seers and by new ones too — may he bring the gods here.
readings.teaches: the second verse of the same hymn — अग्नि now stands as कर्तृ, and the agents come in the instrumental plural

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → Agni is now the agent (नॉम, vs अग्निम् acc in verse 1)

quiz.q: Which form is अग्नि · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → "by the ancient seers" takes तृतीया (the -भिः ending you met in नरैः)

notes.text: a gerundive (कृत्य) of ईड् "praise" — "fit to be praised"

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → सः (he), the तद् pronoun
कर्मणि द्वितीया → देवान् (acc. plural)

notes.text: a future/subjunctive sense — "he will/may bring"

readings.vyakhya: अग्निः पूर्वैः नूतनैश्च ऋषिभिः ईड्यः; स देवान् इह आ वक्षति।
readings.vyakhya_en: The same hymn's second verse, and the frame holds: अग्निः is now the कर्तृ (nominative — last verse he was अग्निम्, the object). The seers who praise him stand in the तृतीया (पूर्वेभिः, ऋषिभिः, नूतनैः — "by the ancient, by the seers, by the new"), the same instrumental "by" you met in नरैः. ईड्यः is a gerundive — "to-be-praised." Then सः (he) देवान् (the gods, acc.) आ … वक्षति — "may bring here." One word, अग्नि, you now know in two cases and with its accent.

readings.translation: Through Agni one may win wealth and growth day by day — glorious, most rich in heroes.
readings.teaches: अग्नि now in the instrumental — अग्निना "through," the करण sense — beside the आम्रेडित दिवेदिवे "day after day"

words.gloss: through Agni, by means of Agni

notes.en: instrument — that by which the gain is won

notes.role: साधकतमं करणम् — Agni is the करण (the most effective means)
कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → अग्निना (the इ-stem, now तृतीया — a third case for अग्नि)

quiz.q: Which form is अग्नि · तृतीया · एकवचन?

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → रयिम् (an इ-stem accusative, like अग्निम्)

notes.text: a subjunctive (लेट्) sense — "may/shall win"

notes.en: object (a second thing won, alongside रयिम्)

notes.text: an आम्रेडित — the word दिवे doubled (दिवे-दिवे) to mean "day after day"

notes.en: adjective qualifying रयिम् (an अस्-stem in द्वितीया)

notes.text: padapāṭha splits वीरवत्-तम (saṃhitā वीरवत्तमम्)

notes.en: superlative adjective qualifying रयिम् (a वत्-stem + तम superlative)

readings.vyakhya: अग्निना इति करणम्, रयिं पोषं च कर्म। दिवेदिवे इति आम्रेडितम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Now अग्नि steps into a third case: अग्निना, the तृतीया — "through Agni." You have met this stem as object (अग्निम्), as agent (अग्निः), and here as instrument (अग्निना): one इ-stem across three कारकas. Through Agni one wins रयिम् (wealth) and पोषम् (growth), both accusatives, qualified by यशसं वीरवत्तमं ("glorious, hero-rich"). दिवेदिवे — दिवे doubled — is an आम्रेडित, "day after day."

readings.sentence: अग्ने॒ यं य॒ज्ञम॑ध्व॒रं वि॒श्वतः॑ परि॒भूरसि॑। स इद्दे॒वेषु॑ गच्छति॥
readings.translation: O Agni, the sacrifice, the rite which you encompass on every side — that alone goes to the gods.
readings.teaches: a Vedic relative-correlative यं … सः, the vocative अग्ने "O Agni," and असि "you are"

notes.role: सम्बोधने च — the vocative; अग्ने (a fourth use of अग्नि, now address)

quiz.q: Which form is अग्नि · सम्बोधन · एकवचन?

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → यद् is a सर्वनाम

notes.text: padapāṭha splits परि-भू (saṃhitā परिभूः); परि "around" + भू "be"

notes.en: 2nd person — "you are" (the मध्यम you met in गच्छसि)

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → सः
सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → देवेषु (सप्तमी, locative plural)

quiz.q: Which form is देव · सप्तमी · बहुवचन?

readings.vyakhya: अग्ने इति सम्बोधनम्; यं यज्ञं परिभूः असि, स इत् देवेषु गच्छति।
readings.vyakhya_en: A relative-correlative, Vedic style: यं … (यज्ञम् अध्वरं) … सः — "which sacrifice … that one." अग्ने is the सम्बोधन (vocative, "O Agni") — your fourth case-use of this one stem. असि is "you are," 2nd person (मध्यमपुरुष), matching the सम्बोधन. The sense: the rite that Agni encloses on every side (विश्वतः परिभूः) — *that one alone* (स इत्) reaches the gods (देवेषु, locative).

readings.sentence: अ॒ग्निर्होता॑ क॒विक्र॑तुः स॒त्यश्चि॒त्रश्र॑वस्तमः। दे॒वो दे॒वेभि॒रा ग॑मत्॥
readings.translation: Agni the invoker, wise in will, true, most brilliant in fame — a god, may he come with the gods.
readings.teaches: nominative epithets predicated without a verb, a बहुव्रीहि compound, and the instrumental of accompaniment

quiz.q: Which form is अग्नि · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: epithet (in apposition to अग्निः) — an ऋ-stem nominative होता

notes.text: padapāṭha splits कवि-क्रतु (saṃhitā कविक्रतुः); कवि "sage" + क्रतु "will"

notes.en: possessive compound — "(one) whose क्रतु is that of a कवि"

notes.role: अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — a बहुव्रीहि naming an external possessor

notes.text: padapāṭha splits चित्रश्रवः-तम; चित्र "bright" + श्रवस् "fame" + तम superlative

notes.role: सहयुक्तेऽप्रधाने → the accompanier takes तृतीया → देवेभिः ("with the gods")

notes.text: an aorist-subjunctive (लुङ्/लेट्) sense — "may he come"

readings.vyakhya: होता कविक्रतुः सत्यः चित्रश्रवस्तमः देवः — सर्वाणि अग्निविशेषणानि प्रथमायाम्। देवेभिः इति सहार्थे तृतीया।
readings.vyakhya_en: Verse 1 strung accusatives; this one strings NOMINATIVES. होता, कविक्रतुः, सत्यः, चित्रश्रवस्तमः, देवः — all प्रथमा, all naming अग्निः (predication, no copula needed). कविक्रतुः is a बहुव्रीहि: "(one) whose क्रतु is a sage's." Then देवेभिः is the तृतीया of accompaniment — "with the gods" — the सह-sense you met in पुत्रेण सह. आ गमत्: "may he come hither."

readings.sentence: यदं॒ग दा॒शुषे॒ त्वमग्ने॑ भ॒द्रं क॑रि॒ष्यसि॑। तवेत्तत्स॒त्यमं॑गिरः॥
readings.translation: Whatever good you will do for the worshipper, O Agni — that, indeed, is your truth, O Aṅgiras.
readings.teaches: दाशुषे "for the giver" as सम्प्रदान in the चतुर्थी, and करिष्यसि in the future

notes.en: relative — here introducing the whole clause

words.gloss: for the worshipper, for the giver (of offerings)

notes.en: recipient — the one for whom the good is done

notes.role: कर्मणा यमभिप्रैति स सम्प्रदानम् → the worshipper is सम्प्रदान
चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → दाशुषे
सम्बोधने च → अग्ने

quiz.q: Which form is अग्नि · सम्बोधन · एकवचन?

notes.role: लृट् शेषे च → future → करिष्यसि (√कृ; 2sg, "you will do")
षष्ठी शेषे → तव ("your")

notes.en: vocative — a second address to Agni

readings.vyakhya: यत् भद्रं दाशुषे करिष्यसि, तत् तव सत्यम्। दाशुषे इति सम्प्रदाने चतुर्थी।
readings.vyakhya_en: A यत्…तत् sentence with two new turns. दाशुषे is the सम्प्रदान — the dative (चतुर्थी), "for the worshipper," the same "for whom" case you met in नमो देवेभ्यः. करिष्यसि is a FUTURE (लृट्), "you will do" — √कृ now in the future, 2nd person. Two vocatives frame it: अग्ने and अङ्गिरः (a name of Agni). The sense: whatever blessing you will do for the giver — *that* is your truth.

readings.vyakhya_en: The worshippers speak now in their own voice: वयम् "we," and एमसि (उप…आ…इमसि) "we come" — a 1st-person PLURAL verb (उत्तमपुरुष बहुवचन), the same person you met as -मि in गच्छामि, now plural. To you (त्वा, accusative) we come, day by day (दिवेदिवे), at night and dawn (दोषावस्तः), in thought (धिया, तृतीया of means), bearing homage (नमः भरन्तः). A whole sentence of grammar you already hold.

readings.vyakhya: राजन्तं गोपां दीदिविं वर्धमानं — सर्वाणि कर्माणि (पूर्वस्या ऋचः त्वा-शब्दस्य विशेषणानि)। अध्वराणाम् ऋतस्य च षष्ठी; स्वे दमे इति सप्तमी।
readings.vyakhya_en: This verse has no new finite verb — it continues verse 7's "to you we come," piling accusative epithets onto that त्वा: राजन्तम् (ruling), गोपाम् (guardian), दीदिविम् (shining), वर्धमानम् (growing). Two participles (राजन्तम् active, वर्धमानम् middle) decline like nouns in the accusative. The genitives अध्वराणाम् (over the rites) and ऋतस्य (of truth) mark domain; स्वे दमे — सप्तमी — locates it: "in his own home." Cases you hold, stacked into Vedic praise.

readings.vyakhya: पिता सूनवे इव, अग्ने नः सूपायनः भव; नः स्वस्तये सचस्व। चतुर्थ्यः बह्व्यः — सूनवे नः स्वस्तये।
readings.vyakhya_en: The hymn closes with a prayer, dense with the चतुर्थी (dative): नः "for us," सूनवे "to a son," स्वस्तये "for well-being" — three datives, all the "for whom" case (सम्प्रदान). The heart is a simile: पिता इव सूनवे — "as a father (is) to a son." Two imperatives (लोट्) carry the request: भव "be!" and सचस्व "abide!" — the command mood you met in गच्छतु, here in real Vedic. With this you have read the whole first hymn of the Ṛgveda, end to end, with its accent.

readings.vyakhya: वायो इति सम्बोधनम्; आ याहि पाहि श्रुधि इति लोडर्थाः। सोमाः कर्तारः, तेषां पाहि — षष्ठ्यर्थे।
readings.vyakhya_en: A new hymn, a new god — but the grammar is the invocation pattern you just met closing hymn 1. वायो is the सम्बोधन (vocative of the उ-stem वायु, गुण → वायो like गुरो), and it is answered by a volley of imperatives (लोट्): आ याहि "come!", पाहि "drink!", श्रुधि "hear!". The Somas (सोमाः, nominative plural) stand ready (अरंकृताः); drink *of them* — तेषाम्, a genitive (षष्ठी) in the partitive sense — and hear the call (हवम्, accusative). The whole verse is address + command, the heartbeat of Vedic prayer.

They praise (जरन्ते, 3rd-person plural) you (त्वाम्, accusative) with hymns (उक्थेभिः) — the तृतीया of means, the same "with/by" you met in नरैः and धिया. Two epithets describe them: सुतसोमाः ("Soma-pressed," a बहुव्रीहि) and अहर्विदः ("day-knowers"). All grammar you hold.

readings.vyakhya_en: A feminine subject leads: धेना ("stream," an आ-stem feminine like विद्या), with two feminine adjectives agreeing — प्रपृञ्चती ("nourishing") and उरूची ("broad"). It is तव ("yours," genitive) and it जिगाति ("goes") दाशुषे ("to the worshipper," dative). The last word shows a second flavour of the dative: सोमपीतये — *for the purpose of* Soma-drinking. One case (चतुर्थी), two senses: "to whom" (दाशुषे) and "for what" (सोमपीतये).

readings.vyakhya: इन्द्रवायू इति द्वन्द्वः द्विवचने; आ गतम् इति द्विवचनलोट्; वाम् इति द्विवचनम्। द्वौ देवौ, द्विवचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The DUAL arrives — Sanskrit's third number, for exactly two. The pair इन्द्रवायू is a द्वन्द्व compound ("Indra and Vāyu") in the dual (द्विवचन, 1.4.22), and everything addressed to them is dual too: आ गतम् "come, *you two*" (a dual imperative), and वाम् "you two" (the dual of युष्मद्). Between, सुताः ("the pressed Somas") and इन्दवः ("the drops") are plural subjects. Singular, plural, and now dual — the वचन triad is complete, here in real Vedic.

readings.vyakhya: वायुः इन्द्रश्च — द्वौ; चेतथः यातम् इति द्विवचने तिङन्ते। सर्वं द्विवचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The dual you just met now drives the VERB. वायो and इन्द्रः, joined by च, are two — so चेतथः ("you two perceive") is a dual finite verb, तौ ("you two") is the dual pronoun, यातम् ("come, you two") the dual imperative, and वाजिनीवसू a dual vocative epithet. Everything addressed to the pair is dual. They take note सुतानाम् — "of the pressed Somas," a partitive genitive (षष्ठी). The whole verse is a drill in द्विवचन.

readings.vyakhya: सुन्वतः निष्कृतम् उप आ यातम् — गत्यर्थे द्वितीया। नरा इति द्विवचनसम्बोधनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The pair is called again — यातम्, "come, you two" — but now with a goal: उप … निष्कृतम्, "up to the prepared offering," where the goal of motion takes the accusative (द्वितीया, just as a destination does). सुन्वतः ("of the presser") is a genitive: whose offering it is. धिया ("by thought") is the instrumental of means you already hold. And the address नरा is नरौ — the DUAL of नर, the very first noun you ever declined, now standing in the vocative dual.

readings.vyakhya: मित्रं वरुणं च हुवे — द्वितीयायाम्। साधन्ता इति द्विवचनं कृदन्तम्, तयोः विशेषणम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: A new divine pair enters — Mitra and Varuṇa. Here they are OBJECTS: मित्रम् … वरुणम् च, accusatives, "I call (हुवे, 1st-person singular) Mitra and Varuṇa," each with its epithet (पूतदक्षम् "pure-skilled," रिशादसम् "foe-destroying"). They jointly perfect धियं घृताचीम् ("the luminous thought," accusative) — and साधन्ता, "the two who perfect," is a participle in the DUAL, agreeing with the pair. The dual now appears even on a participle.

readings.vyakhya: ऋतेन इति करणम्; मित्रावरुणौ ऋतावृधौ ऋतस्पृशा — द्विवचनसम्बोधनानि; बृहन्तं क्रतुम् आशाथे — लिटि द्विवचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Now Mitra-Varuṇa are ADDRESSED, as a single dual द्वन्द्व: मित्रावरुणौ (vocative dual), with two dual epithets, ऋतावृधौ ("Truth-increasers") and ऋतस्पृशा ("Truth-touchers"). The line opens with ऋतेन — "by the Truth," the instrumental of means. And the verb is new: आशाथे, "you two have attained" — a PERFECT (लिट्, the tense of चकार) in the DUAL. Tense, number, and compound all converge on the pair.

readings.vyakhya_en: The hymn closes with the pair as SUBJECTS, all in the nominative dual: कवी ("two seers"), मित्रावरुणा (now agents, not addressed), तुविजाता ("mightily born"), उरुक्षया ("wide-dwelling"). They दधाते — "the two hold" — a present DUAL verb of √धा, the same root as ददाति "gives." For us (नः, dative) they hold दक्षम् अपसम् ("a working skill," accusative). You have now read the whole second hymn, and through it drilled the entire dual — noun, pronoun, adjective, participle, and verb across three tenses.

readings.vyakhya_en: A new hymn, a new dual pair: the अश्विन्s, the twin horsemen, addressed throughout in the dual vocative — अश्विना, द्रवत्पाणी ("swift-handed"), शुभस्पती ("lords of bliss"), पुरुभुजा ("of many bounties"). They are asked to चनस्यतम् — "take pleasure, you two" — a DUAL imperative (लोट्), the same dual-of-command you met as आ गतम् in rd020. What they enjoy is यज्वरीः इषः, "the worshipper's offerings," an accusative PLURAL object (कर्मन्). The dual you drilled across RV 1.2 now carries to a fresh pair.

readings.vyakhya_en: The Aśvins again, addressed as नरा — which is नरौ, the dual of नर, the first noun this whole reader ever declined, now standing in a Vedic hymn. They are to वनतम् ("win, you two," dual imperative) the गिरः, "songs of praise" (accusative plural object). The means is शवीरया धिया, "with forceful thought" — an INSTRUMENTAL (करण, तृतीया), the same धी "thought" you met as धिया in rd014. One verse braids three threads you already hold: the dual address, the accusative object, and the instrument of means.

readings.vyakhya_en: The triplet to the Aśvins closes with a NOMINATIVE string describing the offering: युवाकवः सुताः वृक्तबर्हिषः — "the pressed (soma), yearning for you, with sacred grass strewn." These are predicates: the rite is ready. The pair, addressed as दस्रा ("wondrous"), नासत्या ("truthful"), रुद्रवर्तनी ("of Rudra's path"), are bidden आ यातम् — "come, you two" — the very dual imperative you first met as आ गतम् in rd020. The Aśvin hymn is complete.

readings.vyakhya: इन्द्र चित्रभानो — सम्बोधने एकवचनम्; आ याहि — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम् (द्विवचनयातमः प्रतियोगि); सुताः इमे त्वायवः पूतासः — प्रथमाबहुवचने कर्तृविशेषणानि; अण्वीभिः तना — तृतीया करणे।
readings.vyakhya_en: The hymn turns from the pair to a single god, and the grammar turns with it: इन्द्र is a SINGULAR vocative, and he is bidden आ याहि — "come!" — a 2nd-person SINGULAR imperative, exactly the dual आ यातम् of rd028 with one fewer. Hold the two side by side: यातम् = "come, you two," याहि = "come, you one." The soma is described in a nominative string (सुताः … त्वायवः … पूतासः, "pressed … longing for you … purified"), strained अण्वीभिः, "through the fine filter" (instrumental of means). The dual you drilled all through RV 1.2 now has its singular foil.

readings.vyakhya: इन्द्र — सम्बोधनम्; आ याहि — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम्; धिया — तृतीया करणे; इषितः विप्रजूतः — क्तान्तविशेषणे; उप ब्रह्माणि — द्वितीया कर्मणि गत्यर्थे; सुतावतः वाघतः — षष्ठी सम्बन्धे।
readings.vyakhya_en: The same call — आ याहि, "come" — but now Indra is moved BY something and moves TO something. He is धिया इषितः, "urged on by the thought" (instrumental of means, the धी you met as धिया in rd027), and विप्रजूतः, "hastened by the seers." Where to? उप ब्रह्माणि वाघतः — "up to the prayers of the worshipper," where उप is a preverb steering the verb of motion onto an accusative goal (ब्रह्माणि), and वाघतः is a genitive ("of the worshipper"). Means in the instrumental, goal in the accusative, possession in the genitive — three cases you hold, in one line of the Veda.

readings.vyakhya: इन्द्र हरिवः — सम्बोधनम्; आ याहि — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम्; उप ब्रह्माणि — द्वितीया गत्यर्थे; सुते — सप्तमी अधिकरणे; दधिष्व — लोटि आत्मनेपदम्; नः चनः — आत्मने ग्रहणम्। इन्द्रसूक्तत्रयं समाप्तम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The third and last call to Indra adds one new case: सुते, a LOCATIVE — "at the pressing," the occasion when the soma is pressed (अधिकरण, सप्तमी, by 2.3.36). The verb दधिष्व is √धा again — the root of दधाते "the two hold" in rd025 — but here a MIDDLE (आत्मनेपद) imperative, "take FOR YOURSELF," carrying delight (चनः, the noun of the very चनस्यतम् "take pleasure" that opened the hymn in rd026). The triplet to Indra is complete: three times "come," each adding a case — instrument, goal, and now occasion.

readings.sentence: ओमा॑सश्चर्षणीधृतो॒ विश्वे॑ देवास॒ आ ग॑त। दा॒श्वांसो॑ दा॒शुषः॑ सु॒तं॥
readings.translation: O helpers, upholders of men, O All-Gods, come — you bestowers, to the soma of the worshipper.
readings.teaches: the address turns plural — after the dual Aśvins and Indra alone, the All-Gods as a crowd: विश्वे देवासः in the vocative plural, and आ गत "come, you all"

notes.text: ओमास् = Vedic nom./voc. pl. of ओमन् "helper, friend"

notes.en: vocative PLURAL — a whole company addressed
plural (contrast dual अश्विना rd026, singular इन्द्र rd029)

notes.text: padapāṭha splits चर्षणि-धृतः; चर्षणि "men, peoples" + धृत् "holding, upholding"

notes.en: "all" — qualifying देवासः, the standard epithet विश्वे देवाः "All-Gods"

notes.text: देवासः = Vedic voc./nom. pl. of देव (classical देवाः)

notes.en: "go, come" (with आ → "come hither") — same root as आ गतम् (dual, rd020)
2nd person — PLURAL imperative ("you all, come"), vs dual गतम्, sg याहि

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → गत

notes.text: दाश्वस् = perfect active participle of दाश् "give, worship" — "having given"

words.gloss: of the worshipper, of the giver

notes.text: दाशुषः = genitive sg of the SAME दाश्वस् stem — here "of the (human) worshipper"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → सुतम्

quiz.q: Which form is सुत · द्वितीया · एकवचन?

readings.vyakhya: ओमासः चर्षणीधृतः विश्वे देवासः दाश्वांसः — सम्बोधनबहुवचनम्; आ गत — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषबहुवचनम्; दाशुषः — षष्ठी; सुतम् — द्वितीया कर्मणि।
readings.vyakhya_en: The number completes its circle. RV 1.3 has now addressed a DUAL (the Aśvins, आ यातम्), a SINGULAR (Indra, आ याहि), and here a PLURAL — विश्वे देवासः, "all the gods," a whole company, bidden आ गत, "come, you all." Set the three imperatives of √गम्/√या side by side: यातम् (two), याहि (one), गत (many). Every vocative here is plural too — ओमासः, चर्षणीधृतः, दाश्वांसः. They come दाशुषः सुतम्, "to the worshipper's pressed soma" (genitive + accusative goal). One hymn has now drilled the entire तीन वचन.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole; eighth ṛc of RV 1.3. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: विश्वे॑ दे॒वासो॑ अ॒प्तुरः॑ सु॒तमा गं॑त॒ तूर्ण॑यः। उ॒स्रा इ॑व॒ स्वस॑राणि॥
readings.translation: O All-Gods, crossing the waters, swift, come to the soma — like cattle to their pastures.
readings.teaches: the plural imperative again in आ गन्त, and a simile with इव — "like cattle to their pastures," a locative of goal inside a comparison

notes.text: padapāṭha splits अप्-तुरः; अप् "waters" + तुर् "crossing, speeding"

notes.en: goal of motion — "(come) to the soma"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → सुतम्

quiz.q: Which form is सुत · द्वितीया · एकवचन?

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → गन्त

words.gloss: like cows, like the ruddy cattle

notes.text: उस्राः "cattle" (nom. pl.) + इव "like" — the subject of the simile

notes.en: standard of comparison — "as cattle (come to pastures)"

words.gloss: to the pastures, to the home-stalls

notes.en: goal within the simile — "(as cattle come) to the pastures"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → स्वसराणि (neut. acc. pl.)

readings.vyakhya: विश्वे देवासः अप्तुरः तूर्णयः — सम्बोधनबहुवचनम्; सुतम् आ गन्त — द्वितीया गत्यर्थे लोटि बहुवचनम्; उस्राः इव स्वसराणि — उपमा (इव), द्वितीया गत्यर्थे।
readings.vyakhya_en: The plural call repeats — सुतम् आ गन्त, "come to the soma, all of you" — but the verse closes with a SIMILE: उस्राः इव स्वसराणि, "like cattle (coming) to their pastures." इव "like" marks the comparison; उस्राः ("cattle") is the standard (nominative), and स्वसराणि ("pastures") is its accusative goal, mirroring सुतम्, the gods' own goal. The grammar of the simile is the grammar of the main clause — a goal-of-motion accusative in both halves. As cattle to the fold, so the gods to the soma.

readings.sentence: विश्वे॑ दे॒वासो॑ अ॒स्रिध॒ एहि॑मायासो अ॒द्रुहः॑। मेधं॑ जुषंत॒ वह्न॑यः॥
readings.translation: The All-Gods, unfailing, of ever-approaching power, free of malice — may they, the bearers (of sacrifice), enjoy the offering.
readings.teaches: the verse turns from address to statement: the gods now stand in the nominative, and जुषन्त "may they enjoy" closes the hymn on a wish

notes.en: "all" — now NOMINATIVE (the gods as subject, not addressed)

notes.text: देवासः — here NOMINATIVE (subject), not vocative as in rd032-033
अ-स्रिध् "not failing" (privative अ + स्रिध् "err")

words.gloss: of ever-approaching power, whose wisdom comes near

notes.text: padapāṭha splits एहि-मायासः; एहि "come!" + माया "power, wisdom" — bahuvrīhi
अ-द्रुह् "not hostile" (privative अ + द्रुह् "harm")

notes.en: object — what they are to enjoy

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → मेधम्

words.gloss: may they enjoy, let them take pleasure in

notes.en: "enjoy, take pleasure in" — 3rd-person PLURAL (injunctive, wish sense)
the Vedic subjunctive (लिङर्थे लेट्, 3.4.7) — the wish "may they enjoy"
3rd person plural — "may they enjoy" (the gods as subject)

words.gloss: the bearers (of the sacrifice), the conveyers

notes.text: वह्नि "bearer, conveyer" (from वह् "carry") — in apposition to देवासः

readings.vyakhya: विश्वे देवासः अस्रिधः एहिमायासः अद्रुहः वह्नयः — प्रथमाबहुवचने कर्तृविशेषणानि; मेधम् — द्वितीया कर्मणि; जुषन्त — प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनम्। विश्वेदेवसूक्तत्रयं समाप्तम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The hymn's grammar turns one last time: from ADDRESS to STATEMENT. Through rd032–033 the gods were vocatives ("O All-Gods, come!"); here देवासः is NOMINATIVE — the SUBJECT — qualified by a string of nominative adjectives (अस्रिधः "unfailing," एहिमायासः a bahuvrīhi "whose power approaches," अद्रुहः "guileless," वह्नयः "bearers"). The verb is no longer an imperative TO them but a 3rd-person wish ABOUT them: मेधं जुषन्त, "may they enjoy the offering." The same noun in two cases across one triplet — vocative when called, nominative when described — is the whole lesson of address vs predication. The Viśvedevas triplet, and three-quarters of RV 1.3, complete.

readings.sentence: पा॒व॒का नः॒ सर॑स्वती॒ वाजे॑भिर्वा॒जिनी॑वती। य॒ज्ञं व॑ष्टु धि॒याव॑सुः॥
readings.translation: Purifying Sarasvatī, rich in plenitudes through her abundances, treasure of thought — may she desire our sacrifice.
readings.teaches: one feminine subject — सरस्वती, an ī-stem nominative — with वष्टु "may she desire" and वाजेभिः as accompaniment

notes.text: पावका = feminine of पावक "purifier" (टाप् आ by 4.1.4)

notes.role: अजाद्यतष्टाप् → feminine आ → पावका

notes.text: सरस्वती — feminine ई-stem (the नदी class you met as नदी in rd010)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → करण → वाजेभिः

notes.text: वाजिनीवती = वाजिनी "abundance" + मतुप् (वत्), feminine ई — "she who has abundance"

notes.en: object — what she is to desire

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → यज्ञम्

words.gloss: may she desire, let her wish

notes.en: 3rd person singular — a wish-imperative addressed about her

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → वष्टु

words.gloss: treasure of thought, rich through insight

notes.text: padapāṭha splits धिया-वसुः; धी "thought" + वसु "wealth" — "wealthy through thought"

readings.vyakhya: पावका सरस्वती वाजिनीवती धियावसुः — प्रथमैकवचने स्त्रीलिङ्गकर्तृविशेषणानि; वाजेभिः — तृतीया; यज्ञम् — द्वितीया कर्मणि; वष्टु — लोटि प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The last triplet of the hymn turns to a single FEMININE deity: सरस्वती, an ई-stem noun of the same नदी class you first declined in rd010. She is the subject (nominative), wrapped in feminine epithets — पावका ("purifying," with the टाप् feminine-आ of 4.1.4), वाजिनीवती ("rich in abundance"), धियावसुः ("treasure of thought"). The verb वष्टु is a 3rd-person SINGULAR imperative — "may she desire" — a wish made ABOUT her, not a command TO her. After the dual, singular-Indra, and plural triplets, the hymn closes on one goddess, in the feminine.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole; eleventh ṛc of RV 1.3. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: चो॒द॒यि॒त्री सू॒नृता॑नां॒ चेतं॑ती सुमती॒नां। य॒ज्ञं द॑धे॒ सर॑स्वती॥
readings.translation: Impeller of true sayings, awakener of right thoughts — Sarasvatī has upheld the sacrifice.
readings.teaches: two feminine agent-nouns governing the genitive — चोदयित्री … सूनृतानाम्, "impeller of true words" — and the perfect दधे "she has upheld"

notes.text: चोदयित्री = feminine agent-noun (तृच् → तृ + ई) of चुद् "impel" — "the urger"

notes.en: feminine agent-noun in apposition to सरस्वती (nominative)
genitive governed by the agent-noun — "impeller OF true words"

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → सूनृतानाम्

notes.text: चेतन्ती = feminine present participle (शतृ + ई) of चित् "perceive" — "awakening"

notes.en: feminine participle in apposition to सरस्वती

words.gloss: of right thoughts, of good intentions

notes.text: padapāṭha splits सु-मतीनाम्; सु "good" + मति "thought"

notes.en: genitive governed by the participle — "awakener OF good thoughts"

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → सुमतीनाम्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → यज्ञम्

words.gloss: she has upheld, she has established

notes.en: "hold, establish" — the √धा of दधाते (rd025) and दधिष्व (rd031), here PERFECT
3rd person singular — perfect middle "she has held"

readings.vyakhya: चोदयित्री चेतन्ती सरस्वती — प्रथमैकवचने स्त्रीलिङ्गकर्तृविशेषणानि; सूनृतानां सुमतीनाम् — षष्ठी कर्तृकर्मसम्बन्धे; यज्ञम् — द्वितीया कर्मणि; दधे — लिटि प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Sarasvatī is named by two feminine agent-words: चोदयित्री ("the impeller," a तृच्-agent-noun made feminine with ई) and चेतन्ती ("awakening," a present participle, शतृ + ई). Both GOVERN a genitive — चोदयित्री सूनृतानाम् "impeller OF true words," चेतन्ती सुमतीनाम् "awakener OF good thoughts" — the षष्ठी शेषे relation (2.3.50). Her act is दधे, "she has upheld," a PERFECT of √धा, the same root you have now seen as a present dual (दधाते, rd025), a middle imperative (दधिष्व, rd031), and now a perfect. One root, four tenses-and-moods, across the Saṃhitā.
