readings.sentence: म॒हो अर्णः॒ सर॑स्वती॒ प्र चे॑तयति के॒तुना॑। धियो॒ विश्वा॒ वि रा॑जति॥
readings.translation: Sarasvatī makes the great flood known by her banner; she illumines all our thoughts.
readings.teaches: two preverb+verb pairs (प्र चेतयति "makes known," वि राजति "shines over") + the instrument केतुना ("by her banner") — closing the whole hymn

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → अर्णः

words.gloss: by her banner, by her light-of-intelligence

notes.en: instrument — "BY her banner (she makes it known)"

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → करण → केतुना

notes.en: object — what she illumines (the धी "thought" of rd027, now plural object)

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → धियः (acc. pl.)

notes.en: preverb — "apart, over," with राजति → "shines over, illumines"

readings.vyakhya: महः अर्णः सरस्वती प्र चेतयति केतुना — द्वितीया कर्मणि, तृतीया करणे, प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनम्; धियः विश्वाः वि राजति — द्वितीयाबहुवचनं कर्मणि। ऋग्वेदस्य तृतीयं सूक्तं समाप्तम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The hymn closes with two preverb-verbs that mirror each other: प्र चेतयति, "she makes (it) forth-known," and वि राजति, "she shines over." Each preverb steers the sense of the verb. She makes known महः अर्णः, "the great flood" (accusative), केतुना, "by her banner" (instrument); she illumines धियः विश्वाः, "all the thoughts" (accusative plural) — the धी "thought" you have met since rd014, now the very thing the goddess of insight lights up. Object in the accusative, means in the instrumental, agent in the nominative: the कारक machinery of the whole reader, in the Veda's own words. **RV 1.3 is complete** — three hymns of the Ṛgveda (1.1, 1.2, 1.3) now read end to end.

chapters.title: कृदन्त — primary derivation: participles, infinitive, gerund, action-nouns

readings.translation: The man (who has) gone to the village.
readings.teaches: क्त — the past participle (निष्ठा); a root made into an adjective

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → ग्रामम् (→ ग्रामं before ग)

notes.en: a कृत्-formed word — a participle built from a root

notes.role: निष्ठा → क्त (and क्तवतु) after a root for past sense → गम् + त → गतः

readings.vyakhya: भूते निष्ठा — क्तप्रत्ययः। गम् + क्त → गतः। धातुः विशेषणं जातम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The first कृदन्त: the past participle. The निष्ठा affixes — क्त and क्तवतु (3.2.102) — attach to a root to give a past adjective. गम् + क्त → गतः "gone." It then declines like any अ-stem and agrees with its noun: ग्रामं गतः नरः "the man gone to the village." A root has become an adjective — this is what कृत् affixes do, and the whole chapter is their varieties.

readings.translation: The rice was made by the man.
readings.teaches: क्त as a passive past participle, with the agent in the तृतीया

notes.en: agent — but in the passive, expressed by तृतीया

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → the agent of a passive takes तृतीया → नरेण (with णत्व, 8.4.1)

notes.en: the object — but the grammatical subject of the passive participle

notes.role: निष्ठा → क्त → कृ + त → कृतः

notes.en: agrees with ओदनः (the patient), not the agent

readings.vyakhya: क्तप्रत्ययः कर्मणि — कर्ता तृतीयायाम्, कर्म प्रथमायाम्। नरेण ओदनः कृतः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The क्त participle is usually PASSIVE: it agrees with the patient, and the agent stands in the instrumental (2.3.18) — exactly the कर्मणि (passive) construction. नरेण ओदनः कृतः = "by the man the rice (was) made." This is the everyday Sanskrit past: not a finite verb but a participle + agent-in-तृतीया. (Note रामेण-style णत्व in नरेण.)

readings.translation: The man, (while) going, sees.
readings.teaches: शतृ — the present active participle (replaces लट्)

notes.en: the शतृ affix — present active participle, replacing लट्

notes.role: लटः शतृशानचौ → शतृ/शानच् replace लट् for a participle → गच्छत् → गच्छन्
तौ सत् → these two are termed सत् (the "present-participle" साधन)
उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थाने → the त-stem inserts नुम् before strong endings → गच्छन्

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

readings.vyakhya: लटः स्थाने शतृ — वर्तमाने कर्तरि। गच्छत् → गच्छन् नुमा। "गच्छन् पश्यति" = गच्छन् सन् पश्यति।
readings.vyakhya_en: The present participle: शतृ (active) replaces the present लट् (3.2.124) when the form is a participle agreeing with the agent — गम् → गच्छत्, which surfaces as गच्छन् (नुम्-insertion before strong endings, 7.1.70). "गच्छन् नरः पश्यति" = "the man, going, sees" = "while he goes, he sees." It is a त्-stem consonant participle, declining राजन्-style (strong/weak). The middle counterpart is शानच् (यजमानः "sacrificing").

readings.translation: The man wishes to go to the village.
readings.teaches: तुमुन् — the infinitive ("to do"), for a purposed action

quiz.q: Which form is नर · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → ग्रामं

notes.en: the तुमुन् affix — "to ___", an indeclinable verbal goal

notes.role: तुमुन्ण्वुलौ क्रियायां क्रियार्थायाम् → तुमुन् for the purposed action → गम् + तुम् → गन्तुम्

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

readings.vyakhya: क्रियार्थायां क्रियायां तुमुन् — गन्तुम्। अव्ययम्, इच्छाद्यपेक्षम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The infinitive is तुमुन् (3.3.10): "to go" = गन्तुम्, "to do" = कर्तुम्, "to see" = द्रष्टुम्. It names the action one *aims at* — so it pairs with verbs of wishing, being able, beginning: गन्तुम् इच्छति "wishes to go," गन्तुं शक्नोति "can go." Unlike क्त and शतृ, तुमुन् is indeclinable (an अव्यय) — it never changes form.

readings.translation: Having gone to the village, the man eats rice.
readings.teaches: क्त्वा — the gerund, naming the earlier of two acts by one agent

quiz.q: Which form is नर · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → ग्रामं

notes.en: the क्त्वा affix — the prior action, same agent

notes.role: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले → क्त्वा after the verb of the EARLIER act, one shared agent → गत्वा
क्त्वातोसुन्कसुनः → a क्त्वा-form is an अव्यय (indeclinable)
मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → ओदनं

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

readings.vyakhya: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले क्त्वा — गत्वा खादति = गत्वा पश्चात् खादति। एकः कर्ता, द्वे क्रिये।
readings.vyakhya_en: The gerund (क्त्वा, the "absolutive") chains two acts of ONE agent, marking the EARLIER (3.4.21): गत्वा … खादति = "having gone … (he) eats." First go, then eat — one man, two actions, the क्त्वा-form taking the first. It is indeclinable (1.1.40). When a prefix is present it becomes ल्यप् instead (आगत्य "having come"), but the meaning — "having ___, then ___" — is the same. This is how Sanskrit strings narrative: a row of gerunds ending in one finite verb.

readings.translation: Going is better. / The going is preferable.
readings.teaches: ल्युट् — the action-noun ("the ___ing"), a कृत् abstract

words.gloss: the going, the act of going

notes.en: the ल्युट् affix (→ अन) — names the action

notes.role: ल्युट् च → ल्युट् after a root for the action's name → गम् + अन → गमनम्

readings.vyakhya: भावे ल्युट् — गमनम्। क्रियायाः नाम नपुंसकम्। घञापि भावः (यथा "यागः")।
readings.vyakhya_en: Beyond participles, कृत् affixes also build action-NOUNS — "the going," "the doing." ल्युट् (→ अन, 3.3.115) gives गमनम् "going," दर्शनम् "seeing," a neuter अ-stem that declines like फल. The affix घञ् does the same with a different shape and grade (यज् → यागः "sacrifice," 3.3.18 भावे). So one root yields a whole family: गतः (gone), गच्छन् (going), गन्तुम् (to go), गत्वा (having gone), गमनम् (the going) — the कृदन्त system entire.

readings.translation: He who is lord of the world — he is "Being" itself.
readings.teaches: क्विप् — the kṛt affix that vanishes entirely, leaving the bare root standing as a noun: भू → भूः

notes.text: क्विप् = a कृत् affix that wholly disappears (its क्, व्, प् are all इत्), leaving भू + सुप्

notes.role: क्विप् च — the affix क्विप् (zero) forms a kṛt-noun from the root → भू
अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यते — क्विप् is seen widely, beyond its named bases

notes.en: a kṛt noun with no visible suffix

readings.vyakhya: क्विबन्तः प्रत्ययलोपे धातुरेव नाम। भू + क्विप् = भू, सुपि भूः।
readings.vyakhya_en: Most kṛt affixes add visible material (-त, -मान, -तुम्). क्विप् is the opposite: every one of its letters is an इत्-marker, so the WHOLE affix vanishes, and the bare root stands as a noun (3.2.76). भू "be" + क्विप् → भू, declined भूः "Being." This is how Sanskrit makes nouns like धी (thought, from ध्यै), स्तुत् (praiser), युज् (yoke-fellow) — roots used directly as words.

readings.translation: He who gives wealth is a "wealth-giver."
readings.teaches: क — the short kṛt: after an आ-ending root (with no preverb), क replaces the आ (दा → द)

notes.text: धन (object) + दा + क; the क affix shortens दा → द → धन-द-ः

notes.role: आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः — after an आ-final root without a preverb, the affix is क → -द
कर्मण्यण्… — an object compounded with a kṛt; here क (not अण्) by 3.2.3

readings.vyakhya: आदन्तात् अनुपसर्गात् कः; आकारलोपः। धन + दा + क = धनदः।
readings.vyakhya_en: After a root ending in आ, with no preverb, the agent-suffix is the short क — and it cuts the आ to nothing (3.2.3, आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः). दा "give" → -द; धनं ददाति "gives wealth" condenses to धनदः "wealth-giver." The same क gives गोदः "cow-giver," जलदः "water-giver = cloud," पयोदः. Contrast कुम्भकारः (ex with अण्): the root's final sound decides which kṛt applies.

readings.translation: He goes along eating and eating (eating repeatedly).
readings.teaches: णमुल् — the absolutive of repeated or intense action, reduplicated for "again and again"

notes.text: भुज् + णमुल् → भोजम्; doubled (आभीक्ष्ण्य) to mean "again and again"

notes.role: आभीक्ष्ण्ये णमुल् च — for repeated action, the absolutive णमुल् (-अम्), often doubled

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

readings.vyakhya: आभीक्ष्ण्ये णमुल्; द्विरुक्तिः। भुज् + णमुल् = भोजं भोजम् "पुनः पुनः भुक्त्वा"।
readings.vyakhya_en: Beside क्त्वा "having Xed" (ex with गत्वा), णमुल् is a second absolutive — used for REPEATED or intense action and typically DOUBLED (3.4.22, आभीक्ष्ण्ये णमुल् च). भुज् "eat" → भोजं भोजम् "eating and eating, again and again." So स्मारं स्मारम् "remembering over and over," पायं पायम् "drinking repeatedly": an indeclinable that paints habitual or insistent action.

readings.sentence: कर्ता, कर्तारम्, कर्त्रा, कर्त्रे, कर्तुः, कर्तरि।
readings.translation: The agent-noun कर्तृ "doer" declined: nom, acc, instr, dat, gen/abl, loc (singular).
readings.teaches: कर्तृ through its cases — the तृच् agent-noun is an ऋ-stem, and takes the same strong and weak grades as पितृ

notes.text: कृ + तृच् → कर्तृ "doer" (3.1.133); nom.sg कर्ता with vṛddhi, like पिता

notes.role: ण्वुल्तृचौ — the agent affixes ण्वुल् and तृच् → कर्तृ

quiz.q: Which form is कर्तृ · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.text: गुण-strengthened अर् in the strong cell → कर्तारम् (cf. पितरम्)

notes.role: ऋतो ङिसर्वनामस्थानयोः — ऋ → गुण अर् in the strong cells → कर्तार्

notes.text: weak cell: ऋ stays → कर्त्र् + आ → कर्त्रा

quiz.q: Which form is कर्तृ · तृतीया · एकवचन?
Which form is कर्तृ · चतुर्थी · एकवचन?
Which form is कर्तृ · षष्ठी · एकवचन?
Which form is कर्तृ · सप्तमी · एकवचन?

readings.vyakhya: तृजन्तम् ऋदन्तम्; पितृवत् नरबलदुर्बलभेदेन नमति। कर्ता — कर्तारम् — कर्त्रा …।
readings.vyakhya_en: A तृच् agent-noun (कृ → कर्तृ "doer," 3.1.133) is not a fixed word — it DECLINES, exactly like the kinship ऋ-stem पितृ (ex043/044/141). Strong cells take गुण/vṛddhi (कर्ता nom, कर्तारम् acc), weak cells keep ऋ (कर्त्रा, कर्त्रे, कर्तुः, कर्तरि). So दातृ → दाता/दातारम्, नेतृ → नेता/नेतारम्: every agent-noun is an ऋ-stem paradigm. This closes the loop between कृदन्त (how the word is formed) and सुप् (how it then declines).

readings.translation: He who presses the soma is a "soma-presser."
readings.teaches: क्विप् in an upapada compound — the root (here सु "press") stands as the second member, suffix elided

notes.text: सोम (object) + सु + क्विप्; the affix vanishes, leaving सु → सुत् (with त्-augment in the cluster)

notes.role: सत्सूद्विषद्…उपसर्गेऽपि क्विप् — सू and the listed roots take क्विप् even in compounds → -सुत्

readings.vyakhya: क्विबन्तः उपपदे; प्रत्ययलोपात् धातुः अन्त्यपदम्। सोमं सुनोति = सोमसुत्।
readings.vyakhya_en: क्विप् (the zero affix, ex161) is especially common in COMPOUNDS, where the root becomes the second member and the suffix vanishes (3.2.61). सोमं सुनोति "presses the soma" → सोमसुत् "soma-presser." The same gives अग्निचित् "fire-piler" (चि), धृतव्रत "vow-holder" type, ऋत्विज् "season-sacrificer" (यज्). Such root-final compounds fill the Vedic vocabulary — now you can parse them: object + bare root + क्विप्.

chapters.title: तद्धित — secondary nominal derivation (selected, learner-facing only)

readings.translation: The descendant of Daśaratha is "Dāśarathi" (= Rāma).
readings.teaches: अपत्य — the patronymic; इञ् after an अ-stem, with आदिवृद्धि

notes.en: genitive — the विग्रह "of ___" that the affix replaces

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → दशरथस्य (the analysis; the तद्धित condenses it)
मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → अपत्यं

notes.en: the SENSE the affix carries — "descendant of"
a secondary derivative — noun made from a noun

notes.role: तस्यापत्यम् → in the sense "descendant of ___", a तद्धित affix
अत इञ् → after an अ-stem the affix is इञ् → दशरथ + इ → दाशरथि (आदिवृद्धि अ→आ)

readings.vyakhya: तस्य अपत्यम् इति अर्थे इञ्; आदेर्वृद्धिः। दशरथ → दाशरथिः।
readings.vyakhya_en: A तद्धित attaches to a *finished* word and makes a new one. The patronymic: "descendant of X" (4.1.92) becomes a single word by adding इञ् after an अ-stem (4.1.95), with vṛddhi of the first vowel — दशरथ → दाशरथिः "son of Daśaratha." The genitive phrase दशरथस्य अपत्यम् collapses into one derived noun. (Other bases take अण् → गार्ग्यः, यञ् → for गोत्र lines.)

readings.translation: One born/found in Mathurā is "Māthura."
readings.teaches: तत्र भवः — "born in / belonging to a place", with आदिवृद्धि

notes.en: locus — the सप्तमी base of the derivation

notes.role: सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → मथुरायाम् (the विग्रह "in Mathurā")
तत्र भवः → "being in (that place)" → an affix after the locative base → माथुरः (आदिवृद्धि)

readings.vyakhya: तत्र भवः इति अर्थे अण्; मथुरा → माथुरः। देशकालादेः भवार्थः।
readings.vyakhya_en: "Born in / found in / belonging to a place" — तत्र भवः (4.3.53) — turns a locative phrase into one adjective: मथुरायां भवः → माथुरः "of Mathurā," with vṛddhi (मथुरा → माथुर). The same family gives "relating to X" (तस्येदम्, 4.3.120) and "good for X" (तस्मै हितम्, 5.1.5). These locative/genitive/dative taddhitas are how Sanskrit forms its everyday relational adjectives.

readings.translation: He who has wealth is "wealthy" (dhanavān).
readings.teaches: मतुप् — the possessive "having ___"

notes.en: "be" — the विग्रह "X is his / in him"

notes.role: तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् → मतुप् "it is his / in him" → धन + मतुप् → धनवत् → धनवान्
उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थाने → the मतुप् (वत्) stem inserts नुम् before strong endings → धनवान्

readings.vyakhya: तत् अस्य अस्ति इति मतुप् — मत्वर्थः। धन + मतुप् → धनवान् (बुद्धिमान् वत्)।
readings.vyakhya_en: The possessive: "having X / in whom X is" — मतुप् (5.2.94). धन + मतुप् → धनवान् "wealthy," बुद्धि + मतुप् → बुद्धिमान् "wise" (the affix shows as -वत्/-मत्, declining राजन्-style with नुम्). You met गुणवान् and वीरवत्तमं in real text; this is the rule behind them — the workhorse that turns any noun into "the one who has it."

readings.translation: This one is cleverer than that.
readings.teaches: तरप् — the comparative ("more ___ than")

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → अयं
पञ्चमी विभक्ते → the term compared-from takes पञ्चमी → ततः
द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ → तरप् (तर)/ईयसुन् for comparison of two → पटु + तर → पटुतरः

readings.vyakhya: द्वयोः विभजने तरप्; पञ्चमी विभक्ते। पटु → पटुतरः, अन्यस्मात्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Comparing TWO: तरप् → -तर (5.3.57), "more X (than the other)" — पटु → पटुतरः "cleverer." The thing surpassed stands in the ablative (पञ्चमी, 2.3.42): ततः पटुतरः "cleverer than that." The matching ईयस् (-ीयस्) is the irregular comparative (श्रेयस्, the श्रेयः you met). For surpassing ALL — the superlative — it is तमप्/इष्ठन् (5.3.55): पटुतमः "cleverest" (you saw रत्नधातमम्, वीरवत्तमम्).

readings.translation: The state of being heavy/a-teacher is "gurutva" (heaviness / gravity).
readings.teaches: त्व/तल् — the abstract noun ("-ness, the state of")

words.gloss: of the heavy one / of the teacher

notes.en: genitive — the base whose "-ness" is named (उ-stem गुरु → गुरोः)

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → गुरोः

words.gloss: heaviness, gravity; the state of being a guru

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ → त्व (and तल् → ता) for "the state of ___" → गुरु + त्व → गुरुत्वम्

readings.vyakhya: तस्य भावः इति त्व-तलौ। गुरुत्वम् (नपुंसकम्), गुरुता (स्त्री)। भाववाचकम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The abstract: "the state of being X" — त्व and तल् (5.1.119). गुरु → गुरुत्वम् "heaviness/gurutva" (neuter, with -त्व) or गुरुता "guru-hood" (feminine, with -ता). देव → देवत्वम्/देवता. This is Sanskrit's "-ness / -hood": take any noun or adjective, add त्व or ता, and you have named its quality as a thing. Patronymic, place-adjective, possessive, comparative, abstract — the तद्धित system's productive core.

readings.translation: Among all the clever, this one is the cleverest.
readings.teaches: तमप् — the superlative ("most ___ of all"); निर्धारण in सप्तमी

notes.role: यतश्च निर्धारणम् → the group one is singled out from → सप्तमी (or षष्ठी) → सर्वेषु

notes.en: the class — locative plural, parallel to सर्वेषु

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → अयं
अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ → तमप् (तम)/इष्ठन् for surpassing all → पटु + तम → पटुतमः

readings.vyakhya: अतिशायने तमप्; निर्धारणे सप्तमी। सर्वेषु पटुषु पटुतमः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The superlative completes the pair: तमप् → -तम (5.3.55), "most X of all" — पटु → पटुतमः "the cleverest." The group one is singled out FROM takes निर्धारण-सप्तमी (2.3.41): सर्वेषु पटुषु "among all the clever." So तर/तम are the degree-affixes — पटुतरः "cleverer (of two)," पटुतमः "cleverest (of all)" — closing the productive तद्धित set the reader needs.

readings.translation: This belongs to Upagu — it is "Aupagava" (Upagu's).
readings.teaches: तस्येदम् — "belonging to / coming from X"; अण् with आदिवृद्धि (उपगु → औपगव)

notes.en: genitive — the विग्रह "of ___" the affix replaces

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → उपगोः
तस्येदम् → in the sense "belonging to ___", the affix अण्
तद्धितेष्वचामादेः → आदिवृद्धि उ→औ → औपगव

readings.vyakhya: तस्य इदम् इति अर्थे अण्; आदेर्वृद्धिः। उपगु → औपगवम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The "possession / belonging" affix: तस्येदम् "this is X's" (4.3.120) condenses into one word with अण्, plus आदिवृद्धि — vṛddhi of the first vowel (7.2.117). उपगोः इदम् "Upagu's" → औपगवम्. The same आदिवृद्धि you saw in the patronymic दाशरथिः (ex080) is the signature of this whole अण् family.

readings.translation: A modification of gold is "golden" (made of gold).
readings.teaches: तस्य विकारः — "made of / a modification of X"; अण् with आदिवृद्धि

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → सुवर्णस्य

notes.en: the sense — "a thing made of / changed from X"

notes.role: तस्य विकारः → in the sense "modification/product of ___", अण्
तद्धितेष्वचामादेः → आदिवृद्धि उ→औ → सौवर्ण

readings.vyakhya: तस्य विकारः इति अर्थे अण्। सुवर्ण → सौवर्णम् "स्वर्णमयम्"।
readings.vyakhya_en: "Made of X / a product of X": तस्य विकारः (4.3.134) → अण् with आदिवृद्धि. सुवर्णस्य विकारः "a modification of gold" → सौवर्णम् "golden, of gold." This is the material-adjective: the same shape names "made of wood" (दारु → दारवम्), "made of clay," and so on.

readings.translation: A cloth dyed with ochre is a "kāṣāya" (ochre robe).
readings.teaches: तेन रक्तं रागात् — "dyed with X"; अण् from the name of a dye, with आदिवृद्धि

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → करण → कषायेण

notes.en: अर्थ — here the specialised "dyed-with" sense (तेन रक्तम्)

notes.role: तेन रक्तं रागात् → "dyed with (a dye)", अण् from the dye-name
तद्धितेष्वचामादेः → आदिवृद्धि अ→आ → काषाय

readings.vyakhya: तेन रक्तम् इति रागवाचिनः अण्। कषाय → काषायम्। (मुनीनां वस्त्रम्।)
readings.vyakhya_en: From the name of a dye, "dyed with X": तेन रक्तं रागात् (4.2.1) → अण् with आदिवृद्धि. कषायेण रक्तम् "dyed with ochre" → काषायम् — the ochre robe of ascetics. Notice the विग्रह uses the तृतीया (कषायेण, "by the dye"), the instrument; the affix swallows it into one adjective.

readings.vyakhya: तस्मै हितम् इति अर्थे प्रत्ययः; विग्रहे चतुर्थी। सर्वस्मै हितं सर्वहितम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: A relational affix whose विग्रह uses the चतुर्थी: तस्मै हितम् "good FOR X" (5.1.5). सर्वस्मै हितम् "good for all" → सर्वहितम्. This sits beside तत्र भवः (place, 4.3.53, ex081) and तस्येदम् (possession, ex131): a family of affixes each replacing one case-relation — dative here, locative and genitive there.

readings.translation: He comes from the village.
readings.teaches: पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् — the adverb-affix तसिल् (-तस्) in the ablative sense ("from ___")

notes.role: पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् → in the पञ्चमी (ablative) sense, the affix तसिल् → -तस्

notes.en: an indeclinable तद्धित — ग्राम + तस् = ग्रामतः ("from the village")
indeclinable (it does not take सुप् endings)
the thematic अ between root and ending

readings.vyakhya: पञ्चम्यर्थे तसिल्; ग्राम + तस् = ग्रामतः अव्ययम्। ग्रामात् = ग्रामतः।
readings.vyakhya_en: Instead of the case-ending पञ्चमी (ग्रामात्), the same ablative sense can be carried by a तद्धित adverb: पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् (5.3.7) adds -तस् → ग्रामतः "from the village," an indeclinable. So ग्रामात् आगच्छति and ग्रामतः आगच्छति say the same thing — the second with an अव्यय taddhita. This affix gives ततः, यतः, सर्वतः, and the like.

readings.translation: He studies like a brahmin.
readings.teaches: तेन तुल्यं…वतिः — the affix वति (-वत्), "like / in the manner of X"

words.gloss: like a brahmin, in a brahmin's manner

notes.role: तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः → in the sense "like ___ (in action)", the affix वति

notes.en: an indeclinable तद्धित — ब्राह्मण + वत् = ब्राह्मणवत् ("brahmin-like")

readings.vyakhya: तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेत् वतिः। ब्राह्मण + वत् = ब्राह्मणवत् "ब्राह्मणेन तुल्यम्"।
readings.vyakhya_en: "Like X, in the manner of X (when comparing an action)": तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः (5.1.115) → the affix वति, -वत्. ब्राह्मणवत् अधीते "studies like a brahmin" = ब्राह्मणेन तुल्यम्. An indeclinable adverb of comparison — the same वत् gives मातृवत् "like a mother," राजवत् "like a king."

readings.sentence: द्वौ भ्रातरौ क्षेत्रम् अभजेताम्। ज्येष्ठः अवादीत् — अद्य अहम् अर्धम् अगृह्णाम्, त्वम् च अर्धम् गृहाण। कनिष्ठः तत् अश्रौषीत्, किन्तु न अतुष्यत्। सः ग्रामस्य वृद्धान् अपृच्छत् — केन एषा भूमिः विभक्ता। वृद्धाः अवादिषुः — यः स्वयम् विभजति सः न स्वयम् गृह्णाति। तत् श्रुत्वा ज्येष्ठः लज्जितः अभूत्, कनिष्ठाय च वरम् अर्धम् अददात्।
readings.translation: Two brothers divided a field. The elder spoke — "Today I have taken half; you take the other half." The younger heard that, but was not satisfied. He asked the village elders — "By whom was this land divided?" The elders spoke — "He who divides himself does not himself take." Hearing that, the elder became ashamed, and gave the better half to the younger.
readings.teaches:
अवादीत्, अश्रौषीत्, अवादिषुः, अभूत् — the aorist across three persons and
both numbers. विभक्ता names the act as done; वृद्धाः and अवादिषुः close on
visarga at the pause.

readings.vyakhya: लुङः चत्वारि रूपाणि — अवादीत् अश्रौषीत् इति प्रथमपुरुषे एकवचनम्, अवादिषुः इति बहुवचनम्, अभूत् इति भू-धातोः अपुसीयम्। ज्येष्ठः कनिष्ठः इति इष्ठन्प्रत्ययान्तौ। केन एषा भूमिः विभक्ता इति कर्मणि क्तम्, कर्तरि तृतीया।
readings.vyakhya_en: The aorist widens here: अवादीत् and अश्रौषीत् are third singular, अवादिषुः is third plural of the same verb as अवादीत्, and अभूत् is √भू with no सिच् at all — the ending sits straight on the root. ज्येष्ठः and कनिष्ठः are the same suffix इष्ठन् on two opposed adjectives, and they carry the whole plot between them. केन एषा भूमिः विभक्ता asks the question with a participle and an instrumental agent, and the elders answer with a present-tense generality rather than a fact about this field.

source.ref: the messenger who came today — our own telling
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: अद्य दूतः नगरम् अगमत्। सः राज्ञः पुरतः अवादीत् — शत्रवः सेनाम् अनयन्, ग्रामान् च अदहन्। राजा तत् अश्रौषीत्, क्षणम् च तूष्णीम् आसीत्। ततः सः अवादीत् — यत् त्वया उक्तम् तत् सत्यम् चेत्, अहम् अद्य एव सेनाम् प्रेषयामि। मन्त्री अवदत् — देव, धैर्यम् एव बलम्। राजा अकार्षीत् यत् मन्त्री अवदत्।
readings.translation: Today a messenger went to the city. He spoke before the king — "The enemies led out an army, and burned the villages." The king heard that, and was silent a moment. Then he spoke — "If what has been said by you is true, I send the army this very day." The minister said — "Your majesty, steadiness alone is strength." The king did what the minister said.
readings.teaches:
अगमत्, अवादीत्, अश्रौषीत्, अकार्षीत् — four aorists, the past of what
happened today. शत्रवः and राज्ञः show the visarga taking a sibilant and
a stop; तूष्णीम् holds its ष् unchanged.

readings.vyakhya: अद्येति लुङः निमित्तम्। अगमत् अवादीत् अश्रौषीत् अकार्षीत् इति चत्वारः लुङः। अनयन् अदहन् अवदत् इति लङः, तयोः भेदः कालमात्रे। यत् त्वया उक्तम् इति भावे क्तम्, त्वयेति कर्तरि तृतीया। चेदिति न वाक्यादौ तिष्ठति।
readings.vyakhya_en: अद्य sets the tense: four verbs here are aorists — अगमत्, अवादीत्, अश्रौषीत्, अकार्षीत् — and three are the ordinary past in लङ् — अनयन्, अदहन्, अवदत्. The two sit side by side in one paragraph, so the difference is a matter of what the sentence is doing rather than of what happened. अश्रौषीत् shows the ष् of सिच् after वृद्धि, while तूष्णीम् carries a ष् that no join produced. यत् त्वया उक्तम् puts the agent in the instrumental and the verb in a participle — the clause has no finite verb at all, and तत् सत्यम् answers it with none either.

source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: नगरे धनवान् वणिक् वसति स्म। सः चिन्तयत् — किम् मया कर्तव्यम्, केन मम जीवनम् सफलम् भवेत्। एकः मुनिः अवदत् — दानम् कुरु। तत् श्रुत्वा वणिक् दरिद्रेभ्यः अन्नम् अयच्छत्। तस्य दानेन बहवः जनाः अतुष्यन्। रामेण तत् दृष्टम्, सः च अवदत् — एतत् एव धर्मस्य आचरणम्।
readings.translation: In a city there lived a wealthy merchant. He thought — "What should I do? By what would my life be fruitful?" A sage said — "Practise giving." Hearing that, the merchant gave food to the poor. By his giving many people were satisfied. Rāma saw that, and said — "This alone is the practice of dharma."
readings.teaches:
दानम्, दानेन and आचरणम् name acts as things across one story. भवेत् asks
what would make a life fruitful; रामेण closes with णत्व across the ए.

readings.vyakhya: जीवनम् दानम् आचरणम् — त्रीणि क्रियानामानि एकस्याम् कथायाम्।
readings.vyakhya_en:
जीवनम्, दानम्, आचरणम् — three acts named as things, and the story turns on
treating them that way. A life can be fruitful, a giving can satisfy people,
a practice can be pointed at. None of them needs a verb.

source.ref: the student who went to the forest — our own telling
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: शिष्यः वनम् अगच्छत्। तत्र सः फलानि अभक्षयत्, जलम् च अपिबत्। सायम् गुरुः अपृच्छत् — कुत्र आसीः। शिष्यः अवदत् — वने आसम्, गुरो। तत् श्रुत्वा गुरुः अवदत् — पठनम् एव तव कार्यम्, न तु वनगमनम्। शिष्यः अवदत् — क्षमस्व, अद्य प्रभृति पठेयम्। रामेण अपि तत् श्रुतम्, सः च अहसत्।
readings.translation: The student went to the forest. There he ate fruits and drank water. In the evening the teacher asked — "Where were you?" The student said — "I was in the forest, teacher." Hearing that, the teacher said — "Studying alone is your work, not going to the forest." The student said — "Forgive me; from today I will study." Rāma too heard that, and he laughed.
readings.teaches:
two action-nouns set against each other — पठनम् and वनगमनम् — and the
optative पठेयम् answering the teacher. अभक्षयत् and अपिबत् carry the
narrative; तच्छ्रुत्वा shows श्चुत्व at the join.

readings.vyakhya_en:
पठनम् and वनगमनम् are the same kind of word — an act named as a thing —
and the teacher sets one against the other. Sanskrit can compound the goal
straight into the noun: वनं गमनम् becomes वनगमनम्, going-to-the-forest, in
one word.

source.ref: the potter and the king's brother — our own telling
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: ग्रामे कुलालः वसन् घटान् अकरोत्। एकदा राज्ञः भ्राता तम् ग्रामम् आगच्छत्। कुलालम् कार्यम् कुर्वन्तम् दृष्ट्वा सः अवदत् — मम गृहे शतम् घटाः स्थापनीयाः। कुलालः अवदत् — कर्तव्यम् एतत्, किन्तु मूल्यम् दातव्यम्। भ्राता हसन् अवदत् — पिता मे राजा आसीत्, अहम् न मूल्यम् ददामि। कुलालः अवदत् — तर्हि घटाः न सन्ति। तत् श्रुत्वा भ्राता लज्जितः अभवत्।
readings.translation: In a village a potter lived, making pots. One day the king's brother came to that village. Seeing the potter doing his work, he said — "A hundred pots are to be placed in my house." The potter said — "This is to be done, but the price is to be given." The brother, laughing, said — "My father was a king; I do not give a price." The potter said — "Then there are no pots." Having heard that, the brother was ashamed.
readings.teaches:
a potter refuses a prince. Four participles and three gerundives against
six finite verbs; पिता and भ्राता carry their ऋ-stem grades through it.

readings.vyakhya: कर्तव्यम् एतत्, किन्तु मूल्यम् दातव्यम्। द्वे कृत्ये, द्वौ पक्षौ।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The potter's answer is two gerundives and nothing else: कर्तव्यम् एतत्,
किन्तु मूल्यम् दातव्यम्. He concedes the work and states his condition in
the same construction the prince used to give the order.

That is what makes it a refusal rather than a complaint. स्थापनीयाः was an
instruction; दातव्यम् answers it in kind.

readings.sentence: राजा वनम् गच्छन् एकम् मुनिम् अपश्यत्। मुनिः वृक्षस्य अधः उपविशन् शिष्यान् अवदत् — कर्तव्यम् धर्मम् जानीत। राज्ञः भ्राता अपि तत्र आसीत्। सः पितुः वचनम् स्मरन् मुनिम् अपृच्छत् — किम् मया करणीयम्। मुनिः अवदत् — भ्रातरम् रक्ष, राजानम् सेव, पितरम् च मा त्यज। एतत् त्रयम् सर्वदा स्मरणीयम्। तत् श्रुत्वा भ्रातरौ शान्तौ अभवताम्।
readings.translation: The king, going to the forest, saw a sage. The sage, sitting beneath a tree, said to his students — "Know the dharma that is to be done." The king's brother was there too. He, remembering his father's words, asked the sage — "What is to be done by me?" The sage said — "Protect your brother, serve the king, and do not abandon your father. These three are always to be remembered." Having heard that, the two brothers became calm.
readings.teaches:
three participles doing the work of "while" — गच्छन्, उपविशन्, स्मरन् —
and three gerundives stating obligation with no verb: कर्तव्यम्, करणीयम्,
स्मरणीयम्.

readings.vyakhya: गच्छन् उपविशन् स्मरन् — त्रीणि शतृ-रूपाणि। कर्तव्यम् करणीयम् स्मरणीयम् — त्रीणि कृत्य-रूपाणि।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Three participles here do what English does with "while": राजा वनम् गच्छन्
is "the king, as he went to the forest". None of them is the sentence's
main verb, and none needs a conjunction.

Then three gerundives state obligation without any verb at all —
कर्तव्यम्, करणीयम्, स्मरणीयम्. Two different affixes, तव्य and अनीयर्,
with no difference in sense; a writer picks whichever fits the line.
किम् मया करणीयम् is the whole question: what, by me, is to-be-done.

readings.sentence: कस्मिंश्चित् देशे धनवान् राजा आसीत्। तस्य पिता वृद्धः दरिद्रः च अभवत्। राजा पितरम् न अपश्यत्, न च तम् अस्मरत्। एकदा भगवान् मुनिः सभाम् आगच्छत्। सः राजानम् अवदत् — पितरि भक्तिः एव धर्मः। यः पितरम् त्यजति सः राज्ञः नाम न अर्हति। तत् श्रुत्वा राज्ञा शिरः अवनतम्। ततः सः पितुः गृहम् अगच्छत्, तस्य पादौ च अस्पृशत्।
readings.translation: In a certain country there was a wealthy king. His father had become old and poor. The king did not look at his father, nor did he remember him. One day the Blessed One, a sage, came to the assembly. He said to the king — "Devotion toward one's father is dharma itself. He who abandons his father does not deserve the name of king." Having heard that, the king's head was bowed. Then he went to his father's house, and touched his feet.
readings.teaches:
a king who forgets his father. पितृ appears in four cases across the
story — पिता, पितरम्, पितरि, पितुः.

readings.vyakhya: पिता पितरम् पितरि पितुः — चतुर्षु स्थानेषु एकः जनः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
One man, four shapes: पिता when he is named, पितरम् when the king fails to
look at him, पितरि when devotion is owed toward him, पितुः when his house
is meant. Nothing about the father changes across the story.

The king does the same — राजा, राजानम्, राज्ञः, राज्ञा — and the last of
those, राज्ञा शिरः अवनतम्, has no finite verb: a participle and an
instrumental agent, which is how classical narrative most often reports
what someone did.

readings.sentence: नद्याः तीरे वणिजः वसन्ति स्म। तेषाम् गृहेषु धनम् धान्यम् च आसीत्। एकदा एकः वणिक् दूरम् देशम् गन्तुम् ऐच्छत्। मित्राणि तम् अवदन् — मार्गः दीर्घः, मा गच्छ इति। किन्तु सः अशृणोत् न। श्वः गमिष्यामि इति उक्त्वा सः रात्रौ यानम् असज्जयत्। प्रभाते तेन मित्राणि त्यक्तानि, नगरम् च त्यक्तम्।
readings.translation: On the bank of a river lived merchants. In their houses were wealth and grain. One day one merchant wished to go to a distant country. His friends said to him — "The road is long; do not go." But he did not listen. Saying "I will go tomorrow," he made ready a cart in the night. At dawn the friends were left behind by him, and the city too was left.
readings.teaches:
a merchant leaves against advice. Closes on तेन मित्राणि त्यक्तानि — two
participles and an instrumental agent, with no finite verb.

readings.vyakhya: मा गच्छ इति उक्तम्, तथापि सः अगच्छत्। तेन मित्राणि त्यक्तानि।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The last sentence has no finite verb in it. त्यक्तानि and त्यक्तम् are
participles, and they carry the whole statement — the friends left, the
city left, and तेन telling you by whom.

Classical Sanskrit prefers this to a past-tense verb, which is why so much
narrative reads as a chain of participles with the agent in the
instrumental. Once मित्राणि त्यक्तानि stops needing to be translated as a
passive, it starts reading as ordinary past narration.

readings.sentence: कस्मिंश्चित् ग्रामे एकः ब्राह्मणः वसति स्म। तस्य गृहे एकः नकुलः आसीत्। ब्राह्मणस्य पत्नी बालम् रक्षन्ती गृहे तिष्ठति स्म। एकदा सा जलम् आनेतुम् बहिः अगच्छत्। तस्मिन् काले एकः कृष्णसर्पः बालस्य समीपम् आगच्छत्। तम् दृष्ट्वा नकुलः सर्पेण सह अयुध्यत। तेन सर्पः हतः, नकुलस्य मुखम् च रक्तेन लिप्तम् आसीत्। पत्नी प्रत्यागच्छत्। रक्तानि नकुलस्य मुखे दृष्ट्वा सा अचिन्तयत् — "अनेन मम बालः खादितः" इति। क्रुद्धा सा घटम् तस्य उपरि अक्षिपत्। नकुलः अम्रियत। गृहम् प्रविश्य सा बालम् सुप्तम् अपश्यत्, हतम् सर्पम् च। तदा सा अतीव अरोदीत् — "अहम् मूढा, विचार्य न कृतवती" इति।
readings.translation: In a certain village there lived a brahmin. In his house was a mongoose. The brahmin's wife, guarding the child, used to stay at home. One day she went out to fetch water. At that time a black snake came near the child. Seeing it, the mongoose fought with the snake. By that the snake was killed, and the mongoose's mouth was smeared with blood. The wife returned. Seeing the blood on the mongoose's mouth, she thought — "My child has been eaten by this one." Enraged, she threw a pot upon him. The mongoose died. Entering the house, she saw the child asleep, and the snake killed. Then she wept bitterly — "I am a fool; I did not act after thinking."
readings.teaches:
the mongoose story, told in participles. The tragedy turns on one of them:
रक्तानि दृष्ट्वा, seeing the blood, and what the wife concludes from it.

readings.vyakhya: रक्तानि दृष्ट्वा सा अमन्यत। दर्शनम् सत्यम्, अनुमानम् मिथ्या।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Everything the wife sees is true. There is blood on the mongoose's mouth.
What she adds is the inference, and the story hangs the whole tragedy on
the gap between them — रक्तानि दृष्ट्वा, seeing the blood, and then
खादितः, "he has been eaten", which she never saw at all.

The participles carry it. हतः, लिप्तम्, सुप्तम्, हतम् are all states
someone else could have verified; खादितः is the one she supplied. And the
last word answers it: कृतवती, the active past participle — not something
done to her, but the thing she did.

readings.sentence: शशकः सिंहम् एकम् कूपम् अनयत्। "अत्र सः शत्रुः वसति" इति सः अवदत्। सिंहः कूपम् अपश्यत्। जले तस्य एव प्रतिबिम्बम् आसीत्, किन्तु सः तत् अन्यम् सिंहम् अमन्यत। क्रुद्धः सः गर्जितुम् आरभत। कूपात् प्रतिशब्दः श्रूयते स्म। तेन सः अतीव अक्रुध्यत्। "अहम् एनम् हनिष्यामि" इति उक्त्वा सः कूपे अपतत्। तत्र मग्नः सिंहः अम्रियत। एवम् बुद्ध्या शशकः सर्वान् मृगान् अरक्षत्। बलम् बुद्धिः च — तयोः बुद्धिः एव श्रेष्ठा।
readings.translation: The rabbit led the lion to a well. "Your enemy lives here," he said. The lion looked into the well. In the water was his own reflection, but he took it for another lion. Enraged, he began to roar. An echo was heard from the well. At that he grew still angrier. Saying "I will kill him," he leapt into the well. Sunk there, the lion died. Thus by his wit the rabbit saved all the beasts. Strength and intelligence — of the two, intelligence is the better.
readings.teaches:
the close of the सिंह-शशक story. Eight past verbs against one future —
हनिष्यामि, the thing the lion intends and does not accomplish.

readings.vyakhya: बलवान् सिंहः मृतः, बुद्धिमान् शशकः जीवति। न बलेन, बुद्ध्या जयः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The lion never sees another lion. He sees himself and cannot tell, and the
echo he answers is his own voice returning. The story spends its whole
length on that one joke, and the last line names it: बलम् बुद्धिः च, and
of the two, बुद्धिः.

Nine finite verbs here and eight of them are past — अनयत्, अपश्यत्,
अमन्यत, अक्रुध्यत्, अपतत्, अम्रियत, अरक्षत्, आसीत्. Against them stand
वसति and श्रूयते inside quoted or reported speech, where the present holds,
and हनिष्यामि, the only future in the passage: the one thing the lion
intends and does not accomplish.

readings.vyakhya_en: Your first connected story — and almost every form is grammar you already hold: a locative setting (गोकुले), genitive plurals (गोपानाम्), the सः/तस्य/तं pronoun, present verbs singular and plural. Nothing new to learn — that is the point. Meet the cast: कृष्णः the boy, यशोदा his mother, the गोपाः (cowherds) and गोप्यः (gopīs). They return in every episode, so their forms grow familiar. From here the sentences lengthen.

The same four types, now inside the Gokula story rather than beside it.
गोपपुत्रः is a तत्पुरुष, उपगोकुलम् an अव्ययीभाव, गोपकृष्णौ a द्वन्द्व

readings.sentence: कन्या वने तिष्ठति। सा लताम् पश्यति, मालाम् च रचयति। गङ्गायाम् जलम् अस्ति। कन्या तत्र स्नाति, देवीम् च नमति। सेना अपि आगच्छति, किन्तु कन्या न बिभेति।
readings.translation: A girl stands in the forest. She sees a creeper, and makes a garland. In the Ganges there is water. The girl bathes there, and bows to the goddess. An army comes too, but the girl is not afraid.
readings.teaches:
कन्या, लता, माला, देवी — new words, all in endings already met: सेना's आ
in the nominative, सभाम्'s द्वितीया, सभायाम्'s सप्तमी.

readings.vyakhya: कन्या लता माला देवी — नूतनानि पदानि, प्रसिद्धेषु प्रत्ययेषु। सेनायाः इव आकारः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Four new words here, and not one new ending. कन्या, लता, माला all close in
the same आ that सेना carries; लताम् and मालाम् take the accusative म् of
सभाम्; गङ्गायाम् takes the locative याम् of सभायाम्. देवी follows नदी. The
words are new, the grammar is not — that is the whole reason they can arrive
together, without a sentence apiece.

readings.vyakhya_en: Now a whole scene, not a single fact. Sentences link by connectives — किन्तु ("but," turning Yaśodā's guarding into Kṛṣṇa's wanting), ततः ("then"), च ("and") — so the action flows. The new pieces are small and natural: adverbs (शनैः "quietly," उच्चैः "high up," स्वयम् "himself") and a chain of present verbs (इच्छति, प्रविशति, चोरयति, यच्छति, खादति). The case-roles are all known — नवनीतम् the object, मित्रेभ्यः the dative of recipient. You are reading a story now.

readings.vyakhya: कथा दीर्घतरा। क्रुद्धा बद्धः इति निष्ठे, बन्धितुम् इति तुमुन्, रज्ज्वा प्रेम्णा इति करणे। अन्ते नामनिर्वचनम् — दाम उदरे यस्य सः दामोदरः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The longest reading yet, weaving together what you met as isolated cells: past participles as adjective and predicate (क्रुद्धा "angry," बद्धः "bound"), an infinitive with "can" (बन्धितुम् न शक्नोति "cannot bind"), and the instrumental of means twice (रज्ज्वा "with a rope," प्रेम्णा "by love"). It closes the way Sanskrit tales love to — a name-etymology: दाम (rope) + उदर (belly) makes the बहुव्रीहि दामोदर, "the one with a rope at his belly." The grammar is familiar; the story now carries it.

readings.translation: The demoness Pūtanā comes to Gokula and stands there in the form of a child (i.e. a woman). She wishes to kill Kṛṣṇa by nursing him with poison. But by Kṛṣṇa the breast was suckled, and the poison too was drunk. Thus Pūtanā was slain by Kṛṣṇa.

readings.vyakhya: कर्मणिप्रयोगः — इह कर्ता तृतीयायां, कर्म प्रथमायाम्। कृष्णेन पूतना हता इति न कर्तरि, कर्मणि। दोषाः — आगत्य स्तनयित्वा इति पूर्वकालकृदन्ते।
readings.vyakhya_en: The grammar turn: for the first time the story is told in the **passive** (कर्मणि). In active voice Kṛṣṇa is the subject (कर्तृ) and takes the nominative; in passive he becomes the agent (still the doer, but now marked by तृतीया — instrumental — while the object rises to nominative). The past-passive participle क्त (निष्ठा, 3.2.102) carries this sense: पीतः (was drunk, masc.), पीतम् (neuter), हता (fem.). Two gerunds (क्त्वा / ल्यप्) chain the prior actions: Pūtanā "comes, then nurses, then wishes to kill" — each gerund hands off to the next.

readings.vyakhya: इह कालभेदः स्पष्टः — बालाः अवदन्, यशोदा पप्रच्छ, कृष्णः उवाच इति लिट् परोक्षे; परन्तु स्मृत्या न परोक्षं — नाटकीयतया लिट् उचितः। लङ् तु अनद्यतने — अभक्षयत्, अखादः, अखादम्, अपश्यत् इति। लोट् विवृणुष्व इति विधौ।
readings.vyakhya_en: Two tenses meet in this reading. **लिट् perfect** (परोक्षे लिट्, 3.2.115) appears where the narrator stands at a remove — पप्रच्छ "she asked," उवाच "he said" — verbs of reported or narrated speech. **लङ्** (अनद्यतन, 3.2.111) marks the events directly recalled: the eating (अभक्षयत्), Kṛṣṇa's denial (न अखादम्), and Yaśodā's vision (अपश्यत्). One **लोट् imperative** (3.3.162) lives inside the quoted command — विवृणुष्व "open (your mouth)!" The vision that follows — sky, earth, gods, stars — is the whole universe listed in a single accusative string, with one past-active participle (दृष्टवती, क्तवतु fem.) as the main predicate: "she who saw."

readings.vyakhya: एकस्मिन्नेव आख्याने णिच्, तृच्, त्व, मतुप्, क्त्वा — चत्वारः शब्दप्रकाराः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Four ways of building a word, in one short scene. आनाययत् is a **causative**:
नी "lead" plus णिच् becomes आनाय् "cause to bring," and the one who would have
been the agent — दूतम् — drops to the accusative (1.4.52), because the king is
now the one causing. दाता is an **agent-noun**, दा "give" plus तृच्, "the
giver." शूरत्वम् is an **abstract**, शूर "brave" plus त्व, "bravery" — a quality
named as a thing. धनवान् is a **possessive**, धन plus मतुप्, "wealth-having."
And श्रुत्वा is a **gerund**: श्रु plus क्त्वा, indeclinable, "having heard."
The nouns around them — दूतम्, धनम्, ब्राह्मणेभ्यः, गर्वम् — sit in cases the
reader has long since met; only the five built words are new.

readings.sentence: कालियो नाम महासर्पः कालिन्दीनद्यां वसति स्म। तस्य विषेण जलं दूषितम् आसीत्। गावः पिबन्त्यः तत् जलम् पीत्वा मूर्च्छिताः अभवन्। तदा कृष्णः तरुम् आरुह्य नद्यां अपतत्। सः सर्पस्य फणेषु नृत्यन् तम् अदमयत्। एवम् कालियः कृष्णेन पराजितः।
readings.translation: A great serpent named Kāliya lived in the Yamunā river. By his poison the water was polluted. The cows, while drinking, drank that water and fainted. Then Kṛṣṇa climbed a tree and fell into the river. He danced on the serpent's hoods and subdued it. Thus Kāliya was defeated by Kṛṣṇa.

readings.vyakhya: द्वे नवीने — शतृप्रत्ययः (लटः शतृशानचौ) पिबन्त्यः नृत्यन् च; स्म-सहितः लट् भूतार्थे। कर्मणिप्रयोगः त्रिवारम् — दूषितम् आसीत्, मूर्च्छिताः अभवन्, पराजितः। जलचरे युद्धम् वर्णयितुम् क्त्वा-ल्यपौ बहुशः।
readings.vyakhya_en: Two new tools. First, **शतृ** (the active present participle — लटः शतृशानचौ, 3.2.124): पिबन्त्यः "while drinking" (fem. pl., simultaneous with अभवन्) and नृत्यन् "while dancing" (masc. sg., simultaneous with अदमयत्). The participle says the background action runs alongside the main verb — not before it (that's क्त्वा) and not after it. Second, **वसति स्म** — a present-tense verb with the particle स्म shifts into past habitual: "used to dwell." Passive क्त appears three times (दूषितम्, मूर्च्छिताः, पराजितः), anchoring the pattern from ex098. The gerunds आरुह्य → अपतत् chain the action sequence into one breath.

readings.sentence: एकदा व्रजवासिनः इन्द्राय पूजाम् अकुर्वन्। कृष्णः अवदत् — "गोवर्धनाय पूजाम् कुरुत, न तु इन्द्राय।" जनाः तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा तथा अकुर्वन्। तदा क्रुद्धः इन्द्रः मेघैः वर्षम् अप्रेरयत्। वर्षेण भयभीताः गावः च गोपाः च कृष्णम् अशरणम् अगच्छन्। कृष्णः तु गोवर्धनम् एव एकेन हस्तेन उद्धृत्य सप्त दिवसान् अधारयत्। एवम् गोवर्धनः कृष्णेन छत्रम् इव धृतः।
readings.translation: Once the inhabitants of Vraja were performing a puja for Indra. Kṛṣṇa said — "Offer puja to Govardhana, not to Indra." The people, having heard his words, did so. Then angry Indra sent rain-clouds. Frightened by the rain, the cows and cowherds went to Kṛṣṇa as their refuge. But Kṛṣṇa alone, lifting Govardhana with one hand, held it for seven days. Thus Govardhana was held by Kṛṣṇa like an umbrella.
readings.teaches: anīyar gerundive (implicitly: "the mountain is to-be-held"); upasarga + gerund उद्धृत्य; instrumental of cause (वर्षेण); accusative of duration (सप्त दिवसान्); simile (उपमा with इव); passive close (धृतः)

readings.vyakhya: सर्वाधिकदीर्घा कथा — एका वाक्यपरम्परा। नवीनम् — उपमा (इव); अत्यन्तसंयोगे द्वितीया (सप्त दिवसान्); एकेन हस्तेन इति करणम्; क्रुद्धः इन्द्रः इति निष्ठाविशेषणम्। लोट् कुरुत इति विधौ; लङ् बहुशः कथावर्णने।
readings.vyakhya_en: The longest katha reading, and it earns its length: five separate clauses, each moving the story. New arrivals: **इव** (the simile particle — Govardhana held "like an umbrella," छत्रम् इव); **accusative of duration** — सप्त दिवसान् "for seven days" (अत्यन्तसंयोगे द्वितीया, 2.3.5); the **instrumental of instrument with body-part** — एकेन हस्तेन "with one hand" (2.3.18); and the **dual coordinator** गावः च गोपाः च "both cows and cowherds." The closing passive (धृतः, 3.2.102) rounds the arc: episodes ex098–ex101 all end with a कर्मणि क्त — "was killed," "she saw," "was defeated," "was held" — each one a summary judgment on what just happened.

readings.sentence: कंसः नाम क्रूरः राजा कृष्णस्य मातुलः आसीत्। सः अचिन्तयत् — "अयम् बालः मया हन्तव्यः, अन्यथा सः माम् हनिष्यति।" तस्मात् सः अक्रूरम् गोकुलम् प्रैषयत्। अक्रूरः रथेन गत्वा कृष्णम् अवदत् — "मथुराम् आगच्छ, यतः तव दर्शनम् सर्वे इच्छन्ति।"
readings.translation: A cruel king named Kaṃsa was Kṛṣṇa's maternal uncle. He thought — "This boy must be killed by me, otherwise he will kill me." Therefore he sent Akrūra to Gokula. Akrūra, having gone by chariot, said to Kṛṣṇa — "Come to Mathurā, for everyone desires the sight of you."
readings.teaches: gerundive (अनीयर्/तव्य — हन्तव्यः "to-be-killed," with instrumental agent मया); future लृट् (हनिष्यति, इच्छन्ति present); causative प्रैषयत्; relative यतः-clause (reason); सम्बन्ध-षष्ठी (कृष्णस्य मातुलः, तव दर्शनम्)

readings.vyakhya: महत् नवीनम् — कृत्यप्रत्ययः। हन्तव्यः इति तव्य (तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः), अर्थे "अवश्यं हननीयः"। कृत्ये कर्ता तृतीयायाम् (मया), कर्म प्रथमायाम् (बालः) — कर्मणिवत्। लृट् हनिष्यति इति भविष्यति; यतः इति हेतौ।
readings.vyakhya_en: The big new arrival: the **gerundive** (कृत्य) — हन्तव्यः "(he) who must be killed," तव्य of √हन् (तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः, 3.1.96). It expresses necessity/obligation, and it governs case exactly like the passive: the agent goes to **instrumental** (मया "by me") and the patient to **nominative** (बालः). So "the boy is-to-be-killed by me" reads with मया … बालः … हन्तव्यः all in agreement. Against it stands the plain **future** हनिष्यति "he will kill" (लृट्, 3.3.13) — Kaṃsa weighs necessity against consequence. The reason-clause opens with यतः "because." This is the grammatical hinge from playful Gokula into the Mathurā confrontation.

source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.vyakhya: एकस्मिन्नाख्याने तरप्, कर्मधारयः, यक्, तसिल्, इष्ठन् — पञ्च शब्दप्रकाराः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Degrees and a passive, in one scene. पटुः is the plain grade; पटुतरः the
**comparative** — पटु + तर, "cleverer of the two"; श्रेष्ठ the **superlative**,
the इष्ठन्-grade of प्रशस्य, "best of all." महाबुद्धिः is a **compound** —
महती बुद्धिः यस्य, "he whose mind is great." अश्रूयत is a **passive**: the यक्
stem turns श्रु into "is heard," so तत् (the question) becomes the प्रथमा and
सर्वैः (all who hear) the तृतीया — the object rises to subject, the agent
steps back. And ततः is a **तसिल् adverb**, तद् + तस्, "from that → thereupon."

readings.vyakhya: अधिकरणं त्रिविधम् इह — सति-सप्तमी (कृष्णे गच्छति सति) कालार्थे; रथे हृदये इति देशाधिकरणे। याः…ताः इति वाक्यद्वये सम्बन्धः। रुदतीः इति शतृ कर्मणि (ताः रुदतीः)। दृष्ट्वा अपि इति अनुमत्यर्थे — "दृष्ट्वापि न न्यवर्तत"।
readings.vyakhya_en: Three locatives, three jobs. The **locative absolute** (सति-सप्तमी, 2.3.37) sets the scene in time — कृष्णे गच्छति सति "Kṛṣṇa being-in-the-act-of-going," i.e. "as Kṛṣṇa was leaving": a whole subordinate clause folded into two locative words. Ordinary locatives of place follow — रथे "in the chariot," हृदये "in the heart" (2.3.36). The relative-correlative याः … ताः now spans a full clause ("those gopīs who used to look on him — they all sank in grief"). And the शतृ participle appears for the first time **as an accusative object** — ताः रुदतीः "them, the weeping ones." दृष्ट्वा अपि "even having seen" gives the concessive: he saw, yet did not turn.

readings.sentence: यः कंसः चिरम् कृष्णस्य वधम् इच्छति स्म, सः एव अधुना भयेन कम्पते। कृष्णः मथुराम् प्रविश्य रङ्गभूमौ मल्लान् अहन्। ततः सः उच्चासनात् कंसम् आकृष्य भूमौ अपातयत्। यम् राजानम् सर्वे जनाः अबिभयुः, सः कृष्णेन क्षणेन एव हतः। एवम् अधर्मस्य अन्तः, धर्मस्य च जयः अभवत्।
readings.translation: He who for long had wished for Kṛṣṇa's death — that very one now trembles with fear. Kṛṣṇa, having entered Mathurā, killed the wrestlers in the arena. Then he dragged Kaṃsa down from his high throne and threw him to the ground. The king whom all people had feared — he was killed by Kṛṣṇa in but a moment. Thus came the end of unrighteousness, and the victory of dharma.
readings.teaches: climax — two relative-correlatives (यः…सः on the subject, यम्…सः on the object); अपादान (भयस्य source → उच्चासनात् ablative, अबिभयुः with 5th); causative अपातयत्; षष्ठी of object with कृत् (कृष्णस्य वधम्, 2.3.65); passive close (हतः)

readings.vyakhya: कथायाः शिखरम् — द्वौ सम्बन्धौ यद्-तद्। कर्तरि यः…सः (यः इच्छति स्म सः कम्पते); कर्मणि यम्…सः (यं अबिभयुः सः हतः)। अपादानम् द्विधा — उच्चासनात् (departure), भयस्य हेतुः भी-धातुना अबिभयुः। वधम् इति कृत्, तत्र कर्म षष्ठ्याम् (कृष्णस्य वधम्)। अन्ते कर्मणि हतः — कथार्धम् सर्वम् कर्मणि समाप्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en: The climax, and it gathers everything. Two relative-correlatives frame it, one on each axis: यः … सः on the **subject** ("he who long wished Kṛṣṇa's death — that one now trembles") and यम् … सः on the **object** ("the king whom all feared — he was killed"). Two ablatives of separation: उच्चासनात् "from the high throne" (2.3.28) and the fear-source folded into अबिभयुः. The action-noun वधम् "killing" takes its object in the **genitive** — कृष्णस्य वधम् "the killing OF Kṛṣṇa" (2.3.65, the कृत्-षष्ठी). The arc that began with butter and a rope ends as it must, in the passive: हतः "was killed" — and the whole Kṛṣṇa-childhood sequence closes on its grammatical signature, the कर्मणि क्त, now carrying the weight of a death rather than a game.

readings.translation: In a certain forest there lived a lion named Bhāsuraka. He was strong, but exceedingly cruel. Every day he killed many animals. Because of this all the beasts trembled with fear. They, having gathered, said to the lion — "O master, do not kill all the animals. We ourselves will send one animal every day for your food."

readings.vyakhya: नूतनकथारम्भः — पञ्चतन्त्रात्। कस्मिंश्चित् वने इति लोकप्रसिद्धम् आख्यानारम्भपदम्। मा हन् इति प्रतिषेधे लुङ् अनद्यतनः अनागमकः। आहाराय इति तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी; प्रेषयिष्यामः इति लृट् उत्तमपुरुषबहुवचने।
readings.vyakhya_en: A new story begins — from the Pañcatantra, and it opens with the formula every Sanskrit tale is built on: कस्मिंश्चित् वने "in a certain forest" (कः + चित् = the indefinite "some"). One genuinely new construction: the **prohibitive** — मा with an augmentless past (मा … हन् "do not kill"), the standard way Sanskrit says "don't." Against it stands the animals' **future promise** — प्रेषयिष्यामः "we will send" (लृट्, 1st plural). The dative आहाराय "for food" is the dative of purpose (तादर्थ्य). All the rest — past tenses, gerund मिलित्वा, instrumental of cause भयेन — is grammar you already own, now carrying a fable instead of a god.

readings.sentence: एकदा शशकस्य वारः आगच्छत्। सः बुद्धिमान् शशकः चिरम् विचिन्त्य एकम् उपायम् अकरोत्। सः मन्दम् मन्दम् सिंहस्य समीपम् अगच्छत्। क्रुद्धः सिंहः अपृच्छत् — "किमर्थम् त्वम् विलम्बेन आगतः?" शशकः अवदत् — "मार्गे अन्यः बलवान् सिंहः माम् अरुणत्। सः त्वाम् एव स्वामिनम् न मन्यते।" तत् श्रुत्वा क्रुद्धः सिंहः तम् द्रष्टुम् इच्छति स्म।
readings.translation: One day the rabbit's turn came. That clever rabbit, after thinking for a long time, devised a plan. He went very slowly toward the lion. The angry lion asked — "Why have you come late?" The rabbit said — "On the road another strong lion stopped me. He does not regard you alone as master." Having heard that, the angry lion wished to see him.
readings.teaches: longer dialogue — किमर्थम् (why?), past participle as predicate (आगतः "have come"), gerund विचिन्त्य + श्रुत्वा, accusative of person stopped (माम् अरुणत्), infinitive of purpose (द्रष्टुम्), मन्यते आत्मनेपद

readings.vyakhya: संवादः दीर्घतरः। किमर्थम् इति हेतुप्रश्ने; आगतः इति निष्ठा कर्तरि ("त्वम् आगतः")। माम् अरुणत् इति रुध्-धातोः सप्तमगणे लङ्। स्वामिनम् इति द्विकर्मके मन्यतेः अभिन्ननिर्देशे। द्रष्टुम् इच्छति इति तुमुन् इष्-धातुना।
readings.vyakhya_en: The dialogue lengthens — the trick is told, not just narrated. New touches: किमर्थम् "why? for what purpose?" (the interrogative of cause); the past participle as a finite-like **predicate** — त्वम् … आगतः "you have come" (क्त standing in for "you came/are come"); and a double-accusative with मन्यते — त्वाम् स्वामिनम् न मन्यते "does not regard you AS master," the object and its predicate-complement both accusative. The infinitive द्रष्टुम् इच्छति "wishes to see" closes on the hook that will spring the trap. Everything else is consolidation: four लङ् pasts, two gerunds (विचिन्त्य, श्रुत्वा), locatives, the मतुप् adjectives बलवान्/बुद्धिमान्.

readings.vyakhya: दा-धातोः तृच्प्रत्यये दातृशब्दः सिध्यति, प्रथमैकवचने दाता इति रूपम्। यो ददाति स दाता।
readings.vyakhya_en: By 3.1.133 (ण्वुल्तृचौ) every root may take तृच् (the affix तृ) to name its agent. On दा "give" this yields the stem दातृ, whose nominative singular is दाता "giver". The agent-noun simply names the one who performs the verb's action — here, the one who gives.

readings.vyakhya_en: By 3.2.135 (तृन्) the affix तृन् (तृ) comes after a root to name one who does the action habitually or by disposition (शील). On कृ "do" it gives the stem कर्तृ, nominative singular कर्ता. Unlike a plain agent, this names a characteristic doer — one whose nature it is to act.

readings.vyakhya: ताच्छील्ये गम्यमाने उपपदे सति गम्-धातोः णिनिप्रत्यये गामिन्शब्दः, प्रथमैकवचने गामी। यः शीलेन ग्रामं गच्छति स ग्रामं गामी।
readings.vyakhya_en: By 3.2.78 (सुप्यजातौ णिनिस्ताच्छील्ये) the affix णिनि (इन्) attaches to a root when habit (ताच्छील्य) is meant and an उपपद — a noun in composition — stands with it. With उपपद ग्रामम् and root गम् "go", this yields the stem गामिन्, nominative singular गामी. The whole phrase ग्रामं गामी names one who customarily goes to the village.

readings.vyakhya: अचो यत् इति वचनात् अजन्तात् धातोः दा इत्यस्मात् यत्प्रत्ययः। देयम् इति कृत्यम्। कर्म प्रथमायां, कर्ता तृतीयायाम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: By अचो यत् (3.1.97) a root ending in a vowel takes the कृत्य affix यत्; so दा becomes देयम्, "to be given." Like every gerundive it governs case exactly as the passive does: the patient (धनम्) stands in the nominative, and an agent, if expressed, would stand in the instrumental. Here the recipient ब्राह्मणाय is in the dative (सम्प्रदान).

readings.translation: The task is to be done by me.
readings.teaches: ण्यत् forms a कृत्य gerundive on ऋ-final / consonant-final roots (कृ → कार्यम्).

readings.vyakhya_en: By ऋहलोर्ण्यत् (3.1.124) a root ending in ऋ (short or long) or in a consonant takes the कृत्य affix ण्यत्; so कृ becomes कार्यम्, "to be done, a task." The construction mirrors the passive: the agent मया is in the instrumental (तृतीया, by 2.3.18) and the patient stands in the nominative.

notes.role: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः → अनीयर् variant → पठ् → पठनीयः (gerundive)

notes.en: agrees with the patient in the nominative, as in the passive

readings.vyakhya: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः इति धातोः अनीयर्प्रत्ययः। पठ् इत्यस्मात् पठनीयम्। कर्ता शिष्येण तृतीयायां, कर्म प्रथमायाम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: By तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः (3.1.96) a root may take तव्यत्, तव्य, or अनीयर्; here the अनीयर् variant gives पठ् → पठनीयः, "to be read." As with all कृत्य gerundives the syntax is passive-like: the agent शिष्येण stands in the instrumental (तृतीया, 2.3.18) and the patient पाठः in the nominative.

readings.translation: The potter makes a pot.
readings.teaches: अण् (कर्मण्यण्) forms an agent-noun whose object stands as उपपद in one compound.

notes.en: the object कुम्भ stands in composition with the agent-noun

notes.role: कर्मण्यण् → कुम्भ + कृ + अण् → कुम्भकारः

words.gloss: "pot" — a clay pot (object of the verb)

quiz.q: Which form is घट · द्वितीया · एकवचन?

readings.vyakhya: कुम्भं करोतीति कुम्भकारः। कर्मणि उपपदे कृधातोः अण्प्रत्ययः। उपपदं कर्म च समस्यते एकपदे।
readings.vyakhya_en: When an object (कर्मन्) stands as उपपद beside a root, the root takes अण् to form an agent-noun. Here कुम्भ "pot" joins कृ "make" and the affix अण् gives कुम्भकारः "pot-maker." The object does not stay a separate accusative word; it merges into a single तत्पुरुष compound with the agent-noun.

readings.translation: The cow-giver gives a cow to the brahmin.
readings.teaches: क (आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः) suffixes an आ-final root with an object-उपपद and no उपसर्ग.

notes.en: the object गो stands in composition with the agent-noun

notes.role: आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः → गो + दा + क → गोदः (आ-final दा, no उपसर्ग)

notes.en: dative — the one to whom the gift is given

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → ब्राह्मणाय

quiz.q: Which form is ब्राह्मण · चतुर्थी · एकवचन?
Which form is गो · द्वितीया · एकवचन?

readings.vyakhya: गां ददातीति गोदः। आकारान्तात् दाधातोः अनुपसर्गात् कर्मण्युपपदे कप्रत्ययः। एवं धनदः जलदश्च।
readings.vyakhya_en: A root ending in long आ, with no उपसर्ग before it and an object standing as उपपद, takes क instead of अण्. Thus गो "cow" + दा "give" + क yields गोदः "cow-giver." The same pattern gives धनदः "wealth-giver" and जलदः "water-giver" (the cloud). The object गो merges with the agent-noun into one तत्पुरुष compound.

readings.translation: The delighting son gladdens his mother.
readings.teaches: ल्यु (→ अन) forms an agent-noun from नन्दि-group roots.

notes.role: नन्दिग्रहिपचादिभ्यो ल्युणिन्यचः → नन्द् + ल्यु (अन) → नन्दनः

notes.en: agent-noun in अन from the नन्दि-group

quiz.q: Which form is मातृ · द्वितीया · एकवचन?

readings.vyakhya: नन्दतीति नन्दनः। नन्दिग्रहिपचादिगणे नन्दिधातोः ल्युप्रत्ययः, यस्य अनादेशः।
readings.vyakhya_en: Roots of the नन्दि-group take ल्यु, and ल्यु is replaced by अन, giving agent-nouns like नन्दनः "the delighting one, the son." Unlike अण् and क above, this ल्यु-formation needs no उपपद object to attach; the affix alone names the doer. The same rule routes ग्रहि-roots to णिनि and पच्-group roots to अच्.

chapters.title: संज्ञा व परिभाषा — the grammar's own technical terms & meta-rules

readings.translation: ā, ai, au — these bear the name "vṛddhi."
readings.teaches: the संज्ञा वृद्धि — Pāṇini's name for the strongest vowel grade (आ ऐ औ); the term every "vṛddhi" rule invokes

notes.en: a technical term DEFINED here, used everywhere after

notes.role: वृद्धिरादैच् — आत् (आ) and ऐच् (ऐ, औ) are named वृद्धि

words.gloss: ā and the ऐच् pair (ऐ, औ)

notes.text: आत् = आ; ऐच् = the प्रत्याहार for ऐ, औ — together the वृद्धि vowels

readings.vyakhya: आ ऐ औ इति वृद्धिसंज्ञकाः। एषा संज्ञा "आदिवृद्धिः" "वृद्धिरेचि" इत्यादिषु प्रयुज्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en: Before any rule can SAY "take vṛddhi," the term must be DEFINED — and 1.1.1, the very first sūtra of the Aṣṭādhyāyī, does it: वृद्धिः = आ, ऐ, औ, the strongest vowel grade. You have already SEEN वृद्धि act — दशरथ → दाशरथिः (आदिवृद्धि, ex080), तव + एव → तवैव (ex with वृद्धि-sandhi). Now you know its name. This is metalanguage: a संज्ञा is a label the grammar pins on a set of sounds so later rules can refer to them in one word.

readings.translation: a, e, o — these bear the name "guṇa."
readings.teaches: the संज्ञा गुण — the middle vowel grade (अ ए ओ); the term behind every गुण operation (अग्नये, नयति)

notes.role: अदेङ् गुणः — अत् (अ) and एङ् (ए, ओ) are named गुण

words.gloss: the इक् vowels (इ उ ऋ ऌ) — what guṇa/vṛddhi apply TO

notes.text: इको गुणवृद्धी (1.1.3): गुण/वृद्धि, when ordered without specifics, fall on the इक् vowels

notes.role: इको गुणवृद्धी — गुण and वृद्धि operate on इक् (इ उ ऋ ऌ)

readings.vyakhya: अ ए ओ इति गुणसंज्ञकाः; इको गुणवृद्धी इति इकां गुणवृद्धी भवतः। नी → ने (नयति), अग्नि → अग्नये।
readings.vyakhya_en: गुण, the MIDDLE grade, is named in 1.1.2: अ, ए, ओ. And 1.1.3 (इको गुणवृद्धी) says where it lands — on the इक् vowels (इ, उ, ऋ, ऌ): इ→ए, उ→ओ, ऋ→अर्. You have watched this everywhere — अग्नि → अग्नये (इ→ए, ex029), गुरु → गुरवे (उ→ओ, ex048), पितृ → पितरम् (ऋ→अर्, ex044). गुण and वृद्धि are the two strengthenings; इक् is what they strengthen. Three sūtras (1.1.1–3) underwrite half the sandhi and declension you have done.

readings.translation: Sounds made at the same place with the same effort are "savarṇa" (homorganic).
readings.teaches: the संज्ञा सवर्ण — same-place-and-effort sounds; the term behind सवर्णदीर्घ (अ+अ→आ)

notes.role: तुल्यास्यप्रयत्नं सवर्णम् — same आस्य (place) + प्रयत्न (effort) → सवर्ण

notes.text: आस्य = the mouth-position (कण्ठ, तालु…); प्रयत्न = the manner/effort

readings.vyakhya: समानस्थानप्रयत्नौ वर्णौ सवर्णौ। अ इ-वर्गादीनां स्वस्ववर्गे सावर्ण्यम्। अतः अ + अ → आ (सवर्णदीर्घः)।
readings.vyakhya_en: Why does अ + अ fuse to आ but अ + इ to ए? Because the first pair is सवर्ण — "homorganic," made at the same place with the same effort (1.1.9) — and the second is not. This संज्ञा is the hinge of सवर्णदीर्घ (दधि + इन्द्रः → दधीन्द्रः, ex with 6.1.101): two सवर्ण vowels lengthen into one. The term sorts every sound into क-class, च-class, and so on — the grid behind both sandhi and the सवर्ण-exclusions in declension.

readings.sentence: उपदेशे हल् अन्त्यम् इत्, तस्य लोपः।
readings.translation: A consonant at the end of an affix-citation is an "it"-marker — and it drops.
readings.teaches: the इत् mechanism — affixes carry silent marker-letters that trigger rules, then vanish (क्विप्, तृच्, ण्वुल् are all named by their इत्s)

notes.role: हलन्त्यम् — a final consonant in an उपदेश (citation form) is इत्
उपदेशेऽजनुनासिक इत् — a nasalised vowel in citation is also इत्
तस्य लोपः — that इत् is then dropped, leaving only its effect

readings.vyakhya: उपदेशे अन्त्यो हल् इत्संज्ञकः, स च लुप्यते; कार्यं तु करोति। यथा तृच् → तृ (च् इत्); क्विप् → शून्यम् (सर्वे इतः)।
readings.vyakhya_en: Affixes are cited with extra letters that never appear in the final word — they are इत्, silent markers (1.3.3 for a final consonant, 1.3.2 for a nasal vowel) that DROP by तस्य लोपः (1.3.9), having done their job of triggering rules. तृच् is really just तृ — the च् is an इत् (it conditions accent/operations). क्विप् is ALL इत् — every letter vanishes, which is why it leaves the bare root (ex161, भूः). Decoding इत्-markers is how you read Pāṇini's affix-names: शतृ = अत्, ल्युट् = अन, घञ् = अ.

readings.translation: A genitive (in a rule) means "in the place of"; and the substitute is the one nearest (to the original).
readings.teaches: the two परिभाषाs that drive every substitution (आदेश) — what the षष्ठी means in a rule, and how to pick the replacement

words.gloss: "in-the-place-of" — how a rule's genitive is read

notes.role: षष्ठी स्थानेयोगा — a षष्ठी in a sūtra means "in the place of X" (X is replaced)
स्थानेऽन्तरतमः — among possible substitutes, the one closest to the original is chosen

readings.vyakhya: सूत्रस्थषष्ठी स्थानिनं सूचयति (तस्य स्थाने आदेशः); बहुषु आदेशेषु अन्तरतमः ग्राह्यः। एताभ्यां सर्वः आदेशविधिः प्रवर्तते।
readings.vyakhya_en: These two are not about Sanskrit words — they are about reading the GRAMMAR. 1.1.49: when a rule puts a word in the genitive (इकः, अचः…), it means "IN THE PLACE OF that" — a substitution. 1.1.50: when several substitutes are possible, take the अन्तरतम, the one nearest in place/effort to the original. Together they govern every आदेश you have met — why ऋ becomes अर् (the nearest गुण) and not something else, why इ + vowel goes to य् (the nearest semivowel, यण्). The परिभाषाs are the operating system under the rules.

readings.translation: A form ending in a सुप् (noun-ending) or तिङ् (verb-ending) is a "pada" (word).
readings.teaches: the संज्ञा पद — what counts as a finished word, which decides where पद-level sandhi and the final-consonant rules apply

notes.role: सुप्तिङन्तं पदम् — what ends in सुप् or तिङ् is a पद

words.gloss: ending in a सुप् or a तिङ्

notes.text: सुप् = the 21 noun-endings (4.1.2); तिङ् = the 18 verb-endings (3.4.78)

notes.en: "that which has सुप्/तिङ् at its end"

readings.vyakhya: यत् सुबन्तं तिङन्तं वा तत् पदम्। पदान्ते एव जश्त्वादीनि, पदयोः सन्धिः च प्रवर्तते। नरः, गच्छति — पदे।
readings.vyakhya_en: Many rules say "at the end of a पद" or "between पदs" — so the term must be fixed: a पद is anything ending in a noun-ending (सुप्) or a verb-ending (तिङ्), by 1.4.14. नरः (सुबन्त) and गच्छति (तिङन्त) are both पदs; a bare stem नर or root गम् is not. This संज्ञा gates the whole final-tail of the grammar — जश्त्व (वाक्→वाग्), न-lopa (राजन्→राजा), म्→anusvāra all fire at पद-end, and external sandhi happens between पदs. The word-boundary is itself a defined object.

chapters.title: सङ्ग्रह — consolidation passages: everything met, nothing new

readings.sentence: महाबलः नृपः सभाम् आगच्छत्। तस्य पार्श्वे मन्त्रिपुरोहितौ आस्ताम्। नीलाम्बरः दूतः प्रविश्य उपसभम् अतिष्ठत्। सः महाबलम् अवदत् — शत्रुसेना पराजिता, राष्ट्रम् च रक्षितम्।
readings.translation: The mighty king came to the assembly. At his side were the minister-and-priest. A blue-clad messenger, having entered, stood near the assembly. He said to the mighty one — "The enemy-army is defeated, and the kingdom protected."
readings.teaches:
the four compound types again, none of them new: महाबलः (बहुव्रीहि),
मन्त्रिपुरोहितौ (द्वन्द्व), उपसभम् (अव्ययीभाव), शत्रुसेना (तत्पुरुष).

words.gloss: the mighty one (whose strength is great)

notes.en: possessive — neither member is the head; it names the one who HAS great strength

notes.role: शेषो बहुव्रीहिः — the remaining kind of compound is बहुव्रीहि
अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — several words denoting ANOTHER thing (the possessor) form a बहुव्रीहि

quiz.q: Which form is नृप · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: copulative — both members are heads, joined as "and"

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः — words standing in the sense of "च" (and) form a द्वन्द्व

notes.en: possessive — the one whose garment is blue
gerund — a कृदन्त that does not decline
the ल्यप् suffix — a क्त्वा-gerund WITH a preverb (प्र), so आगत्य-style not आगत्वा
प्र — the preverb that selects ल्यप् over क्त्वा
adverbial — उप heads it, and the whole compound is indeclinable

notes.role: अव्ययीभावः — a compound headed by an indeclinable is अव्ययीभाव

notes.en: possessive — here standing for the king himself
determinative — सेना, the second member, is the head; शत्रोः सेना

notes.text: विग्रह: शत्रोः सेना — "the army of the enemy"

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — a compound whose second member carries the main sense is तत्पुरुष
षष्ठी — a षष्ठी-relation (शत्रोः) compounded → षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष

notes.en: agent — subject of the passive predicate
the क्त निष्ठा suffix — passive, "was defeated"
passive — agrees with शत्रुसेना, no finite verb
the thing protected — subject of the passive predicate
the क्त निष्ठा suffix — passive, "was protected"

readings.vyakhya: चत्वारः समासाः एकस्मिन् दृश्ये — महाबलः, मन्त्रिपुरोहितौ, उपसभम्, शत्रुसेना।
readings.vyakhya_en:
All four kinds in one scene, and each doing ordinary work. महाबलः is a
बहुव्रीहि — not "great" and not "strength" but the one who HAS great strength,
the king. मन्त्रिपुरोहितौ is a द्वन्द्व, minister and priest taken as a pair.
उपसभम् is an अव्ययीभाव, उप carrying it and the whole going indeclinable. And
शत्रुसेना is a तत्पुरुष — शत्रोः सेना, the enemy's army — whose defeat the
passive participle पराजिता reports without a finite verb.

readings.sentence: अद्य राजा सभाम् अगमत्। तत्र दूतः अवादीत् — शत्रवः पराजिताः, ग्रामाः च रक्षिताः। राजा तत् अश्रौषीत्, मन्त्रिणः च अपृच्छत् — केन एतत् कृतम्। मन्त्रिणः अवादिषुः — यः स्वयम् न भाषते सः एव अकार्षीत्। ततः राजा तम् वीरम् आह्वयत्, वरम् च अददात्। सः वीरः तूष्णीम् आसीत्, न च किञ्चित् अयाचत।
readings.translation: Today the king went to the assembly. There a messenger spoke — "The enemies are defeated, and the villages protected." The king heard that, and asked the ministers — "By whom was this done?" The ministers spoke — "He who does not speak of himself is the very one who did it." Then the king summoned that hero, and gave a boon. That hero was silent, and asked for nothing.
readings.teaches:
अगमत्, अवादीत्, अश्रौषीत्, अवादिषुः, अकार्षीत् — five aorists in one
scene. पराजिताः and रक्षिताः stand as predicates without a verb.

quiz.q: Which form is राजन् · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.role: लुङ् — past action → अगमत्
खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — final स् → visarga → शत्रवः

notes.en: past passive participle (क्त) with परा — predicate, no verb

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — the plural स् → visarga → ग्रामाः

quiz.q: Which form is ग्राम · प्रथमा · बहुवचन?
Which form is राजन् · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.role: आदेशप्रत्ययोः — the सिच् स् goes ष् after the ओ

notes.en: nominative plural — the same form as the accusative above

notes.role: लुङ् — past action → अवादिषुः
लुङ् — past action → अकार्षीत्
खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — the स् of ततस् → visarga

quiz.q: Which form is राजन् · प्रथमा · एकवचन?
Which form is वीर · द्वितीया · एकवचन?
Which form is वीर · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: neuter accusative with the indefinite particle

readings.vyakhya: पञ्च लुङः एकस्मिन् प्रसङ्गे — अगमत् अवादीत् अश्रौषीत् अवादिषुः अकार्षीत्। पराजिताः रक्षिताः कृतम् इति कर्मणि क्तानि, तिङन्तम् अन्तरेण। मन्त्रिणः इति द्वितीयाबहुवचने प्रथमाबहुवचने च समानम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Five aorists carry the scene, and three of the sentences have no finite verb at all — शत्रवः पराजिताः, ग्रामाः रक्षिताः, केन एतत् कृतम् all rest on a participle. मन्त्रिणः appears twice, first as the accusative of the persons asked and then as the nominative of the persons answering; nothing in the form distinguishes them, only the verb each one stands beside. The hero's silence is the point of the last sentence and also its grammar — तूष्णीम् आसीत् and न किञ्चित् अयाचत say it twice, once with an indeclinable and once with a verb.

readings.sentence: कस्मिंश्चित् ग्रामे मुनिः वसति स्म। जनाः तम् अपृच्छन् — किम् कुर्याम। मुनिः अवदत् — दानम् कुरुत, सत्यम् वदत। दानेन सुखम् भवति, असत्येन च दुःखम्। यः सत्यम् वदेत् सः श्रेष्ठः। रामेण एतत् वचनम् स्मृतम्।
readings.translation: In a certain village there lived a sage. The people asked him — "What should we do?" The sage said — "Practise giving, speak the truth. From giving comes happiness, and from untruth, sorrow. He who speaks truth is the best." These words were remembered by Rāma.
readings.teaches:
दानम् and असत्येन name acts as things; कुर्याम and वदेत् ask what ought to be
done. कस्मिंश्चित् opens with a श्चुत्व join and रामेण closes with णत्व.

notes.en: कस्मिन् + चित् — the न् goes श् before च्

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — श्चुत्व at the join → कस्मिंश्चित्

quiz.q: Which form is ग्राम · सप्तमी · एकवचन?
Which form is मुनि · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the optative, first person plural — asking for an obligation

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रण… लिङ् — the optative → कुर्याम

notes.en: the act named as a thing — giving, not a giver

notes.role: ल्युट् च — the neuter भाव action-noun → दानम्

notes.en: imperative plural — an instruction, against the optative above
cause — the same action-noun, now in the instrumental
negation compounded in front — न + सत्य
the optative in a general statement — whoever may speak

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रण… लिङ् — the optative → वदेत्

notes.en: the agent of a passive participle

notes.role: अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि — णत्व reaches across the ए → रामेण

notes.en: what was remembered — nominative under the participle
past participle — no finite verb needed

readings.vyakhya: दानम् दानेन — एकम् नाम, द्वे विभक्ती। कुरुत आज्ञा, कुर्याम प्रश्नः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
दानम् and दानेन are one word twice: the act as the thing given, then the act
as the reason something follows. And कुरुत orders where कुर्याम asks — the
people want to know what they ought to do, the sage tells them.

readings.sentence: गुरुः अवदत् — शिष्यः पठेत्, न तु शयीत। तस्य पठनम् एव धर्मः। एकदा सः शिष्यः न अपठत्, वनम् अगच्छत् च। तत् श्रुत्वा गुरुः अक्रुध्यत्। रामेण तत् वचनम् श्रुतम्। सः चिन्तयत् — अहम् सदा पठेयम् इति।
readings.translation: The teacher said — "A student should study, and not sleep. His studying alone is his dharma." One day that student did not study, and went to the forest. Hearing that, the teacher grew angry. Rāma heard those words. He thought — "I will always study."
readings.teaches:
पठेत् and पठेयम् in one exchange, against अपठत् and अगच्छत्. पठनम् names
the act rather than the actor; श्रुत्वा and श्रुतम् are built from one root.

quiz.q: Which form is गुरु · प्रथमा · एकवचन?
Which form is शिष्य · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the optative — what ought to be done, not what is

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रणामन्त्रण… लिङ् — the optative for an obligation → पठेत्

notes.en: a second optative, आत्मनेपद — शी takes the middle

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रण… लिङ् — the optative → शयीत

notes.en: the action-noun — the studying, not the one who studies

notes.role: ल्युट् च — ल्युट् makes a neuter भाव action-noun → पठनम्

quiz.q: Which form is धर्म · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the past — the same root as पठेत्, and only the ending differs
gerund — the hearing precedes the anger
past — क्रुध् is दिवादि, so श्यन् and no गुण
the agent of a passive participle — instrumental

notes.role: अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि — णत्व reaches across the ए → रामेण

notes.en: what was heard — nominative under the participle
past participle from the same root as श्रुत्वा above
the optative in the first person — a resolve rather than an obligation

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रण… लिङ् — the optative → पठेयम्

readings.vyakhya: पठेत् पठेयम् अपठत् — एकः धातुः, त्रीणि रूपाणि।
readings.vyakhya_en:
पठ् appears three times and means three different things by its ending
alone: पठेत् is what a student ought to do, पठेयम् is what this one resolves
to do, अपठत् is what he did not do. The root never changes.

readings.sentence: नद्याः तीरे तिष्ठन् राजा दूरात् आगच्छन्तम् भ्रातरम् अपश्यत्। भ्राता श्रान्तः आसीत्। राज्ञा जलम् दातव्यम् इति मन्त्री अवदत्। राजा स्वयम् जलम् अददात्। पिता तत् पश्यन् अवदत् — एतत् एव राज्ञः कर्म, न अन्यत्। स्मरणीयम् एतत् सर्वैः।
readings.translation: Standing on the bank of a river, the king saw his brother coming from afar. The brother was tired. The minister said that water was to be given by the king. The king himself gave water. The father, seeing that, said — "This alone is a king's work, not anything else. This is to be remembered by all."
readings.teaches:
three participles set against three finite verbs, with two gerundives in
between: दातव्यम् and स्मरणीयम्, both stating obligation with no verb.

notes.en: genitive — the ई of नदी becomes य् before the ending

quiz.q: Which form is नदी · षष्ठी · एकवचन?

notes.en: present participle — where he was while he saw

notes.role: लटः शतृशानचौ — शतृ replaces लट् → तिष्ठन्

notes.en: nominative — the न् of राजन् drops

notes.role: नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य — the stem-final न् drops → राजा

quiz.q: Which form is राजन् · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the same participle in the accusative, qualifying भ्रातरम्

notes.role: लटः शतृशानचौ — शतृ replaces लट् → आगच्छन्तम्
सर्वनामस्थाने चासम्बुद्धौ — lengthening in the strong cases → भ्रातर्

quiz.q: Which form is भ्रातृ · द्वितीया · एकवचन?

notes.en: strong nom.sg — the ऋ lengthens to आ

notes.role: ऋतो ङिसर्वनामस्थानयोः — गुण of the ऋ-stem in the strong cases → भ्राता

notes.en: past participle used as a predicate
the agent of a gerundive — instrumental

quiz.q: Which form is राजन् · तृतीया · एकवचन?

notes.en: what is to be given — nominative under the gerundive
gerundive — obligation, with no finite verb

notes.role: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः — तव्य forms the gerundive → दातव्यम्

notes.en: nominative — an इन्-stem, the न् dropping and the इ lengthening
strong nom.sg of an ऋ-stem, like भ्राता above

notes.role: ऋतो ङिसर्वनामस्थानयोः — गुण in the strong cases → पिता

notes.en: the weak stem — the अ drops before a vowel ending

notes.role: नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य — the stem-final न् is gone in राज्ञ् too

quiz.q: Which form is राजन् · षष्ठी · एकवचन?

notes.en: neuter nominative — an अन्-stem, the न् dropping
the अनीयर् gerundive beside दातव्यम् above

notes.role: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः — अनीयर् forms the gerundive → स्मरणीयम्

notes.en: the agent of the gerundive, again instrumental

quiz.q: Which form is सर्व · तृतीया · बहुवचन?

readings.vyakhya: तिष्ठन् आगच्छन्तम् पश्यन् — शतृ। दातव्यम् स्मरणीयम् — कृत्य। क्रिया अन्यथा अपि उच्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Six of the words here would be verbs in English and are not. तिष्ठन्,
आगच्छन्तम् and पश्यन् are participles; दातव्यम् and स्मरणीयम् are
gerundives. Only अपश्यत्, आसीत्, अवदत् and अददात् are finite.

राज्ञा जलम् दातव्यम् has no verb at all — an instrumental agent, a
nominative object, and a word meaning "to-be-given". Sanskrit says a great
deal this way, and it reads as ordinary statement once it stops being
turned into an English passive.

readings.sentence: राजा सभायाम् आसीत्। तत्र भगवान् मुनिः आगच्छत्। राज्ञः पिता अपि तत्र। मुनिः राजानम् अवदत् — पितरम् पश्य, धनवान् सः न, तथापि श्रेष्ठः। राज्ञा तत् श्रुतम्। ततः सः पितरि भक्तिम् अकरोत्। भगवतः वचनेन राजा शान्तः अभवत्।
readings.translation: The king was in the assembly. There the Blessed One, a sage, came. The king's father was there too. The sage said to the king — "Look at your father; he is not wealthy, yet he is the better man." That was heard by the king. Then he showed devotion to his father. By the Blessed One's words the king became calm.
readings.teaches:
consonant stems in one scene, each in both grades: राजा / राज्ञः / राजानम्,
भगवान् / भगवतः, पिता / पितरम्.

notes.en: nominative — the bare form loses the final न् of राजन्

notes.role: नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य — the stem-final न् drops → राजा

quiz.q: Which form is राजन् · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the strong form — नुम् inserted, then the vowel lengthens

notes.role: उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थानेऽधातोः — a उगित् stem takes नुम् in the strong cases → भगवान्

quiz.q: Which form is मुनि · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the WEAK stem — the अ of राजन् drops before a vowel ending, giving राज्ञ्

quiz.q: Which form is राजन् · षष्ठी · एकवचन?
