present — दा has the stem यच्छ्
the root vowel strengthens before शप् — रुच् → रोच्
the thematic अ between root and ending
present plural — the FRUITS are the agent here, not the boy

notes.role: रुच्यर्थानां प्रीयमाणः — the one pleased is सम्प्रदान → बालाय

quiz.q: Which form is गृह · द्वितीया · एकवचन?

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
भी again — a SECOND meeting with the rule, different noun

sequence.vyakhya: क्रियया विभक्तिः नियम्यते। भीत्रार्थे पञ्चमी, क्रुधार्थे चतुर्थी — एकस्मिन् वाक्ये उभे।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The boy fears the wolf and is angry at his mother in consecutive clauses.
Both are objects of an emotion; neither takes the accusative; and they take
DIFFERENT cases — वृकात् ablative, मात्रे dative. Nothing about the nouns
explains that. Only the verb does.

That is the whole content of special government, and a sentence like
बालः वृकेभ्यः बिभेति cannot show it, because with one verb on the page
there is no choice being made. Here the verb arrives first and the case
follows from it.

sequence.translation: The man cooks rice.
sequence.teaches: the verb's ending is परस्मैपद — the active-voice set of तिङ् endings

quiz.q: Which form is नर · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
active voice — the तिप्-तस्-झि set of endings

notes.role: लः परस्मैपदम् — the तिङ् endings replacing a लकार are by default परस्मैपद

sequence.vyakhya: लादेशाः परस्मैपदम् — तिप्तस्झ्यादयः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The endings that replace a लकार are, in general, परस्मैपद — the active set (तिप्, तस्, झि …). पचति is one of them. A second set, the आत्मनेपद, stands beside it for the middle voice.

sequence.translation: The man cooks rice (for himself).
sequence.teaches: the आत्मनेपद — the middle-voice set, action for the agent's own sake

quiz.q: Which form is नर · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
middle voice — the त-आताम्-झ set of endings

notes.role: तङानावात्मनेपदम् — the तङ् (and शानच्/कानच्) replacements are आत्मनेपद
तान्येकवचन… — the nine endings distribute as 3 पुरुष × 3 वचन (एक/द्वि/बहु)

sequence.vyakhya: पचति परस्मैपदम्, पचते आत्मनेपदम् — स एव धातुः, फलम् अन्यत्र वा स्वे वा।
sequence.vyakhya_en: One root, two ending-sets. पचति (परस्मैपद) cooks for another; पचते (आत्मनेपद) cooks for oneself. The nine endings of each set fill the same grid — three पुरुष across three वचन — so a verb-form names person, number, and voice all at once.

sequence.translation: Homage to the gods.
sequence.teaches: नमः and its companions (स्वस्ति, स्वाहा …) govern the चतुर्थी

notes.text: the word of salutation

notes.role: नमःस्वस्ति… — with नमः (and स्वस्ति, स्वाहा, स्वधा, अलम्, वषट्) the word takes चतुर्थी
चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → देवेभ्यः

sequence.vyakhya: नमसा योगे चतुर्थी। नमो देवेभ्यः, न देवान्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A handful of fixed words — नमः foremost — govern the चतुर्थी by themselves, no verb needed. "नमो देवेभ्यः," homage to the gods (चतुर्थी), never देवान्. Learn the word, and its case comes with it.

sequence.translation: The man studies for a month.
sequence.teaches: duration and extent (काल, अध्वन्) in continuous connection take द्वितीया

quiz.q: Which form is नर · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: object — here, the span filled by the action

notes.role: कालाध्वनोरत्यन्तसंयोगे — a time-word (or distance) in unbroken connection takes द्वितीया

sequence.vyakhya: अत्यन्तसंयोगे कालाध्वनोः द्वितीया। मासम् अधीते — कृत्स्नं कालम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: When an action fills a whole stretch of time or space without a break, that span stands in the द्वितीया: मासम् अधीते, "studies through a whole month." The accusative here measures extent, not an object reached.

sequence.translation: He goes to the village.
sequence.teaches: गत्यर्थ — with a verb of motion, the goal (कर्म) takes द्वितीया

notes.en: the goal of motion is treated as the object

notes.role: कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → the most-desired goal is कर्मन्
गत्यर्थकर्मणि द्वितीयाचतुर्थ्यौ — with a motion-verb the goal takes द्वितीया (or चतुर्थी)

notes.text: ग्रामम् → ग्रामं (final म् → anusvāra before ग)

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

notes.role: वर्तमाने लट् → present

sequence.vyakhya: गत्यर्थस्य धातोः कर्म गन्तव्यं द्वितीयायाम्। ग्रामो गन्तव्यः, अतः ग्रामम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A verb of motion (गम् "go") makes its destination the कर्मन् — the goal one most wants to reach (1.4.49) — and that takes the accusative (2.3.12). So "go TO the village" is simply ग्रामम् (acc.), no preposition needed. The same rule allows चतुर्थी (a dative of goal) in Vedic and poetry; classical prose prefers द्वितीया.

sequence.translation: He studies for a month.
sequence.teaches: अत्यन्तसंयोग — unbroken extent of time/space takes द्वितीया

notes.en: extent — the span over which the action runs without break

notes.role: कालाध्वनोरत्यन्तसंयोगे — a word of time or distance spanning an unbroken stretch takes द्वितीया

sequence.vyakhya: कालस्य अध्वनश्च अत्यन्तसंयोगे द्वितीया। मासम् इति कालपरिमाणम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Duration and distance, when the action fills the whole stretch without a gap, stand in the accusative (2.3.5) — मासम् "(for) a month," क्रोशम् "(for) a krośa of road." Not "to a month" but "across the whole of it." This is why "he studies for a month" needs no "for": the bare accusative मासम् carries the span.

sequence.sentence: नरः ग्रामे वसति। तस्य पुत्रः बालः। प्रभाते नरः बालः च वनम् गच्छतः। वने वृक्षाः सन्ति। नरः वृक्षात् फलानि आहरति। बालः फलानि इच्छति। नरः बालाय फलम् यच्छति। बालः फलम् खादति। ततः नरौ ग्रामम् आगच्छतः।
sequence.translation: A man lives in a village. His son is a boy. At dawn the man and the boy go to the forest. In the forest there are trees. The man brings down fruits from a tree. The boy wants the fruits. The man gives the boy a fruit. The boy eats the fruit. Then the two of them come back to the village.
sequence.teaches:
all six कारकas across nine sentences of connected prose. प्रभाते and वने
share the सप्तमी — time and place take the same case. The dual opens and
closes the passage.

quiz.q: Which form is नर · प्रथमा · एकवचन?
Which form is ग्राम · सप्तमी · एकवचन?

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
genitive — a relation, not a कारक

quiz.q: Which form is पुत्र · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: nominative — a nominal sentence, no verb needed

quiz.q: Which form is बाल · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: locus in TIME — the same सप्तमी that marks place
indeclinable — joins two agents, so the verb goes dual
dual verb — two agents joined by च take the तस् ending
goal of motion — what the agent reaches
locus — now the scene, not the goal
plural — अ-stem नर-type, so वृक्ष + जस् → वृक्षाः
source — the fixed point departed from

quiz.q: Which form is वृक्ष · पञ्चमी · एकवचन?

notes.en: neuter plural — प्रथमा = द्वितीया, so फलानि serves either
the thematic अ between root and ending
recipient — the one the giving is aimed at

quiz.q: Which form is बाल · चतुर्थी · एकवचन?

notes.en: object — singular now, against the plural फलानि above
the thematic अ between root and ending
present — दा has the irregular stem यच्छ्
the thematic अ between root and ending
dual — the man and the boy, taken together

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने — two of them, so द्विवचन → नरौ

quiz.q: Which form is ग्राम · द्वितीया · एकवचन?

notes.en: dual verb — तस् ending agrees with नरौ, closing the frame

sequence.vyakhya: एकस्मिन् वाक्ये यत् पृथक् दृष्टं तत् अत्र सङ्गतम्। षट् कारकाणि एकस्याम् कथायाम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
Nothing here is new, and none of it is the point. ग्रामे is where the man
lives, not an example of the सप्तमी; वृक्षात् is where the fruit comes
from, not a demonstration of अपादान.

sequence.translation: "curds, Indra" → दधीन्द्रः (curds-Indra)
sequence.teaches: सवर्णदीर्घ — two like (सवर्ण) vowels merge into one long vowel

notes.text: दधि + इन्द्रः: इ meets इ

notes.en: homogeneous — vowels of the same place of articulation

notes.role: अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः — a simple vowel before a like vowel; the two become one long vowel

notes.text: → ई → दधीन्द्रः

sequence.vyakhya: समाने सवर्णे अकः दीर्घ एकादेशः। इ + इ = ई।
sequence.vyakhya_en: When a simple vowel (अक्) meets a homogeneous vowel — इ with इ, उ with उ, अ with अ — the pair fuses into the single long vowel of that class. दधि + इन्द्रः gives दधीन्द्रः: two इ become one ई.

sequence.translation: "not here" → नेह
sequence.teaches: गुण — अ/आ before इ/उ/ऋ yields the गुण vowel (ए, ओ, अर्)

notes.text: न + इह: अ meets इ

notes.role: आद्गुणः — when अ/आ is followed by another vowel, the two become the single गुण vowel

notes.text: अ + इ → ए → नेह

sequence.vyakhya: अवर्णात् अचि गुण एकादेशः। अ + इ = ए।
sequence.vyakhya_en: An अ or आ followed by इ, उ, or ऋ does not merge to a long vowel but shifts to the गुण grade: अ + इ → ए, अ + उ → ओ, अ + ऋ → अर्. So न + इह → नेह. The same अ behaves differently depending on the vowel it meets.

sequence.translation: "yours indeed" → तवैव
sequence.teaches: वृद्धि — अ/आ before ए/ऐ/ओ/औ yields the वृद्धि vowel (ऐ, औ)

notes.text: तव + एव: अ meets ए

notes.role: वृद्धिरेचि — when अ/आ is followed by एच् (ए ऐ ओ औ), the two become the वृद्धि vowel

notes.text: अ + ए → ऐ → तवैव

sequence.vyakhya: अवर्णात् एचि वृद्धिः एकादेशः। अ + ए = ऐ।
sequence.vyakhya_en: When अ or आ meets one of the diphthong-grade vowels (ए, ऐ, ओ, औ), the result climbs to the वृद्धि grade: अ + ए → ऐ, अ + ओ → औ. So तव + एव → तवैव. गुण and वृद्धि are the two upward grades of इ and उ.

sequence.translation: "the wise one is to be served" → सुध्युपास्यः
sequence.teaches: यण् — इ/उ/ऋ before an unlike vowel become the glide य्/व्/र्

notes.text: सुधी + उपास्यः: ई meets उ (unlike)

notes.en: the glides य् व् र् ल्

notes.role: इको यणचि — an इक् vowel (इ उ ऋ ऌ) before any vowel becomes its corresponding यण् glide

notes.text: ई → य् → सुध्युपास्यः

sequence.vyakhya: इकः अचि यण् आदेशः। ई + उ → य् + उ = यु।
sequence.vyakhya_en: When इ, उ, or ऋ meets an unlike vowel, it does not merge but turns into its glide — य्, व्, र् — and the following vowel stands: सुधी + उपास्यः → सुध्युपास्यः. (Like meeting like gave the long vowel of ex023; unlike gives the glide here.)

sequence.translation: He too goes.
sequence.teaches: visarga → ओ before a voiced sound (अतो रोः → उ, then गुण ओ); the अवग्रह (ऽ) marks the elided अ

notes.text: विग्रह: सः + अपि; the अः before a voiced sound → ओ, and अ of अपि elides (ऽ)

notes.role: अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते — अः (from रु) becomes उ before a voiced sound → स उ
आद्गुणः — अ + उ → गुण ओ → सो; the following अ drops (पूर्वरूप), marked ऽ

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: अतो रोः उत्वम्, ततः गुणः। सः + अपि = सोऽपि। लोपे अवग्रहः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The commonest visarga outcome: सः before a voiced sound. The अः (a visarga from रु, 8.2.66) becomes उ (6.1.113), then अ + उ fuse by गुण to ओ (6.1.87) → सो; the following short अ then drops, written with the अवग्रह ऽ. सः + अपि → सोऽपि "he too." This is why सः appears as सो only before voiced sounds — before a vowel other than अ, or a consonant, it shifts differently.

sequence.translation: Salutation to you.
sequence.teaches: visarga → स् before a त्-class stop (विसर्जनीयस्य सः)

notes.text: विग्रह: नमः + ते; the visarge before त् becomes स् (its homorganic sibilant)

notes.role: विसर्जनीयस्य सः — visarga → स् before a sibilant/dental-स् context → नमस्

sequence.vyakhya: विसर्जनीयस्य सकारः सवर्णे। नमः + ते = नमस्ते।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Before a dental, the visarga assimilates to स् (8.3.34, विसर्जनीयस्य सः). नमः + ते → नमस्ते "salutations to you" — the visarga of नमः becomes स् before the त् of ते. The same gives दुस्तर (दुः + तर), निस्तेज (निः + तेज): visarga takes the sibilant of the place that follows.

sequence.translation: He covers over.
sequence.teaches: छ-doubling (तुक्) — a short vowel before छ inserts त् → च्छ (छे च)

notes.text: विग्रह: आ + छादयति; before छ a त् (तुक्) is inserted → च्छ

notes.role: छे च — a short vowel (here the आ-preverb context) before छ takes the augment तुक् (त्) → च्छ

sequence.vyakhya: छकारे परे तुक् (त्); त् + छ = च्छ। आ + छादयति = आच्छादयति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: छ never stands alone after a vowel: छे च (6.1.73) inserts the augment तुक् (त्), and त् + छ surfaces as च्छ. आ + छादयति → आच्छादयति "covers over." The same doubling gives तच्छ्रुत्वा (तत् + छ्रुत्वा... via श्), शिवच्छाया (शिव + छाया "Śiva's shade"): a vowel + छ always becomes -च्छ-.

sequence.translation: For this (is so).
sequence.teaches: before ह, a stop voices and doubles it — here त् + ह gives द्ध

notes.text: विग्रह: एतत् + हि; final त् → द् (जश्त्व) before voiced ह, and ह → ध (झयो हः)

notes.role: झलां जशोऽन्ते — final त् voices to द् before a voiced sound
झयो होऽन्यतरस्याम् — ह after a झय् stop optionally becomes its voiced aspirate → ध

notes.en: "for, indeed" (the ह that triggers the change)

sequence.vyakhya: अन्त्यस्य जश्त्वम् (त्→द्), झयः परस्य हस्य घोषवदादेशः (ह→ध)। एतत् + हि = एतद्धि।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Two changes meet at त् + ह. First जश्त्व: the final त् voices to द् before the voiced ह (8.2.39). Then the ह, now after a voiced stop, optionally becomes that stop's voiced aspirate — झयो होऽन्यतरस्याम् (8.4.62) — so ह → ध and the cluster surfaces as द्ध: एतत् + हि → एतद्धि. The same gives तद्धित (तत् + हित), वाग्घरि (वाक् + हरि): a stop + ह coalesces into a doubled voiced aspirate.

sequence.translation: He delights again.
sequence.teaches: visarga → र् before a voiced sound — the other outcome, beside सोऽपि

notes.text: पुनः ends in रु; before a voiced sound the visarga surfaces as र् (not ओ)

notes.role: ससजुषो रुः — word-final स् → रु; its visarga becomes र् before a voiced sound
अतो रोः — applies to अ-final रु (सः→सो); पुनर् keeps र् because its base is पुनर्, not अतः

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: रेफान्तस्य रुत्वम् घोषे। पुनः + रमते = पुनर् रमते। (अतो भिन्नत्वात् न ओत्वम्।)
sequence.vyakhya_en: Not every visarga becomes ओ. Words whose underlying final is -र् (पुनर्, अन्तर्, प्रातर्) show र् before a voiced sound, NOT the अ + उ → ओ fusion of ex155. पुनः + रमते → पुनर् रमते "delights again." Contrast सोऽपि (सः, base स-अः → सो) with पुनर् (base पुनर्): the visarga's outcome depends on what stands under it — an अ that fuses to ओ, or an र् that simply reappears.

sequence.sentence: रामः च लक्ष्मणः च → रामश्च लक्ष्मणश्च।
sequence.translation: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.
sequence.teaches: visarga → श् before a च्-class stop (श्चुत्व applied to the visarga-sibilant)

notes.text: विग्रह: रामः + च; visarga → स् (8.3.34), then स् → श् before च् (श्चुत्व)

notes.role: विसर्जनीयस्य सः — visarga → स् before the following stop
स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — स्/त् before a च्-class sound become श्/च् → रामश्च

notes.text: same change: लक्ष्मणः + च → लक्ष्मणश्च

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः → श् before च

sequence.vyakhya: विसर्जनीयस्य सः, ततः श्चुत्वम्। रामः + च = रामश्च। द्वयोः योगे चकारः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The visarga before a च-class stop ends up as श्. First it becomes स् (8.3.34); then स् before च् is cerebralised — really palatalised — to श् by स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40). रामः च → रामश्च, लक्ष्मणः च → लक्ष्मणश्च, the standard "X and Y" linkage. The visarga's three sibilant outcomes — स् (before त्, ex156), श् (before च्, here), ष् (before ट्) — all follow the place of the stop that comes next.

sequence.sentence: रामश्च लक्ष्मणश्च वनमगच्छताम्। तत्रर्षिरुवाच — नमस्ते वीर, सोऽपि धर्मं रक्षति। तयोर्गुरुराच्छादयति वनम्। पुनर्ग्राममागच्छतो नरौ।
sequence.translation: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa went to the forest. There a sage said — "Homage to you, hero; he too protects dharma." Their teacher covers the forest. The two men come back to the village again.
sequence.teaches:
sandhi as it appears in text — joined and unmarked: रामश्च, तत्रर्षिरुवाच,
सोऽपि, पुनर्ग्राममागच्छतो. The word-list gives the constituents.

notes.en: रामः + च — the visarga becomes श् before a च्-class stop

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — श्चुत्व applied to the visarga-sibilant → रामश्च

notes.en: लक्ष्मणः + च — the same join, immediately repeated
वनम् + अगच्छताम् — the म् simply carries onto the following vowel
वनम् is कर्मन्, goal of motion; अगच्छताम् is dual past (लङ्)
तत्र + ऋषिः + उवाच — अ + ऋ merge, then the visarga of ऋषिः → र्

notes.role: अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः — तत्र + ऋषिः gives तत्रर्षिः

notes.en: नमः + ते — the visarga becomes स् before a त्-class stop
ते is dative — नमस् governs the चतुर्थी

quiz.q: Which form is वीर · सम्बोधन · एकवचन?

notes.en: सः + अपि — visarga → ओ, and the अ of अपि elides, marked by ऽ

notes.role: अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते — रु → उ, then गुण gives सो, and अपि loses its अ

notes.en: accusative — written with anusvāra before the following र्
the thematic अ between root and ending
तयोः + गुरुः + आच्छादयति — two visargas → र्, then आ + छ doubles the छ

notes.role: छे च — a short vowel before छ takes the तुक् augment → आच्छादयति

words.gloss: come back to the village again

notes.en: पुनः + ग्रामम् + आगच्छतः — visarga → र्, then final visarga → ओ before न्

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — the रु/visarga alternation running twice in one word-group

notes.en: nominative dual — agreeing with the dual verb आगच्छतः

sequence.vyakhya: सन्धिः पदच्छेदे ज्ञायते, न तु योजने। यत् पठसि तत् विभज।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
A sandhi rule is usually shown from the pieces inward: रामः + च, and watch
them join. Text runs the other way. It gives you रामश्च and तत्रर्षिरुवाच
whole, and the work is taking them apart. That is पदच्छेद — sandhi is not
something performed in writing so much as undone in reading.

Nothing in the sentence is marked. The joins are easier to hear than to
see — रामश्च and पुनर्ग्राममागच्छतो resolve on the tongue before they
resolve on the page. The word-list carries the constituents for the ones
that don't.

sequence.translation: He did that (long ago / it is told).
sequence.teaches: लिट् — the perfect, for remote or reported past; the root reduplicates

notes.en: perfect — the remote or reported past (परोक्ष)

notes.role: परोक्षे लिट् — for a past beyond direct witness, लिट् replaces the लकार

notes.text: कृ reduplicates → च-कार → चकार

sequence.vyakhya: परोक्षे भूते लिट्। धातुः द्विरुक्तः — चकार।
sequence.vyakhya_en: For a past the speaker did not witness — the deep past of story and report — the लिट् is used, and the root doubles its first syllable: कृ → चकार, "he did" (out of sight, or long ago). Compare अकरोत् (लङ्, the past one saw): same act, different reach into time.

sequence.translation: He will do that tomorrow.
sequence.teaches: लृट् — the future; built on the root with a स्य-marker

notes.text: the adverb fixing the time as future

notes.role: लृट् शेषे च — for what is yet to be, लृट् is used

notes.text: करि + ष्य + ति → करिष्यति

sequence.vyakhya: भविष्यति लृट्। करोति, अकरोत्, चकार, करिष्यति — एकः धातुः, चत्वारः कालाः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: For what is still to come, the लृट् is used. Now the whole time-axis stands on one root √कृ: करोति (does), अकरोत् (did, witnessed), चकार (did, long ago), करिष्यति (will do). The लकार is the verb's clock — choose it, and the tense is set.

sequence.translation: He did that yesterday.
sequence.teaches: लङ् — the imperfect, for a past before today (अनद्यतन)

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → सः
अनद्यतने लङ् → the imperfect for a not-today past → अकरोत्
तिङ्: तिप् (3·sg) on the past base → अकरोत् (with अट्-augment)

sequence.vyakhya: अनद्यतने भूते लङ्। ह्यः इति अनद्यतनकालः, अतः अकरोत्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Sanskrit splits the past three ways by *remoteness*. लङ् (the imperfect, 3.2.111) is the past that does NOT fall on the current day — hence ह्यः "yesterday" → अकरोत् "he did." The अ- prefix (अट्-augment) is the past marker you also saw in अगच्छत्. Same root √कृ as करोति "does," now in the not-today past.

sequence.translation: He did that long ago.
sequence.teaches: लिट् — the perfect, for a remote (परोक्ष) past beyond witness

notes.en: indeclinable — "of old" (marks the परोक्ष, beyond-sight, past)
perfect — remote past, not directly witnessed

notes.role: परोक्षे लिट् → the perfect for a past beyond the speaker's witness → चकार (reduplicated)

sequence.vyakhya: परोक्षे भूते लिट्। अदृष्टं चिरातीतं — चकार। तदेव कृ-धातुः, द्विरुक्तम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The perfect (लिट्, 3.2.115) is the *remote* past — परोक्ष, "beyond the eye," what the speaker did not himself witness (history, legend, "long ago"). √कृ reduplicates to चकार "he did (of old)." Contrast ex060: अकरोत् (लङ्) is yesterday's deed, चकार (लिट्) is the ancient deed. The tense itself tells you how far back, and whether anyone saw it.

sequence.translation: He did that today.
sequence.teaches: लुङ् — the aorist, the tense-neutral past (and today’s past)

notes.en: aorist — the general past (and the past of today)

notes.role: लुङ् → the aorist for past sense → अकार्षीत्
च्लेः सिच् — the aorist takes the सिच् (s-aorist) marker (derivation deferred)

sequence.vyakhya: भूते सामान्ये लुङ्। अद्यतनं भूतम् अपि लुङा — अकार्षीत्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The aorist (लुङ्, 3.2.110) is the *unmarked* past — it states a past act without committing to remoteness, and it is the proper past for *today's* events (अद्य "today" → अकार्षीत् "he has done"). √कृ now spans all three pasts: अकरोत् (yesterday, लङ्) · चकार (long ago, लिट्) · अकार्षीत् (today, लुङ्). The full form-building (सिच्, वृद्धि) is a Track-B derivation.

sequence.translation: He will do that tomorrow.
sequence.teaches: लुट् — the periphrastic future, for a future beyond today (अनद्यतन)

notes.en: periphrastic future — a future not on the current day

notes.role: अनद्यतने लुट् → the लुट् future for a not-today future → कर्ता (= कर्तृ + an understood अस्ति)

sequence.vyakhya: अनद्यतने भविष्यति लुट्। श्वः इति अनद्यतनः, अतः कर्ता।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Sanskrit splits the FUTURE too. लुट् (3.3.15) is the future that does NOT fall today — श्वः "tomorrow" → कर्ता "he will do." It is "periphrastic": the form कर्ता is literally an agent-noun ("(he is) a doer (tomorrow)"). Contrast करिष्यति (लृट्, the general future, ex028). Past and future each have a today/not-today split — the लकार is the verb's calendar.

sequence.sentence: यदि सः अगमिष्यत् तर्हि सुखम् अलप्स्यत।
sequence.translation: Had he gone, he would have obtained happiness.
sequence.teaches: लृङ् — the conditional, for an act that never came about (क्रियातिपत्ति)

notes.role: लिङ्निमित्ते लृङ् क्रियातिपत्तौ — when the act fails to happen, लृङ् → अगमिष्यत्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → सुखम्
लिङ्निमित्ते लृङ् क्रियातिपत्तौ → अलप्स्यत

sequence.vyakhya: क्रियायाः अनिष्पत्तौ लृङ्। यदि अगमिष्यत् — न तु अगच्छत्। फलमपि न लब्धम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The लृङ् conditional is for what would-have-been but was NOT — क्रियातिपत्ति, the act's non-occurrence (3.3.139). It looks like the future-stem (गमिष्य-, लप्स्य-) with the augment अ and the लङ् imperfect endings: अगमिष्यत्, अलप्स्यत. यदि सः अगमिष्यत् "had he gone" — implying he did not. This completes the ten लकारs: present, three pasts, two futures, three moods, and now the conditional.

sequence.translation: The village is gone-to by Rāma. (Rāma goes to the village.)
sequence.teaches: कर्मणि प्रयोग — the passive: the object becomes the nominative subject; agent → instrumental; यक् + आत्मनेपद

notes.en: the agent, now in the instrumental (not nominative)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → कर्तृ in the passive → रामेण

words.gloss: the village — now the grammatical subject

notes.en: the logical object, raised to nominative subject in the passive

notes.role: प्रातिपदिकार्थ…प्रथमा → the कर्म, when verb-denoted, takes प्रथमा → ग्रामः

quiz.q: Which form is ग्राम · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the passive विकरण — root + य, with आत्मनेपद endings

notes.role: सार्वधातुके यक् — the passive विकरण यक् (य) → गम्यते
लः कर्मणि च — the ल-affix denotes the कर्म (passive) → ātmanepada ending
भावकर्मणोः — passive/impersonal take आत्मनेपद → गम्यते

sequence.vyakhya: कर्मणि यक्, आत्मनेपदं च। रामः गच्छति → रामेण ग्रामः गम्यते।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The passive (कर्मणि प्रयोग) re-stages the same act: the OBJECT becomes the nominative subject (ग्रामः), the AGENT drops to the instrumental (रामेण), and the verb takes the passive marker यक् (य, 3.1.67) with ātmanepada endings (1.3.13) — गम्यते "is gone-to." Active रामः ग्रामं गच्छति = passive रामेण ग्रामः गम्यते. The ल-affix now points to the कर्म, not the कर्तृ (3.4.69).

sequence.translation: It is slept by Devadatta. (Devadatta sleeps.)
sequence.teaches: भावे प्रयोग — the impersonal passive of an intransitive verb: no subject, agent in the instrumental

notes.en: the agent, in the instrumental (no nominative exists)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → कर्तृ in भाव/passive → देवदत्तेन

notes.en: the passive विकरण — root + य, with आत्मनेपद endings

notes.role: …भावे चाकर्मकेभ्यः — for intransitive roots the ल-affix denotes भाव (the bare act)
भावकर्मणोः → आत्मनेपद → सुप्यते (3sg, no agreement with any noun)

sequence.vyakhya: अकर्मकात् भावे प्रयोगः। कर्तृ तृतीयायाम्, क्रिया एव प्रधाना। देवदत्तेन सुप्यते।
sequence.vyakhya_en: An intransitive verb has no object to promote, so its passive is IMPERSONAL — भावे प्रयोग, "the bare act" (3.4.69 …भावे चाकर्मकेभ्यः). There is no subject at all: the verb stands in a fixed 3rd-singular (सुप्यते), and the agent is instrumental (देवदत्तेन). Literally "it-is-slept by Devadatta" = "Devadatta sleeps." Sanskrit's way of foregrounding the action over the doer.

sequence.translation: He did (it). / He made (it).
sequence.teaches: लुङ् — the aorist, the simple/unmarked past (no restriction to a time-frame)

notes.role: लुङ् — past action without a time restriction → the aorist → अकार्षीत्

sequence.vyakhya: सामान्ये भूते लुङ्। अकार्षीत् — न अद्यतनानद्यतनविशेषः। कृ-धातोः सिजन्तम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The लुङ् aorist is the UNMARKED past: plain "did," with none of the today/before-today restrictions that लङ् (अकरोत्, imperfect) and लिट् (चकार, perfect) carry — 3.2.110 simply says लुङ् for past action. √कृ → अकार्षीत् "he did," with the augment अ and the सिच् marker. So √कृ now spans all four pasts-and-presents: करोति · अकरोत् · चकार · अकार्षीत्, plus the future करिष्यति. The full time-axis of one root.

sequence.translation: The boy cooks; the rice is cooked.
sequence.teaches: कर्तरि शप् vs कर्मणि यक् — the विकरण (stem-marker) shows the voice: active शप् (अ) vs passive यक् (य)

quiz.q: Which form is बाल · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.role: कर्तरि शप् — in the active, the विकरण शप् (अ) → पच् + अ + ति → पचति

words.gloss: the rice — subject of the passive clause

notes.en: the object, raised to nominative in the passive

notes.role: सार्वधातुके यक् — in the passive, the विकरण यक् (य) → पच् + य + ते → पच्यते

sequence.vyakhya: कर्तरि शप्, कर्मणि यक्। पच् + अ → पचति; पच् + य → पच्यते। विकरणः प्रयोगं सूचयति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: What tells active from passive is the विकरण — the little stem-marker between root and ending. Active uses शप्, अ (3.1.68 कर्तरि शप्): पच् + अ + ति → पचति "cooks." Passive uses यक्, य (3.1.67 सार्वधातुके यक्): पच् + य + ते → पच्यते "is cooked." Same root पच्, same tense; the विकरण अ vs य, and the ending परस्मै- vs आत्मनेपद, carry the whole voice contrast.

sequence.sentence: भवामि भवावः भवामः। भवसि भवथः भवथ। भवति भवतः भवन्ति।
sequence.translation: Present tense of भू "be", all nine cells: I/we-two/we am/are; you/you-two/you-all are; he/those-two/they are.
sequence.teaches: the whole present-tense paradigm — three पुरुष across three वचन

notes.role: तिप्तस्झि… — the ending series; 1sg मिप् → भवामि
तिप्तस्झि… → 3sg तिप् → भवति
बहुषु बहुवचनम् → plural → भवन्ति

sequence.vyakhya: लटि परस्मैपदस्य नव तिङः — त्रयः पुरुषाः त्रीणि वचनानि च। भू + शप् + तिङ् = भवति इत्यादि।
sequence.vyakhya_en: You met the तिङ् frame one cell at a time (ex014–016, ex092). Here is the WHOLE present-tense paradigm of भू "be" in one place — the verbal counterpart to the देव declension table (ex094). Read across each row for a person (उत्तम / मध्यम / प्रथम), down each column for a number (sg · dual · pl). The nine endings come from one master sūtra, तिप्तस्झि… (3.4.78); the stem is भू + शप् (अ) → भव-. Learn these nine and every parasmaipada present (गच्छति, पठति, वदति) falls into place.

sequence.sentence: बालः ओदनम् पचति। बालेन ओदनः पच्यते।
sequence.translation: The boy cooks the rice. The rice is cooked by the boy.
sequence.teaches:
the same event twice, and the case of every noun changes. In the first the
agent is nominative and the object accusative; in the second the object has
become nominative and the agent instrumental. The verb's ending is what
decides which.

notes.en: agent — expressed by the verb's ending, so the noun is nominative

quiz.q: Which form is बाल · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: object — NOT expressed by the ending here, so it takes a case of its own

notes.role: अनभिहिते — a रोल takes its case only when the verb has not already expressed it

notes.en: the ending ति expresses the AGENT — so बालः needs no case of its own

notes.role: लस्य — the तिङ् endings replace the लकार, and carry agent or object with them

notes.en: still the agent — but now the ending expresses the OBJECT, so the agent takes a case

notes.role: अनभिहिते — unexpressed by the verb, the agent falls back to the तृतीया

quiz.q: Which form is बाल · तृतीया · एकवचन?

notes.en: the same object as ओदनम् above, now expressed by the ending
nominative — what the verb expresses stands in the प्रथमा
the passive विकरण — पच् + य + ते
the ending ते expresses the OBJECT

notes.role: भावकर्मणोः — आत्मनेपद endings in the passive → पच्यते

sequence.vyakhya: अनभिहिते इति अधिकारः। यत् तिङा उक्तं तत् प्रथमायाम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
Both sentences describe one boy cooking one pot of rice. What moves is
which participant the verb's ending points at.

ति in पचति points at the cooker, so the cooker needs no case of its own and
stands in the प्रथमा; the rice, unmentioned by the ending, takes the
द्वितीया. ते in पच्यते points at what is cooked, so now the rice stands in
the प्रथमा and the boy — no longer pointed at — falls back to the तृतीया.

The rule behind it is one word: अनभिहिते, "when not already expressed." A
noun takes a case for its role only if the verb has not already said it.

sequence.translation: The fire blazes.
sequence.teaches: an इ-stem masculine: nominative अग्निः (नर-like सु, but on an इ-stem)

notes.role: ससजुषो रुः — the ending स् becomes रु, then visarga → अग्निः

notes.text: अग्नि + सु → अग्निः

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: इकारान्तं पुंलिङ्गम् अग्निशब्दः। प्रथमायाम् अग्निः, यथा नरः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: अग्नि is a masculine stem ending in इ. In the प्रथमा it takes the same सु that नर did, giving अग्निः — outwardly like नरः. The stem-class shows itself not here but in the oblique cases, where the इ shifts.

sequence.translation: The man gives water to the fire.
sequence.teaches: the इ-stem dative अग्नये — the stem इ takes गुण (इ → ए) before the ending

quiz.q: Which form is नर · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → the recipient अग्नि takes चतुर्थी
घेर्ङिति — before a ङित् ending (here ङे, the dative), the इ-stem takes गुण; अग्नि + ए → अग्नये

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: घेः ङिति गुणः। अग्नि + ए → अग्नये — इकारस्य गुणः एकारः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Where नर simply added its ending (नराय), the इ-stem first shifts its इ to the गुण grade ए before the dative: अग्नि → अग्नय् + ए → अग्नये. Same case, same role as बालाय — but the stem-vowel changes, which is what marks the इ-class.

sequence.translation: The fires blaze.
sequence.teaches: the इ-stem nominative plural अग्नयः — again गुण before the plural ending

notes.role: जसि च — before जस् (nom.pl), the short इ-stem takes गुण; अग्नि + अस् → अग्नय् + अस् → अग्नयः

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: जसि गुणः। अग्नि + अस् → अग्नयः, यथा चतुर्थ्याम् अग्नये।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The same गुण appears in the nominative plural: अग्नि + जस् → अग्नयः ("the fires"), where नर gave नराः. The इ-stem reveals its character wherever an ending pulls the इ up to ए.

sequence.sentence: अग्निः ज्वलति। नरः जलम् नयति। बालः वनम् गच्छति। गुरुः शिष्यम् बोधति। सः धर्मम् वदति। जनाः शृण्वन्ति। अग्नयः ज्वलन्ति, नराः च पश्यन्ति।
sequence.translation: The fire blazes. The man leads the water. The boy goes to the forest. The teacher instructs the student. He speaks dharma. The people listen. The fires blaze, and the men watch.
sequence.teaches:
seven present verbs built the same way: an अ between root and ending, and
the root vowel strengthened before it. नी → नयति, बुध् → बोधति.

quiz.q: Which form is अग्नि · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: ज्वल् + अ + ति — the अ between root and ending

notes.role: कर्तरि शप् — the शप् विकरण inserted after the root → ज्वल् + अ

quiz.q: Which form is नर · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the root vowel strengthens before शप् — नी → ने → नय्
नी + अ + ति, and ई strengthens to ए — ने + अ gives नय्

notes.role: सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः — गुण of the root vowel before शप् → नयति

quiz.q: Which form is बाल · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the same अ, on a root that also changes shape — गम् appears as गच्छ्

quiz.q: Which form is गुरु · प्रथमा · एकवचन?
Which form is शिष्य · द्वितीया · एकवचन?

notes.en: the root vowel strengthens before शप् — बुध् → बोध्
बुध् + अ + ति, and उ strengthens to ओ — the same step as in नयति

quiz.q: Which form is धर्म · द्वितीया · एकवचन?

notes.en: वद् + अ + ति — अ already, so nothing to strengthen
present plural — श्रु takes श्नु, not शप्, so the stem is शृणो/शृण्व्
nominative plural — इ strengthens before the ending, अग्नि → अग्नय्

notes.role: जसि च — गुण before the plural ending → अग्नयः

notes.en: same stem ज्वल + अ, a different ending — ज्वलति beside ज्वलन्ति
present plural — दृश् appears as पश्य्

sequence.vyakhya: धातोः परं शप्, तस्मात् पूर्वं गुणः। नी → ने → नय्। बुध् → बोध्।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
Between the root and the ending there is almost always a अ. It is not part
of either — it is inserted, and it is why भू gives भवति rather than भूति.
Once it is there, a short इ उ ऋ in the root strengthens in front of it:
नी becomes ने and then नय्, बुध् becomes बोध्.

वद् shows nothing happening, because अ cannot strengthen further. शृण्वन्ति
shows a root that takes a different insert altogether. The अ is the default,
not the rule without exception.

sequence.translation: The father comes with the son.
sequence.teaches: सह "with" → the accompanying (subordinate) person takes तृतीया

notes.role: सहयुक्तेऽप्रधाने — with सह, the accompanying (non-principal) thing takes तृतीया

notes.text: the particle governing पुत्रेण

quiz.q: Which form is पितृ · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: सहयोगे अप्रधाने तृतीया। पिता प्रधानम्, पुत्रः अप्रधानम् — पुत्रेण सह।
sequence.vyakhya_en: With सह "together," the secondary companion — not the principal actor — stands in the तृतीया: पुत्रेण सह "with the son." The father is principal (प्रधान, प्रथमा); the son accompanies (अप्रधान, तृतीया). The same case that named the instrument also names the companion.

sequence.translation: A family [is sustained] by wealth.
sequence.teaches: हेतु "cause, reason" → the cause takes तृतीया

notes.role: हेतौ — the word naming a cause takes तृतीया

notes.en: instrumental — here the sense "by reason of"

sequence.vyakhya: हेतौ तृतीया। येन फलं साध्यते सः हेतुः — धनेन कुलम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: What brings a result about — the cause — takes the तृतीया: धनेन "by reason of wealth." This is the same case as the instrument करण, widened: the means by which, and the cause for which, share one form.

sequence.translation: He comes with his son.
sequence.teaches: सह — the accompanying (subordinate) word takes तृतीया

notes.en: here the तृतीया of accompaniment, not instrument

notes.role: सहयुक्तेऽप्रधाने — with सह, the accompanier (the non-principal) takes तृतीया

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: सहयोगे अप्रधानं तृतीयायाम्। पिता प्रधानम्, पुत्रः अप्रधानः — अतः पुत्रेण।
sequence.vyakhya_en: "With" (सह) puts the companion — the *subordinate* party, not the principal — in the instrumental (2.3.19). The father is the principal (he is the agent who comes); the son merely accompanies, so the son is पुत्रेण, तृतीया. One case (तृतीया) thus carries two senses you now hold: instrument (by) and accompaniment (with).

sequence.translation: A family (is honored) on account of wealth.
sequence.teaches: हेतु — the cause/motive takes तृतीया

words.gloss: on account of wealth, because of wealth

notes.en: cause — the reason for which something happens

notes.role: हेतौ — a word denoting the cause takes तृतीया (विद्यया यशः, धनेन कुलम्)

sequence.vyakhya: हेतौ तृतीया। धनं हेतुः, तेन कुलम् उन्नतम् — धनेन।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The cause or motive — "because of X" — takes the instrumental (2.3.23). विद्यया यशः "fame through learning," धनेन कुलम् "a family (raised) by wealth." It is the same तृतीया as instrument and accompaniment, now in a third sense: the reason. Note how much one case-ending does — the reader must read the *sense* from context, not the form alone.

sequence.translation: Without dharma there is no happiness.
sequence.teaches: word-government: अन्तरा / अन्तरेण ("between, without") govern the द्वितीया

notes.en: governs the accusative of what is excluded

notes.role: अन्तराऽन्तरेण युक्ते — a word governed by अन्तरा/अन्तरेण takes the द्वितीया

quiz.q: Which form is धर्म · द्वितीया · एकवचन?

sequence.vyakhya: अन्तरेणयुक्ते द्वितीया। अन्तरेण धर्मं — न धर्मस्य, न धर्मेण।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Certain governing words fix a case by themselves. अन्तरा "between" and अन्तरेण "without, apart from" take the द्वितीया (2.3.4): अन्तरेण धर्मम् "without dharma." Not the genitive English suggests — the word अन्तरेण demands the accusative. A small class of indeclinables (विना, नाना, also) work this way; the word, not the role, sets the case.

sequence.translation: An ascetic, (recognizable) by his matted hair.
sequence.teaches: इत्थंभूतलक्षणे — the mark by which someone is recognised takes the तृतीया

notes.role: इत्थंभूतलक्षणे — the sign that marks someone as being in a state → तृतीया

sequence.vyakhya: इत्थंभूतस्य लक्षणे तृतीया। जटाभिः तापसः — जटा एव चिह्नम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The mark by which you recognize someone as being "thus" (इत्थंभूत) stands in the तृतीया (2.3.21). जटाभिः तापसः "an ascetic — (you know him) by his matted hair." The instrumental here is not an instrument of action but a sign of identification: अक्ष्णा काणः "one-eyed by (the bad) eye," जटाभिः तापसः. A distinct, idiomatic use of the third case.

sequence.translation: He dwells (there) for the sake of food.
sequence.teaches: षष्ठी हेतुप्रयोगे — when हेतु is used, both it and the cause stand in the षष्ठी

notes.en: the cause — here in the genitive because हेतु is used

notes.role: षष्ठी हेतुप्रयोगे — with the word हेतु, the cause takes the षष्ठी

words.gloss: for the sake of, by reason of

notes.text: हेतु itself stands in the षष्ठी, agreeing with the cause-word

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: हेतुशब्दप्रयोगे कारणं हेतुश्च षष्ठ्याम्। अन्नस्य हेतोः — कारणे षष्ठी।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Cause is normally the तृतीया (धनेन "because of wealth," ex033). But when the explicit word हेतु "reason" is used, BOTH it and the cause it names go into the षष्ठी (2.3.26): अन्नस्य हेतोः "for the sake of food," literally "by-reason of-food." So किम् + हेतु → किं हेतोः "why," and the common कस्य हेतोः. The presence of हेतु re-cases the cause.

sequence.translation: He moves far from the village.
sequence.teaches: दूरान्तिकार्थैः — words for "far" / "near" optionally take the द्वितीया for what they are far/near from

notes.en: the reference point of "far", in the accusative

notes.role: दूरान्तिकार्थेभ्यो द्वितीया च — with दूर/अन्तिक words, the द्वितीया (also षष्ठी/पञ्चमी)

quiz.q: Which form is ग्राम · द्वितीया · एकवचन?

notes.en: the root vowel strengthens before शप् — सृ → सर्
the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: दूरान्तिकार्थैः द्वितीया (षष्ठी पञ्चमी च)। ग्रामं दूरम् — ग्रामस्य / ग्रामात् इति विकल्पः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Words meaning "far" (दूर) and "near" (अन्तिक) let the reference point take the द्वितीया (2.3.35) — ग्रामं दूरम् "far from the village" — though षष्ठी (ग्रामस्य दूरम्) and पञ्चमी (ग्रामात् दूरम्) are also allowed. A rare case where one relation offers three cases; the speaker chooses. Distance, like time (ex056), bends the usual case-assignment.

sequence.translation: The king is the lord of the cattle.
sequence.teaches: स्वामि-ईश्वरादिभिः — with "owner / lord / master" words, what is owned takes the षष्ठी (or सप्तमी)

notes.en: what is owned — governed by स्वामिन्

notes.role: स्वामीश्वराधिपति… — with स्वामिन्/ईश्वर/अधिपति etc., the related thing takes षष्ठी (also सप्तमी)

quiz.q: Which form is गो · षष्ठी · बहुवचन?

notes.text: इन्-stem स्वामिन् → nom.sg स्वामी (न-lopa, as दण्डी ex139)

quiz.q: Which form is स्वामिन् · प्रथमा · एकवचन?
Which form is नृप · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

sequence.vyakhya: स्वाम्यादिभिः सम्बन्धिनः षष्ठी (सप्तमी वा)। गवां स्वामी — गोषु स्वामी इति वा।
sequence.vyakhya_en: With "owner, lord, master, heir, witness, guarantor" (स्वामिन्, ईश्वर, अधिपति, दायाद…), the thing owned or presided over takes the षष्ठी — or optionally the सप्तमी (2.3.39). गवां स्वामी "lord of the cattle" (= गोषु स्वामी). So धनस्य ईश्वरः / धने ईश्वरः "master of wealth": the relation-word offers genitive or locative, the speaker's choice. (Note स्वामी itself = the इन्-stem of ex139.)

sequence.translation: A son good (in his conduct) toward his mother.
sequence.teaches: साधु-निपुणाभ्याम् — with "good / skilful (toward someone)" the person is in the सप्तमी

notes.en: the person toward whom the conduct is directed → locative

notes.role: साधुनिपुणाभ्यामर्चायां सप्तमी — with साधु/निपुण (good conduct toward), use सप्तमी

quiz.q: Which form is मातृ · सप्तमी · एकवचन?
Which form is पुत्र · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

sequence.vyakhya: साधुनिपुणयोः अर्चायां सप्तमी। मातरि साधुः — यं प्रति सौजन्यम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: With साधु "good (in behaviour)" and निपुण "adept," when the sense is right conduct TOWARD someone (अर्चा), that person stands in the सप्तमी (2.3.43): मातरि साधुः "good toward his mother," पितरि निपुणः "attentive to his father." Not the dative one might expect — the locative marks the object of one's good conduct. With ex166–171 the कारक.vibhakti reference now spans the idiomatic case-government rules, not just the core six.

sequence.translation: The fruit is seen by the man.
sequence.teaches: a-stem masc. नर तृतीया एकवचन = नरेण — टा→इन (7.1.12) + णत्व

notes.en: agent expressed by the instrumental (of the passive दृश्यते)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया — the agent of the passive दृश्यते takes तृतीया
टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः — after an a-stem, तृतीया टा → इन → नर + इन = नरेन
अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि — णत्व applies across the intervening vowel → ण्

quiz.q: Which form is नर · तृतीया · एकवचन?

notes.en: the passive विकरण — root + य, with आत्मनेपद endings

notes.text: a passive (कर्मणि प्रयोग); its agent stands in तृतीया → नरेण

sequence.vyakhya: नरशब्दात् तृतीयैकवचने टा, सा अकारात् परा इनादेशम् (७.१.१२), ततो रेफात् नकारस्य णत्वम् (८.४.१), इति नरेण।
sequence.vyakhya_en: For नर in the instrumental singular the ending is टा; after an a-stem टा becomes इन (7.1.12), giving नरेन. The र then retroflexes the following न to ण (णत्व, 8.4.1) — नरेण. As the agent of the passive दृश्यते "is seen," it stands in the तृतीया (2.3.18).

sequence.sentence: तापसः गिरौ वसति। जटाभिः सः तापसः ज्ञायते। अन्नस्य हेतोः बालः तम् गच्छति। पुत्रेण सह सः आगच्छति। धनेन न सुखम्, धर्मेण सुखम् इति तापसः वदति। गवाम् स्वामी नृपः अपि तम् शृणोति।
sequence.translation: An ascetic lives on a mountain. By his matted hair he is recognized as an ascetic. For the sake of food a boy goes to him. He comes with his son. "Happiness is not from wealth; happiness is from dharma," says the ascetic. Even the king, lord of cattle, listens to him.
sequence.teaches:
the instrumental past its plain करण sense: जटाभिः as a mark of
recognition, पुत्रेण सह for accompaniment. धनेन and धर्मेण stand in one
sentence as competing causes.

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
the MARK by which someone is recognized — not an instrument proper

notes.role: इत्थंभूतलक्षणे — the identifying mark takes तृतीया → जटाभिः

notes.en: the passive विकरण — root + य, with आत्मनेपद endings
passive — the ascetic is what is known, not the knower
genitive — with हेतोः, BOTH words stand in the षष्ठी

notes.role: षष्ठी हेतुप्रयोगे — when हेतु is used, the cause takes षष्ठी → अन्नस्य हेतोः

quiz.q: Which form is बाल · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

notes.role: सहयुक्तेऽप्रधाने — the accompanying party takes तृतीया → पुत्रेण सह

quiz.q: Which form is पुत्र · तृतीया · एकवचन?

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
cause — the तृतीया of motive, not of instrument

quiz.q: Which form is धन · तृतीया · एकवचन?

notes.role: अतोऽम् — the neuter अ-stem takes अम् in प्रथमा and द्वितीया → सुखम्

notes.en: the same cause-instrumental, set against धनेन

quiz.q: Which form is धर्म · तृतीया · एकवचन?

notes.en: indeclinable — marks the end of reported speech
the thematic अ between root and ending
genitive plural — what is owned stands in the षष्ठी

notes.role: स्वामीश्वराधिपति… — with "lord/owner" words the thing owned takes षष्ठी → गवाम् स्वामी

quiz.q: Which form is गो · षष्ठी · बहुवचन?

notes.en: nominative — इन्-stem, न् drops in the nom.sg

quiz.q: Which form is स्वामिन् · प्रथमा · एकवचन?
Which form is नृप · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: present — श्रु takes the श्नु विकरण, श्रु → शृणो

sequence.translation: Without wealth, (there is) sorrow.
sequence.teaches: विना — "without" takes तृतीया (optionally पञ्चमी/द्वितीया)

notes.role: पृथग्विनानानाभिस्तृतीयान्यतरस्याम् — with पृथक्/विना/नाना the word takes तृतीया (also पञ्चमी, द्वितीया)
अतोऽम् — the neuter अ-stem takes अम् in प्रथमा and द्वितीया → दुःखम्

sequence.vyakhya: विना-योगे तृतीया अन्यतरस्याम्। धनेन विना, धनाद् विना, धनं विना — त्रयं साधु।
sequence.vyakhya_en: पृथक्, विना, and नाना — all meaning "apart / without" — govern the instrumental, *optionally* (अन्यतरस्याम्, 2.3.32); the genitive… no, the ablative (पञ्चमी) and accusative are also allowed. So धनेन विना = धनाद् विना = धनं विना, all correct. The optionality (विभाषा / अन्यतरस्याम्) is itself a feature to notice: Pāṇini often sanctions more than one form.

sequence.translation: The mountain is far from the village.
sequence.teaches: अपादान/पञ्चमी for separation-distance — "from"

notes.en: the fixed point from which distance is measured

notes.role: ध्रुवमपायेऽपादानम् — the fixed source-point is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी → ग्रामात्
सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → दूरे (सप्तमी)

notes.text: पर्वतः → पर्वतो before the voiced द (visarga सन्धि)

sequence.vyakhya: अपायस्य ध्रुवम् अपादानम्, तस्मिन् पञ्चमी। ग्रामो ध्रुवः, ततो दूरम् — ग्रामात्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The ablative (पञ्चमी) marks the fixed point one moves or measures *from* (1.4.24, 2.3.28). With words of distance — दूरे "far," अन्तिके "near" — the reference point stands in the ablative: ग्रामात् "from the village." You met पञ्चमी as "from" in विनयाद् याति; here it is spatial separation, the rule's core sense.

sequence.translation: The man comes from the village.
sequence.teaches: अपादान/पञ्चमी singular — ङसि → आत् after the a-stem → ग्रामात्

notes.text: नरः → नरो before the voiced ग (visarga सन्धि)

quiz.q: Which form is नर · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the fixed point from which departure happens

notes.role: ध्रुवमपायेऽपादानम् — the fixed point one moves away from is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी — the अपादान takes पञ्चमी
टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः — after an a-stem ङसि → आत् → ग्रामात्

quiz.q: Which form is ग्राम · पञ्चमी · एकवचन?

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: ग्रामो ध्रुवम् अपायस्य, ततो नरस्य आगमनम्। अतो ग्रामात् इति अपादाने पञ्चमी; अकारान्तत्वात् ङसेः आत्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The village is the fixed point the man moves away from, so it is अपादान (1.4.24), expressed by the पञ्चमी (2.3.28). Because the stem ends in अ, the ablative ending ङसि becomes आत् (7.1.12) → ग्रामात् "from the village."

sequence.translation: "speech here" → वाग् अत्र
sequence.teaches: जश्त्व — a word-final hard stop softens to its voiced counterpart

notes.en: the soft (voiced) stops ग् ज् ड् द् ब्

notes.role: झलां जशोऽन्ते — a stop at word's end becomes its जश् (voiced) counterpart; क् → ग्

notes.text: वाक् → वाग्

sequence.vyakhya: पदान्ते झलां जश्। क् → ग्, यथा वाक् → वाग्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A hard stop standing at the end of a word softens to its voiced partner: क्→ग्, त्→द्, प्→ब्. So वाक् "speech" appears as वाग् before अत्र. The word's lemma is वाक्; its sentence-form follows the join.

sequence.translation: "and that" → तच्च
sequence.teaches: श्चुत्व — a dental meeting a palatal becomes palatal

notes.text: तत् + च: dental त् meets palatal च

notes.en: the palatal series श् च् छ् ज् झ् ञ्

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — a dental (त-class/स) next to a palatal (च-class/श) turns palatal; त् → च्

notes.text: त् → च् → तच्च

sequence.vyakhya: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुत्वम्। त् + च → च् + च = च्च।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A dental sound touching a palatal is pulled into the palatal series: तत् + च → तच्च. The त् becomes च् to match the following च. Assimilation — the first sound takes on the place of the second.

sequence.translation: "the forest laughs" → वनं हसति
sequence.teaches: a word-final म् becomes anusvāra (ं) before a consonant

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — a word-final म् before a consonant becomes anusvāra; म् → ं

notes.text: वनम् → वनं (before हसति)

sequence.vyakhya: पदान्ते मकारस्य हलि अनुस्वारः। वनम् → वनं हसति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A म् at the end of a word, when a consonant follows, contracts to the anusvāra ं: वनम् हसति → वनं हसति. (Before a vowel, or at a true pause, the म् stays — so it is the following consonant that triggers the change.)

sequence.translation: "by Rāma": रामेन → रामेण (न becomes ण after र)
sequence.teaches: णत्व — न् becomes ण् after र्/ष् in the same word

notes.text: राम + इन (instr.sg ending ट्→इन): the न् stands after the र् of राम

notes.role: अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि — णत्व applies across the intervening vowel → ण्
अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि → the change still applies across an intervening vowel/guttural/labial (here the ए) → रामेण

sequence.vyakhya: रेफात् परः नकारः णकारः समानपदे, अट्-व्यवधानेऽपि। रामेन → रामेण।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Within one word, a न् turns cerebral (ण्) when an र् or ष् precedes it (8.4.1) — even when a vowel, guttural, or labial stands between them (8.4.2). So राम + the instrumental -इन gives रामेण, not *रामेन*: the र् of राम reaches across the ए to retroflex the न्. This णत्व is why we say रामायण, ब्राह्मणः, नारायण.

sequence.translation: "Rāma the sixth" → रामष्षष्ठः (स/त-series cerebralised by ष)
sequence.teaches: ष्टुत्व — स् and the dentals turn cerebral (ष्/ट-series) next to ष् or a cerebral

notes.text: रामस् + षष्ठः: a dental स् meets the cerebral ष्

notes.en: cerebralisation — स्/तवर्ग → ष्/टवर्ग in contact with ष् or a cerebral

notes.role: ष्टुना ष्टुः → स् and the dentals next to ष्/टवर्ग become ष्/टवर्ग → रामष्षष्ठः

sequence.vyakhya: षकारटवर्गसन्निधौ सकारतवर्गयोः ष्टुत्वम्। रामस् षष्ठः → रामष्षष्ठः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Mirror of श्चुत्व (which palatalised before श्/च-series): ष्टुत्व *cerebralises*. A dental स् or त-series sound, meeting a cerebral ष् or ट-series sound, itself becomes cerebral (8.4.41). रामस् + षष्ठः → रामष्षष्ठः; तत् + टीका → तट्टीका. The articulation simply assimilates to its neighbour's place — the same logic as जश्त्व and श्चुत्व, one row over.

sequence.sentence: सम् कृतम् → संस्कृतम् (सङ्… → the nasal homorganic).
sequence.translation: "well-made" सम्+कृत → the nasal matches the following stop
sequence.teaches: अनुस्वार → परसवर्ण — anusvāra becomes the nasal of the following class

notes.text: सम् + कृत: final म् → anusvāra (8.3.23), then the anusvāra may take the class-nasal

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः → word-final म् before a consonant → anusvāra (संकृत)

notes.en: the nasal homogeneous with the following sound

notes.role: अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः → the anusvāra becomes the class-nasal of the following यय् consonant

sequence.vyakhya: मकारः अनुस्वारः, सः ययि परसवर्णः। सम् + कृत → संकृत → सङ्… परसवर्णेन।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A final म् before a consonant first becomes anusvāra (8.3.23, the rule that gave वनं); then that anusvāra may take the *homorganic* nasal — the nasal belonging to the following sound's class (8.4.58). सम् + कृतम् → संस्कृतम्; सम् + गतः → सङ्गतः (the guttural ङ् before ग). The nasal quietly tunes itself to whatever stop follows.

sequence.translation: "homage to thee": the विसर्ग returns to स् before त
sequence.teaches: विसर्ग → स् — a visarga becomes स् before a hard dental (खर्)

notes.text: नमः + ते: the visarga of नमः meets the त् of ते

notes.role: विसर्जनीयस्य सः → a visarga → स् before a खर् consonant → नमस्ते

notes.text: नमस् here is a गति/preverb-like form; 8.3.40 also fixes its स् → नमस्ते, नमस्कारः

sequence.vyakhya: विसर्गस्य सकारः खरि। नमः + ते → नमस्ते। पुनः सकारः प्रत्येति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The visarga is not the end of the story — before a hard consonant (खर्) it can revert to स् (8.3.34): नमः + ते → नमस्ते, नमः + कारः → नमस्कारः. The final स् of नरः became visarga before pause (8.2.66 → 8.3.15); here the reverse environment pulls the visarga back to स्. Sandhi is contextual all the way down: the same sound shows different faces by what stands next.

sequence.translation: "again and again" — पुनर् at the pause shows as पुनः
sequence.teaches: रु → visarga before a hard consonant and at the pause (खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः)

notes.text: the word ends in र्; before a vowel or soft sound it stays पुनर् — पुनर् अपि

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — र् → visarga before a खर् consonant and at the pause

notes.text: the second one stands at the pause, and takes the visarga for that reason alone

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — अवसान, the pause, is the other trigger

sequence.vyakhya: खरि अवसाने च रोः विसर्जनीयः। पुनर् → पुनः। स्वरे तु पुनर् अपि इति तिष्ठति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: One rule, two triggers. The र् of पुनर् becomes visarga both before a hard consonant (पुनः कः) and at a pause, where nothing follows at all — पुनः पुनः shows the second case twice over. Before a vowel the र् survives: पुनर् अपि. So the visarga is not part of the word; it is what the word's final र् turns into when the surroundings give it nothing voiced to lean on.

sequence.sentence: वाग् अत्र शुभा। तच्च सत्यं वदति। वनं हसति, नदी च शोभते। रामेण सह मुनिर्गच्छति। संस्कृतं वचनं तेषां प्रियम्। नमस्ते गुरो, इति ते वदन्ति।
sequence.translation: Speech here is auspicious. And it speaks the truth. The forest laughs, and the river shines. The sage goes with Rāma. Refined speech is dear to them. "Homage to you, teacher," they say.
sequence.teaches:
consonant joins inside sentences rather than shown as transformations:
वाग्, तच्च, वनं, संस्कृतं, रामेण, नमस्ते.

notes.en: वाक् + अत्र — the final क् voices to ग् before a vowel

notes.role: झलां जशोऽन्ते — a final stop takes its voiced counterpart → वाग्

notes.en: तत् + च — त् becomes च् before a च्-class stop

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — श्चुत्व assimilates the dental to the palatal → तच्च
मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → सत्यं

notes.en: वनम् + हसति — final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — म् → anusvāra at a word join → वनं

notes.en: the root vowel strengthens before शप् — शुभ् → शोभ्
राम + इन → रामेन, then न् becomes ण् because र् precedes

notes.role: अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि — णत्व applies across the intervening vowel → ण्

notes.en: मुनिः + गच्छति — the visarga becomes र् before a voiced sound

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — the रु/visarga alternation → मुनिर्

notes.en: सम् + कृत — the nasal takes the point of the following स्क्

notes.role: अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः — the nasal goes homorganic → संस्कृतम्
मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → वचनं

notes.en: वचनम् + तेषाम् — म् → anusvāra again, a second instance

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → तेषां
अतोऽम् — the neuter अ-stem takes अम् in प्रथमा and द्वितीया → प्रियम्

notes.en: नमः + ते — the visarga becomes स् before त्
ते is dative — नमस् governs the चतुर्थी

quiz.q: Which form is गुरु · सम्बोधन · एकवचन?

sequence.vyakhya: यत्र पदं पदेन मिलति तत्र सन्धिः। वाग्, तच्च, वनं, रामेण — सर्वत्र।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
Six joins here and none of them announced. वाक् voices to वाग् because a
vowel follows; त् becomes च् because च follows; म् goes to anusvāra twice;
न् turns ण् in रामेण because an र् sits two syllables back.

That last one is worth noticing — the trigger is not adjacent. र् and न्
are separated by ए, and the rule still reaches across. Sandhi is not only
about what touches what.

sequence.translation: "in the fires" → अग्निषु
sequence.teaches: षत्व — the ending's स् becomes ष् after an इ (आदेशप्रत्ययोः)

notes.text: the ending is सु; its स् meets the इ of अग्नि

notes.role: आदेशप्रत्ययोः — a प्रत्यय's स् goes ष् after an इण् vowel → अग्निषु

quiz.q: Which form is अग्नि · सप्तमी · बहुवचन?

sequence.vyakhya: प्रत्ययस्य सकारः इण्कुभ्याम् उत्तरः षकारः। अग्नि + सु = अग्निषु। न तु सर्वः सकारः — प्रत्ययस्य एव।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The locative plural ending सु carries a स्, and after the इ of अग्नि that स् retroflexes to ष् — अग्निषु. The rule is narrow in a way worth noticing: it applies to the स् of an ending, not to every स् in the language. A स् that belongs to the stem itself is untouched by it, which is why the same इ does nothing to the स् of a following separate word.

sequence.translation: Hari dwells among the sages.
sequence.teaches: one sentence, both sibilant outcomes — हरिः takes visarga, ऋषिषु takes ष्

notes.en: nominative — the ending स् stands at a pause before a vowel

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — the स् of the ending → visarga → हरिः
आदेशप्रत्ययोः — the स् of सु → ष् after the इ → ऋषिषु

sequence.vyakhya: एकस्मिन् वाक्ये द्वौ सकारौ द्वयोः गत्योः — हरिः इति विसर्जनीयः, ऋषिषु इति षत्वम्। उभयत्र इकारः पूर्वः, फलम् तु भिन्नम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Both words end their stem in इ and both have an ending in स्, and the two स् go different ways: हरिः becomes visarga, ऋषिषु becomes ष्. What separates them is where the स् stands — at the end of the word in हरिः, with nothing after it to give it a place, and inside the word in ऋषिषु, with a उ following. The इ before it is the same in both.

sequence.translation: When the sun has risen, the lotus opens.
sequence.teaches: सति सप्तमी — the locative absolute: one act marking the time of another

notes.en: the locative-absolute subject — its action marks the time

notes.role: यस्य च भावेन भावलक्षणम् — that whose action marks another's time takes सप्तमी

notes.en: a past participle (क्त), agreeing with सूर्ये in सप्तमी

notes.text: उद् + इ → उदित "risen"

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → कमलं

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: यस्य भावेन अन्यस्य भावः लक्ष्यते, तत्र सप्तमी — सति सप्तमी। सूर्ये उदिते इति कालः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The "locative absolute" (सति सप्तमी): when one event fixes the *time* of another, the first stands — subject and participle together — in the locative (2.3.37). सूर्ये उदिते "the sun having risen" = "when the sun rose." It is Sanskrit's compact "when / while" clause: a noun + participle in सप्तमी, needing no conjunction.

sequence.translation: The man's doing / the deed of the man.
sequence.teaches: कृत्-योग — with a कृत् noun, agent & object take षष्ठी

notes.en: the agent, but expressed through षष्ठी before a कृत् noun

notes.role: कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति — before a कृत्-formed word, agent and object take षष्ठी

notes.en: a कृत् noun (action-noun in क्तिन्) from कृ "do"

notes.role: स्त्रियां क्तिन् — the feminine action-noun in क्तिन् → कृति

sequence.vyakhya: कृति उपपदे कर्तृकर्मणोः षष्ठी। नरः कर्ता, कृतिः कृत्, अतः नरस्य कृतिः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: When the head word is a कृत्-derivative (an action- or agent-noun built from a root), its agent and object are expressed by the genitive, not their usual cases (2.3.65). नरस्य कृतिः = "the man's deed" — नर is logically the doer, but before कृति (a कृत् noun) it takes षष्ठी. This is why "the seeing of the lotus" is कमलस्य दर्शनम्: the कृत् noun pulls everything into the genitive.

sequence.translation: The man is in the village.
sequence.teaches: सप्तमी (locative) singular — the अधिकरण as locus → ग्रामे

quiz.q: Which form is नर · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: locus — the substratum of the action

notes.role: आधारोऽधिकरणम् — the locus (आधार) is termed अधिकरण
सप्तम्यधिकरणे च — सप्तमी after the अधिकरण कारक

notes.text: ग्राम + ङि (loc.sg); the a-stem before ङि yields ग्रामे

quiz.q: Which form is ग्राम · सप्तमी · एकवचन?

notes.role: वर्तमाने लट् — present tense

sequence.vyakhya: ग्रामे इति अधिकरणे सप्तमी। आधारोऽधिकरणम् इति संज्ञा, सप्तम्यधिकरणे च इति विभक्तिः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: ग्रामे is the locus (अधिकरण) of the being: by आधारोऽधिकरणम् (1.4.45) the village as substratum gets the अधिकरण name, and सप्तम्यधिकरणे च (2.3.36) then assigns it the locative. The a-stem locative singular ending gives ग्रामे.

sequence.translation: The king of the gods shines.
sequence.teaches: a-stem masc. षष्ठी plural — आम् takes नुट् → नाम्, vowel lengthens, न → ण

notes.en: the genitive of relation/possession (the शेष relation)

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे — the षष्ठी for the leftover relation, here "of the gods"
ह्रस्वनद्यापो नुट् — after a short-vowel/नदी/आप् stem, आम् takes the नुट् augment → नाम्
नामि — before नाम्, the stem-final vowel lengthens → देवा
अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि — णत्व applies across the intervening vowels → देवानाम्

quiz.q: Which form is देव · षष्ठी · बहुवचन?
Which form is राजन् · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

notes.en: the root vowel strengthens before शप् — शुभ् → शोभ्
the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: देवानाम् इति षष्ठीबहुवचनम् — आमि नुट् (नाम्), नामि पूर्वस्य दीर्घः, रेफात् परस्य नस्य णत्वम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: देवानाम् is the genitive plural. The ending आम् first takes the नुट् augment न (7.1.54) → नाम्; before नाम् the stem-vowel lengthens to देवा (6.4.3, नामि); finally the र retroflexes the न to ण across the intervening vowels (8.4.2) → देवानाम्. With राजा (nom. sg.) the phrase means "the king of the gods shines."

sequence.sentence: देवः देवौ देवाः। देवम् देवौ देवान्। देवेन देवाभ्याम् देवैः। देवाय देवाभ्याम् देवेभ्यः। देवात् देवाभ्याम् देवेभ्यः। देवस्य देवयोः देवानाम्। देवे देवयोः देवेषु। हे देव हे देवौ हे देवाः॥
sequence.translation: The complete declension of देव "god" (a-stem masculine) — eight cases × three numbers.
sequence.teaches: the whole अकारान्त पुंलिङ्ग paradigm — देव in every case and number, with the सूत्र behind each ending

notes.role: स्वौजस्… — सु, the nom. sg. सुप् affix
ससजुषो रुः — final स् → रु → visarga → देवः
प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः — अ + औ (the dual ending) → औ → देवौ
प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः — अ + जस् (अस्) → आः → देवाः
अमि पूर्वः — अ + अम् → अम् → देवम्

words.gloss: द्वितीया द्वि — acc. dual (= nom. dual)

notes.text: acc. dual = nom. dual (औट् → औ), one form देवौ

notes.role: तस्माच्छसो नः पुंसि — masc. शस् → आन् → देवान्
टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः — a-stem टा → इन → देवेन

words.gloss: तृ/च/पं द्वि — instr/dat/abl dual (भ्याम्); ONE form for all three

notes.role: सुपि च — अ → आ before भ्याम् → देवाभ्याम् (covers तृतीया/चतुर्थी/पञ्चमी dual)
अतो भिस ऐस् — a-stem भिस् → ऐस् → देवैः
ङेर्यः — a-stem ङे → य; + सुपि च (अ→आ) → देवाय

words.gloss: च/पं बहु — dat/abl pl. (भ्यस्); ONE form for both

notes.role: बहुवचने झल्येत् — अ → ए before भ्यस् → देवेभ्यः (covers चतुर्थी/पञ्चमी pl.)
टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः — a-stem ङसि → आत् → देवात्
टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः — a-stem ङस् → स्य → देवस्य

words.gloss: ष/स द्वि — gen/loc dual (ओस्); ONE form for both

notes.role: ओसि च — अ → ए before ओस् → देवयोः (covers षष्ठी/सप्तमी dual)
ह्रस्वनद्यापो नुट् — आम् takes नुट् → नाम्
नामि — vowel lengthens before नाम् → देवानाम्
ङेर्यः / अ + ङि — the अ-stem locative singular → देवे

words.gloss: सप्तमी बहु — loc. pl. (सुप् → सु; स → ष)

notes.role: ओसि च / अ → ए before the plural locative ending → देवेषु
आदेशप्रत्ययोः — स् → ष् after the इण् ए → देवेषु
सम्बोधने च — the vocative; sg. is the bare stem → हे देव

sequence.vyakhya: अकारान्तस्य पुंलिङ्गस्य (देव) सर्वाः विभक्तयः सर्वाणि वचनानि च — एकत्र दर्शिताः। एकैकं सूत्रं प्रत्येकं प्रत्ययम् आदेशं च साधयति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: You met प्रथमा through सप्तमी one cell at a time (ex001–ex013). Here is the WHOLE a-stem masculine paradigm of देव in one place — the reference table the readings were building toward. Read down each column for a number (sg · dual · pl), across each row for a case. Note the economies Pāṇini builds in: the dual collapses three oblique cases into देवाभ्याम् and two more into देवयोः; the plural shares देवेभ्यः for dative and ablative. Every other a-stem masculine — नर, राम, बाल, पुत्र, अश्व — declines exactly thus; learn देव and you hold them all. Each cell names the sūtra that shapes its ending, so the table doubles as an index into the अङ्ग-operations of adhyāyas 6–7.

sequence.sentence: फलम् फले फलानि। फलम् फले फलानि। फलेन फलाभ्याम् फलैः। फलाय फलाभ्याम् फलेभ्यः। फलात् फलाभ्याम् फलेभ्यः। फलस्य फलयोः फलानाम्। फले फलयोः फलेषु। हे फल हे फले हे फलानि॥
sequence.translation: The complete declension of फल "fruit" (a-stem neuter) — eight cases × three numbers.
sequence.teaches: the whole अकारान्त नपुंसक paradigm — फल follows देव everywhere but the प्रथमा and द्वितीया (फलम्/फले/फलानि), where the neuter rules take over

notes.text: neuter प्रथमा = द्वितीया throughout — the defining feature

notes.role: अतोऽम् — after a short अ, neuter सु/अम् both → अम् → फलम्

notes.en: neuter — nom. and acc. always identical

notes.role: स्वमोर्नपुंसकात् — neuter सु/अम् drop; the dual takes शी
अ + ई → ए → फले

words.gloss: प्रथमा/द्वितीया बहु — nom.=acc. pl. (शि → नुम् + इ)

notes.role: जश्शसोः शिः — neuter जस्/शस् → शि (इ) in the plural
नपुंसकस्य झलचः — नुम् (न्) inserted before the ending → फलानि

words.gloss: तृतीया एक — instr. sg. (= देव: फलेन)

notes.text: from the instrumental on, neuter declines EXACTLY like देव (masculine)

sequence.vyakhya: अकारान्तनपुंसकं देववत्, किन्तु प्रथमाद्वितीययोः नपुंसकविशेषः — फलम्/फले/फलानि। शेषं समानम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The neuter फल is the masculine देव (ex094) with ONE difference, repeated thrice: in the प्रथमा and द्वितीया — which are always identical in the neuter — the cells are फलम् (sg, अतोऽम्), फले (dual, शी), फलानि (pl, शि + नुम्). From the तृतीया down (फलेन, फलाय, फलस्य, फले…) it is letter-for-letter देव. So learn देव, change three cells, and you have every a-stem neuter — फल, वन, ज्ञान, पुष्प.

sequence.sentence: नदी नद्यौ नद्यः। नदीम् नद्यौ नदीः। नद्या नदीभ्याम् नदीभिः। नद्यै नदीभ्याम् नदीभ्यः। नद्याः नदीभ्याम् नदीभ्यः। नद्याः नद्योः नदीनाम्। नद्याम् नद्योः नदीषु। हे नदि हे नद्यौ हे नद्यः॥
sequence.translation: The complete declension of नदी "river" (ī-stem feminine, ङीप्) — eight cases × three numbers.
sequence.teaches: the whole ईकारान्त स्त्रीलिङ्ग paradigm — नदी, with its distinct नद्यै / नद्याः / नद्याम् and ई → य् before a vowel

words.gloss: प्रथमा एक — nom. sg. (long ई, सु elided)

notes.role: स्त्रियाम् — feminine; the ङीप् (ई) stem-forming affix → नदी

words.gloss: प्रथमा द्वि — nom. dual (ई → य् before औ)

notes.role: इको यणचि — ई before a vowel → य् (यण्) → नद्यौ

words.gloss: द्वितीया एक — acc. sg. (अम्, ई kept)

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया (the case sense); form नदी + अम् → नदीम्

words.gloss: चतुर्थी एक — dat. sg. (ङे → स्याट् → यै)

notes.role: ङेराम्नद्याम्नीभ्यः — ई/नदी-class stems take आम्/यै etc.; dat. → नद्यै
ङेराम्नद्याम्नीभ्यः — the नदी-class oblique sg → नद्याः
ङेराम्नद्याम्नीभ्यः — loc. sg. of the नदी-class → नद्याम्

words.gloss: सम्बोधन एक — voc. sg. (shortened ई → इ)

notes.role: vocative shortening; हे नदि (the इ-shortened call)

sequence.vyakhya: ईकारान्तं स्त्रीलिङ्गं (ङीप्) — अजादौ यण् (नद्यौ), अन्यत्र विशेषप्रत्ययाः नद्यै नद्याः नद्याम्। हे नदि इति ह्रस्वः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The ī-stem feminine नदी (ङीप्, 4.1.3) gathered whole. Two signatures: (1) before a vowel ending the long ई becomes य् by यण् — नद्यौ, नद्यः, नद्या; (2) the oblique singular takes the special नदी-class endings नद्यै (dat), नद्याः (abl/gen), नद्याम् (loc), all by ङेराम्नद्याम्नीभ्यः (7.3.116). The vocative shortens to हे नदि. So every ङीप् feminine — नदी, देवी, गौरी, कुमारी — declines thus. With ex094 (देव), ex172 (फल), and this, the three commonest stem-classes now each have a full reference paradigm.

sequence.translation: the king's man (विग्रह: राज्ञः पुरुषः)
sequence.teaches: तत्पुरुष — the second member is primary, and the first qualifies it

notes.text: विग्रह: राज्ञः पुरुषः — "the man of the king"

notes.role: प्राक् कडारात् समासः — from here the combinations are named समास

notes.en: determinative — the second member is the head

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — a compound whose second member carries the main sense is तत्पुरुष

sequence.vyakhya: उत्तरपदार्थप्रधानः तत्पुरुषः। राजपुरुषः — पुरुषः प्रधानम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: In a तत्पुरुष the second member is the head and the first qualifies it: राजपुरुषः is a kind of पुरुष (man) — the king's. Resolve it (विग्रह) as राज्ञः पुरुषः, "the man of the king." The compound is whatever its last member is.

sequence.translation: Rāma-and-Kṛṣṇa (विग्रह: रामः च कृष्णः च)
sequence.teaches: द्वन्द्व — members are coordinate ("and"); none subordinate

notes.text: विग्रह: रामः च कृष्णः च

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः — words standing in the sense of "च" (and) form a द्वन्द्व

notes.en: dual — two people, so the compound is dual

sequence.vyakhya: उभयपदार्थप्रधानः द्वन्द्वः। रामः च कृष्णः च = रामकृष्णौ।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A द्वन्द्व joins members that would each stand with "and" — none is subordinate, both are heads: रामः च कृष्णः च collapses to रामकृष्णौ, "Rāma and Kṛṣṇa." Two people, so the compound itself is dual.

sequence.translation: the yellow-clothed one [Viṣṇu] (विग्रह: पीतम् अम्बरम् यस्य सः)
sequence.teaches: बहुव्रीहि — neither member is the head; the compound points outside itself

words.gloss: the one whose garment is yellow

notes.text: विग्रह: पीतम् अम्बरम् यस्य सः

notes.en: possessive / exocentric — denotes someone characterised by the members

notes.role: शेषो बहुव्रीहिः — the remaining kind of compound is बहुव्रीहि
अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — several words denoting ANOTHER thing (the possessor) form a बहुव्रीहि

sequence.vyakhya: अन्यपदार्थप्रधानः बहुव्रीहिः। पीतम् अम्बरम् यस्य — सः विष्णुः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A बहुव्रीहि names neither member: पीताम्बरः is not "yellow" and not "garment" but the one who has a yellow garment — Viṣṇu. The sense lies OUTSIDE the compound (अन्यपदार्थ). Resolve with यस्य: "he whose (यस्य) garment is yellow."

sequence.translation: near Kṛṣṇa (विग्रह: कृष्णस्य समीपम्)
sequence.teaches: अव्ययीभाव — the first member, an indeclinable, is primary, and the whole behaves as one

notes.text: विग्रह: कृष्णस्य समीपम् — उप = "near"

notes.en: adverbial — the compound behaves as an indeclinable

notes.role: अव्ययीभावः — a compound headed by an indeclinable (here उप) is अव्ययीभाव

sequence.vyakhya: पूर्वपदार्थप्रधानः अव्ययीभावः। उप कृष्णस्य समीपम् — सर्वम् अव्ययम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: In an अव्ययीभाव the first member — an indeclinable like उप ("near") — is primary, and the whole compound becomes an indeclinable itself: उपकृष्णम्, "near Kṛṣṇa," fixed in form. Four types, four answers to one question: which member carries the sense?

sequence.translation: The boy gone-to-Kṛṣṇa (who has taken refuge with Kṛṣṇa).
sequence.teaches: द्वितीया-तत्पुरुष — the विग्रह uses the accusative (कृष्णं श्रितः); named by that case

words.gloss: gone to / having resorted to Kṛṣṇa

notes.text: विग्रह: कृष्णं श्रितः — "resorted-to Kṛष्ण"; the first member is logically accusative

notes.role: द्वितीया श्रितातीतपतित… — a 2nd-case word compounds with श्रित etc. → द्वितीया-तत्पुरुष

quiz.q: Which form is बाल · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

sequence.vyakhya: द्वितीयान्तं श्रितादिभिः समस्यते। कृष्णं श्रितः = कृष्णश्रितः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: तत्पुरुष compounds are NAMED by the case the analysis (विग्रह) would use. Here the विग्रह is कृष्णं श्रितः — "resorted-to Kṛṣṇa," with कृष्ण in the द्वितीया (accusative) — so the compound is a द्वितीया-तत्पुरुष (2.1.24). The later member श्रित heads it, as in every तत्पुरुष; only the internal case-relation differs. This is the template: each case gives a named sub-type.

sequence.translation: Bring the wood for the sacrificial post.
sequence.teaches: चतुर्थी-तत्पुरुष — the विग्रह uses a dative of purpose: यूपाय दारु, "wood for a post"

notes.text: विग्रह: यूपाय दारु — "wood for-a-post"; first member is logically dative (purpose)

notes.role: चतुर्थी तदर्थार्थ… — a 4th-case (purpose) word compounds → चतुर्थी-तत्पुरुष

notes.en: object of आनय (accusative neuter, unchanged in form)

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → आनय

sequence.vyakhya: चतुर्थ्यन्तं तदर्थेन समस्यते। यूपाय दारु = यूपदारु।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The dative-of-purpose तत्पुरुष: यूपाय दारु, "wood FOR a sacrificial post," compounds to यूपदारु (2.1.36). The विग्रह's चतुर्थी (purpose, "for") names it. Compare कृष्णश्रितः (द्वितीया, ex143): same heads-later frame, the internal case is what the name records.

sequence.translation: The king's man comes.
sequence.teaches: षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष — the commonest तत्पुरुष; the विग्रह uses the genitive (राज्ञः पुरुषः)

notes.text: विग्रह: राज्ञः पुरुषः — "the king's man"; first member is logically genitive

notes.role: षष्ठी → a 6th-case word compounds with what it relates to → षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: षष्ठ्यन्तं सुबन्तेन समस्यते। राज्ञः पुरुषः = राजपुरुषः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष is the workhorse compound: राज्ञः पुरुषः "the king's man" → राजपुरुषः (2.2.8). Whenever the relation between two nouns is the plain "of / 's" (the genitive, षष्ठी शेषे), it can compound this way — देवदत्तस्य गृहम् → देवदत्तगृहम्, and so on. It is the तत्पुरुष you meet most.

sequence.translation: A man skilled at dice.
sequence.teaches: सप्तमी-तत्पुरुष — the विग्रह uses the locative (अक्षेषु शौण्डः, "expert AT dice")

notes.text: विग्रह: अक्षेषु शौण्डः — "expert at dice"; first member is logically locative

notes.role: सप्तमी शौण्डैः — a 7th-case word compounds with शौण्ड etc. → सप्तमी-तत्पुरुष

quiz.q: Which form is नर · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

sequence.vyakhya: सप्तम्यन्तं शौण्डादिभिः समस्यते। अक्षेषु शौण्डः = अक्षशौण्डः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The locative तत्पुरुष: अक्षेषु शौण्डः, "expert AT dice," → अक्षशौण्डः (2.1.40). The विग्रह's सप्तमी (the locus of the skill) names it. With ex143–146 you now have the four case-तत्पुरुषes — द्वितीया, चतुर्थी, षष्ठी, सप्तमी — each the same heads-later compound, distinguished only by which case the analysis restores.

sequence.translation: This one is a non-brahmin.
sequence.teaches: नञ्-तत्पुरुष — negation by नञ् (न → अ before a consonant); "non-X"

notes.text: विग्रह: न ब्राह्मणः — "not a brahmin"; नञ् (न) prefixes, surfacing as अ before a consonant

notes.role: नञ् → the negative नञ् compounds with the following word → नञ्-तत्पुरुष

sequence.vyakhya: नञः समासे न-कारस्य अ-आदेशः (हलि)। न ब्राह्मणः = अब्राह्मणः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The नञ्-तत्पुरुष negates: न ब्राह्मणः "not a brahmin" → अब्राह्मणः (2.2.6). The particle नञ् surfaces as अ- before a consonant (and as अन्- before a vowel — अनश्वः "non-horse"). This is the productive "non-/un-/a-" prefix of Sanskrit: अधर्मः, अहिंसा, असत्य — every one a नञ्-तत्पुरुष.

sequence.translation: The eminent teacher instructs.
sequence.teaches: प्रादि-तत्पुरुष — a preverb/particle (here प्र "forth, eminent") compounds as the first member

notes.text: विग्रह: प्रगतः आचार्यः — "a foremost teacher"; प्र (preverb) is the first member

notes.role: कुगतिप्रादयः → कु, गति-words, and the प्र-class particles compound (तत्पुरुष)

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: प्रादयः सुबन्तेन समस्यन्ते (कुगतिप्रादयः)। प्रगतः आचार्यः = प्राचार्यः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The प्रादि-तत्पुरुष lets a preverb or particle head a compound: प्र "forth, eminent" + आचार्य → प्राचार्यः, "a foremost teacher" (2.2.18, कुगतिप्रादयः — कु "bad," the गति preverbs, and the प्र-series). The same rule gives अतिराजः "surpassing a king," कुपुरुषः "a wretched man." It rounds out the तत्पुरुष: not only case-relations but particles can occupy the first slot.

sequence.sentence: राजपुरुषः सभाम् आगच्छति। सः महापुरुषः, पीताम्बरः च। रामकृष्णौ तम् पश्यतः। अब्राह्मणः अपि तत्र तिष्ठति। उपकृष्णम् जनाः सीदन्ति। राज्ञः पुरुषः धर्मम् कथयति।
sequence.translation: The king's man comes to the assembly. He is a great man, and yellow-robed. Rāma and Kṛṣṇa see him. A non-brahmin stands there too. The people sit near Kṛṣṇa. The king's man speaks about dharma.
sequence.teaches:
the four compound types in prose: राजपुरुषः, पीताम्बरः, रामकृष्णौ,
उपकृष्णम्. The passage opens on राजपुरुषः and closes on राज्ञः पुरुषः —
compounded and not.

notes.en: the second member is what the compound names; राजन् qualifies it

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — the class where the last member is primary

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
a तत्पुरुष whose members share one case — महा describes पुरुष
names neither पीत nor अम्बर but the man wearing them

notes.role: शेषो बहुव्रीहिः — the compound points outside itself → पीताम्बरः

notes.en: both members stand equal — the dual ending counts them

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः — the coordinate compound → रामकृष्णौ

notes.en: dual verb — रामकृष्णौ is two people, so the verb follows
negation compounded in front — न becomes अ before a consonant
the thematic अ between root and ending
the preverb उप leads, and the whole behaves as an indeclinable

notes.role: अव्ययीभावः — the first member governs and the compound is invariable

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
the uncompounded विग्रह of राजपुरुषः — weak stem राज्ञ्

quiz.q: Which form is राजन् · षष्ठी · एकवचन?

notes.en: nominative — two words now, where the opening had one

quiz.q: Which form is धर्म · द्वितीया · एकवचन?

sequence.vyakhya: राजपुरुषः इति समासः, राज्ञः पुरुषः इति विग्रहः। एकः अर्थः, द्वे रूपे।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The passage opens with राजपुरुषः and closes with राज्ञः पुरुषः. Same man,
same sense — one written as a single word, the other with the genitive
showing. That second form is the विग्रह, the analysis a compound can always
be unpacked into, and knowing which विग्रह a compound answers to is what
tells you its type.

पीताम्बरः is the one that will not unpack that way. Neither पीत nor अम्बर
is what the word names; it names a man neither member mentions.

sequence.sentence: राजपुरुषः उपकृष्णम् आसीत्। तत्र रामकृष्णौ अपि आगच्छताम्। राजपुरुषः तौ अपश्यत् — रामः श्यामः, कृष्णः पीताम्बरः। सः पीताम्बरं ननाम, यतः पीताम्बरः एव विष्णुः।
sequence.translation: The king's man was near Kṛṣṇa. There Rāma-and-Kṛṣṇa also arrived. The king's man saw the two of them — Rāma dark, Kṛṣṇa yellow-clad. He bowed to the yellow-clad one, because the yellow-clad one is Viṣṇu himself.
sequence.teaches:
all four compound types back to back, doing no new work: राजपुरुषः
(तत्पुरुष), उपकृष्णम् (अव्ययीभाव), रामकृष्णौ (द्वन्द्व), पीताम्बरः
(बहुव्रीहि).

notes.en: determinative — the second member, पुरुष, is the head

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — a compound whose second member carries the main sense is तत्पुरुष

notes.en: adverbial — headed by the indeclinable उप, the whole compound is indeclinable

notes.role: अव्ययीभावः — a compound headed by an indeclinable is अव्ययीभाव

notes.en: copulative — both members are heads, joined as "and"

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः — words standing in the sense of "च" (and) form a द्वन्द्व

quiz.q: Which form is कृष्ण · प्रथमा · एकवचन?

words.gloss: the one whose garment is yellow

notes.en: possessive — neither member is the head; the compound points at Kṛṣṇa

notes.role: शेषो बहुव्रीहिः — the remaining kind of compound is बहुव्रीहि
